Salam kasih persaudaraan untuk semuanya. Tahun 2022 hampir berlalu. Banyak hal telah terjadi. Satu lagi tahun penuh badai dahsyat, banjir, kebakaran, gempa bumi, perang, dan desas-desus peperangan. Amerika telah melalui satu musim lagi pemilihan politik, menyebabkan kaum konservatif dan liberal menjadi semakin terpolarisasi menjadi pihak yang saling berlawanan.

Akhir-akhir ini, saya merenungkan status hidup saat ini sebagai seorang Kristen yang berkomitmen dan percaya Alkitab di dunia kita sekarang. Tentu, ada tempat-tempat tertentu di dunia kita di mana orang Kristen hidup dalam ancaman konstan dipenjara atau dibunuh hanya karena mereka berusaha hidup sesuai dengan Firman Allah. Namun, dunia tampaknya bergerak ke arah perspektif yang semakin negatif terhadap umat Allah. Dalam kecenderungan yang berkembang, ada peningkatan mengejutkan permusuhan terhadap orang percaya yang berkomitmen.

Apa yang sedang terjadi? Saya telah melakukan banyak percakapan dengan berbagai orang percaya dari seluruh negeri yang tampak semakin khawatir tentang kemenangan kejahatan atas kebaikan yang sedang berlangsung, tentang agenda liberal atas gaya hidup konservatif, dan daftar kekhawatiran terus berlanjut. Inflasi yang melonjak saat ini, potensi biaya pemanasan yang belum pernah terjadi sebelumnya bagi banyak orang, desas-desus kenaikan suku bunga, dan kelangkaan barang yang terus berlangsung cenderung membuat seseorang terkejut dan tersingkap dari rasa normalitas.

Bagi kita sebagai orang Kristen, marilah kita selalu tetap memusatkan perhatian pada Allah di sorga. Inilah Allah yang dinyatakan Paulus di Bukit Mars—Allah yang menjadikan dunia dan segala isinya, karena Dialah yang harus dipandang sebagai Tuhan sorga dan bumi, Ia tidak diam di tempat-tempat buatan tangan manusia; juga tidak ditujukan untuk disembah dengan tangan manusia, seolah-olah Ia memerlukan sesuatu, karena Dialah yang memberi kepada semua orang hidup dan nafas dan segala sesuatu; – Kisah Para Rasul 17:24-25.

Marilah kita berhenti memusatkan perhatian pada kenyataan bahwa kejahatan tampaknya menguasai dan meningkat di sekitar kita dan kemudian menyimpulkan bahwa entah bagaimana Iblis saat ini mempunyai keunggulan. Sebaliknya, marilah kita diingatkan tentang apa yang dikatakan Firman Allah. Tetapi orang jahat dan penipu akan makin bertambah jahat, menyesatkan dan disesatkan. Tetapi engkau harus tetap berpegang pada apa yang telah engkau pelajari dan yang telah kukatakan kepadamu, mengetahui dari siapa engkau telah belajar hal-hal itu; dan sedari kecil engkau telah mengenal Kitab-kitab Suci, yang dapat memberi hikmat kepadamu untuk keselamatan oleh iman yang ada dalam Kristus Yesus. Segala tulisan yang diilhamkan Allah memang berfaedah untuk mengajar, untuk menyatakan kesalahan, untuk memperbaiki kelakuan, untuk mendidik orang dalam kebenaran, supaya manusia Allah diperlengkapi untuk setiap perbuatan baik – 2 Timotius 3:13-17.

Marilah kita memusatkan mata kita pada Yesus …yang oleh iman-Nya memimpin dan menyempurnakan iman kita; yang demi sukacita yang tersedia bagi-Nya menanggung salib, dan menganggap kehormatan itu sebagai sesuatu yang hina, dan duduk di sebelah kanan takhta Allah – Ibrani 12:2. Daripada percaya pada kebohongan Iblis bahwa ia entah bagaimana sedang memenangkan pertempuran untuk Kebenaran saat ini, marilah kita ingat bahwa Alkitab mengungkapkan bahwa Iblis tidak dapat berbuat apa-apa tanpa Allah mengizinkan dia kebebasan sementara. Tampak bagi mereka yang menyaksikan bahwa Iblis mempunyai keunggulan penuh ketika Yesus disalibkan dan dikuburkan. Kejutan, kejutan! Iblis tanpa sengaja mengizinkan Allah menggunakan dia untuk memenuhi segala sesuatu yang telah dinubuatkan di seluruh Kitab Suci. Demikian juga hari ini… Allah sekali lagi akan mengizinkan Iblis segala kebebasan yang diperlukan untuk menyelesaikan segala yang telah dinyatakan Alkitab akan terjadi mengenai akhir zaman.

Dalam edisi majalah ini, kami sekali lagi berusaha menghadirkan informasi dalam artikel-artikel yang berguna dan relevan dengan masa kita dalam sejarah. Saudara Leonard Martin, seorang uskup di salah satu gereja kami, telah membagikan suatu nasihat mengenai karunia rohani di gereja dengan sejumlah pengamatan yang jelas dan praktis bagi kita saat ini. Artikel yang kami pilih untuk dibagikan dari “Bible Helps” dalam edisi ini adalah salah satu khotbah terbaik tentang pokok “iman dan perbuatan” yang pernah saya baca. Penulis bahkan membahas, dengan kesederhanaan dan kejelasan alkitabiah, tentang pokok kontroversial pilihan ilahi dan predestinasi. Akhirnya, kami menyajikan The Foolishness of Preaching sebuah penilaian mengenai dasar gereja-gereja yang menggunakan “panggilan di altar”—apakah itu berlandaskan pada Kitab Suci dan sejarah gereja ataukah itu metode yang dipinjam gereja dari dunia pada tahun-tahun belakangan ini?!

Semua ini pasti akan membangkitkan pemikiran dan diskusi—yang merupakan tujuan kami dengan jenis artikel seperti ini. Silakan merasa bebas untuk menanggapi melalui surel atau surat biasa dengan pemikiran Anda yang berhati-hati atau yang memberi dorongan. Ini bermanfaat bagi kami dan penulis-penulis kami. Ketika Anda menulis, kami juga mohon agar Anda menyebutkan ya atau tidak jika kami boleh menggunakan pertanyaan atau komentar Anda dalam majalah kami. Kami telah menerima berbagai permintaan untuk membentuk bagian di majalah kami yang dikhususkan untuk mendengar dari para pembaca.

Satu pemikiran terakhir… selama bertahun-tahun para pembaca kami terkadang telah berbagi kepada kami cara-cara yang mereka kira dapat memperbaiki majalah kami demi kebaikan semua yang membacanya dan untuk menyajikan pesan Injil yang lebih jelas. Kami menyambut agar hal ini terus berlanjut.

Semoga Allah melimpahkan berkat kepada kalian sekalian,

Curvin L. Wenger

I want to introduce this article on Spiritual Gifts by observing an interesting verse: Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men –Ephesians 4:8. Throughout history, when a king went to battle against a city and conquered it, he and his army returned home, to be greeted by their people with great fanfare. They would march through the city with all the spoils of war, after which the king would hand out gifts from the stuff that was taken in battle, giving it to his people.

Likewise, when Jesus was crucified, through His death and resurrection, He conquered the enemy. He took the power from death, hell, the grave and from Satan himself for those who repent and believe in Him. When He returned home (ascended up on high) He gave gifts to His people— the Church. Here in Ephesians, we have a condensed list of spiritual gifts: And he [God] gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers –Ephesians 4:11.

We observe more detailed descriptions of these gifts given to the Church in 1 Corinthians chapter 12 both at the beginning of the chapter and the end of the chapter and in Romans chapter 12 verses 6 to 8. In 1 Corinthians we see the following gifts given—the word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, tongues, discerning of tongues, helps, and governments. Then, in Romans, we have more gifts added to our list—ministry, exhortation, giving, ruling, and showing mercy.

If I did not miss any, there is a total of 19 gifts given to the church. What a wealth of gifts have been given to the church when Jesus ascended up on high! It would be good for us to do a thorough study on each one of these gifts so that we would be able to recognize them in our congregations. One thing that could be observed is that our Pentecostal friends have taken a select few of these gifts such as miracles, healing, and speaking in tongues, and have held them above the rest, making them a validation of whether a person is born again, baptized in the Holy Spirit, or if they are more spiritual than those lacking these gifts. Or we could consider how the evangelicals tend to do the same with the gift of evangelism, which has made inroads into many conservative Anabaptist churches. Finally, we might examine how some of us plain churches take only the gifts that have to do with Church government, leaving it only to those who are ordained to have gifts, while most all the rest of the gifts are left unrecognized.

This all leads me to ask the question, “Should we be lifting one or two gifts out above the rest and emphasizing them, or should all of the gifts be recognized equally?” The only time that I see one lifted above the rest is in Paul’s letter to the Corinthians in the last verse of Chapter 12, and the first verse in chapter 14, where he exhorts them to covet after the best gift which, with careful reading, we will notice is referring to prophesy. As we continue with our careful reading, we discover that prophecy should hold precedence over speaking in tongues since apparently the Corinthian understanding of speaking in tongues was being abused and misused and the Church might not have been edified by their behavior.

Spiritual Gifts Should Not Excuse Ungodly Behavior

A word of caution might be in order here. There is an emphasis by some, on “knowing what my spiritual gift is.” I think this can be good, but it should not be done to the fault of excusing myself for bad behavior because “I have this gift and not the other.” For example, the prophet might excuse himself for being harsh because his gift is that of a prophet; since he may not have the gift of mercy, people may be unnecessarily hurt. We will all probably have a primary gift or gifts. As much as we may try to be well-equipped with as many of the gifts as we can, some will still be more dominant than others.

I have asked numerous people which gift was primary in the life of our Lord Jesus and the short answer is that He was full of the Holy Ghost and without measure and had them all. True enough, but even so, since we all want to be like Jesus, maybe we should stop excusing ourselves to one limited gift and pursue to be as fully equipped as possible. I know, and you know, that in this flesh we will not master them all and yet we should be receptive to them all. Having said that, we must realize, we are meant to be interdependent; that is why Jesus handed out these gifts severally to each man and we will all have our primary gift or gifts. But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will –1 Corinthians 12:11. Nevertheless, let’s be careful that we do not excuse wrong behavior, or, on the other hand, negligence of doing good, because “Well, that is just not my gift”.

Spiritual Gifts Are Not The Christian’s Identity

A couple of cautions may also be in place when seeking to understand spiritual gifts. Our identity should not be the gift that we have but rather that our identity is in Christ. We are a child of the King; we are not primarily a prophet, a teacher, or an evangelist. However, in being a child of the King, we have been given a gift by Him, to do His work, with His power. Recognizing first and foremost who we are in Christ will keep us in a beautiful place of humility, but if our primary identity is “this gift that I have,” I suppose it would be hard not to fall into pride and thus we open ourselves up to many pitfalls and dangers.

Spiritual Gifts Are God-Given, Not To Be Sought After By Man

Could there be a caution given in how we seek this gift? What does it mean when the Scripture says that God gives gifts according to His choosing? For instance, God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? –Hebrews 2:4. Or, But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will –1 Corinthians 12:11.

Do you notice in both verses the WILL of God being very involved in the giving of gifts in the Church? Maybe our “seeking spiritual gifts” should be done alone in our closet, asking God to make me humble and endue me with whatever gift He wants me to have to make me a useful tool in the church body that I am a part of—“Not my will, but thine be done”. Maybe He has given me a gift that I am not recognizing or using, and what I actually need is to stir up that gift and not neglect it, but rather use it in the place I fill in the church. Could it be possible that, if I were to seek enough after another spiritual gift, I just might get myself a counterfeit?

Also, it would be good to mention very directly again that when there is a focused seeking after spiritual gifts usually there is some resulting negative problem. Sometimes a select few are lifted out and taught to be more spiritually important, such as speaking in tongues, miracles, and healing. Some will promote that there is little to no value in the teaching of spiritual gifts and that the only ones which are for our day are the ones pertaining to the ordained church leaders such as government, pastors, and teachers. While some people use their understanding of spiritual gifts to become individualistic and they see little value in being a part of a body. This is wrong, since a careful reading of these Scriptures show us that ALL the gifts are essential so that God will have the ability to make use of all the gifts by a collaboration of all the people. Could it be possible that where certain gifts are elevated above the rest, whether it is speaking in tongues, healings, and miracles; or if it is evangelism; or if it is those more suited for the ordained among us, that there could be an unrecognized element of pride in our midst? We are so prone to disillusionment that it would be good to check our hearts thoroughly when seeking after spiritual gifts.

Spiritual Gifts Are Not Included In The Biblical List of Qualifications For Church Leaders

Paul told Timothy, Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery –1 Timothy 4:14. Maybe rather than seeking out a gift, we need to stop neglecting the gift that has been given to us. Rather than seeking something new and exciting, we should stir up the gift we do have. It has happened that men in leadership have been removed from their post, because they do not have the gift for that which they were ordained. I would be very slow and very prayerful before removing an ordained brother from his office for that reason. Would it not be better to pray that God would increase that gift that had been given him by the laying on of hands? To quickly conclude that he does not have the gift may just be the easy way out.

We would never do that in a marriage. How often has it happened that a wife was more gifted in leadership than her husband? Disannulling the marriage is not an option, nor is it an option to add a third person to the marriage union to bring balance to the perceived lack of a proper balance of gifting. We have often seen that when prayer and the Holy Ghost was involved in a situation like this, God gave the husband what he lacked (1 Corinthians 12:24-25), and the wife learned to yield her gifting in a way that allowed her husband to be the godly head of the home.

God can also give the necessary gift to those in such a marriage and in such a ministry team if they find themselves lacking. For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked: That there should be no schism [division] in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another –1 Corinthians 12:24-25. Is there ever a time to remove one from an office because of the lack of gifting? Maybe so, but let’s be very cautious, slow, careful, and prayerful.

In the case of church difficulty that seems to be due to the lack of gifting among the ordained, we need to consider the following verses. Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom. But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth. This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace. –James 3:13-18. Very rare is the case of church trouble involving church leadership when there is not a major lack by one or more of the ordained to be fully living out of God’s will and wisdom as defined herein.

The biblical answer to solving church problems that involves church leaders is three-fold. (1a) The leaders in question must humble their hearts in repentance before God and His Word, before the rest of the ordained, and where necessary before the local church. (1b) If the situation has deteriorated too much, then the wisdom of outside overseers should be sought. (2) The leaders who may be lacking in a specific gift should seek God through fervent prayer, both personally and of the local church, and should seek God’s provision for enabling ability through …the laying on of the hands of the presbytery –1 Timothy 4:14. (3) Then AFTER stability is restored the local brotherhood is at a good place to seek God’s will together about ordaining another brother to assist.

God’s Goal for Spiritual Gifts

I would see two main reasons for the gifts of the Spirit to be given to the Church.

The first reason is for the benefit of the church. In Ephesians we read: and he gave… [various spiritual gifts to believers] [to some this gift and to others a different gift] … For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: –Ephesians 4:11-12. First Corinthians chapter 12 has a long dialogue on how the gifts are to be utilized so as to benefit the body of Christ (the local church) and in verse 25 in particular, that there should be no schisms in the body, but that the members should have the same care one for another.

There are those who are going about preaching the need to have spiritual gifts, encouraging specific gifts such as evangelism, healing, miracles, and tongues, and it can be seen in many cases that this focused teaching actually causes divisions rather than unity. The Bible says that the gifts were given to bring the Church together and if it is not doing that, we should consider whether it is the real thing or if it is a counterfeit. I realize divisions happen for many reasons, but if the gifts in the body are not bringing together but dividing, we had better seek God for answers on why, because the gifts were meant to bring unity, oneness, and edification.

The second reason is for the benefit of the unbeliever. Some of the gifts were given as a sign for the unbeliever. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe –1 Corinthians 14:22. We see that throughout the New Testament tongues, miracles and healings followed the gospel in places where it was being presented to those who had never heard it before. This was a way that God used to solidify and validate in the hearts and minds of the unbeliever that this gospel must be of God because of the supernatural manifestations. We see that tongues also followed the spreading of the gospel so that all could hear it in their own language as on the day of Pentecost.

I would consider these to be the two main reasons and are the primary purposes of the gifts. We would do well to evaluate our gifts in light of these two main reasons to be sure we have the real thing and are using them according to the purposes for which they were given.

It is interesting that of the 19 gifts we are considering, most of these will be best utilized in the local Church. Remember, God uses the church to reach the world. Some of the gifts given to the church are for reaching the world, for instance, the evangelist has a more unique calling to reach the world. Gifts like healings, miracles, and speaking in tongues are some of the gifts that are more prevalent on the frontier of the gospel. This is not to say that these gifts are never seen in the local church. My prayer is that if someone came into our services who cannot understand a word of English, and there is no one who can interpret the preaching of the Word into their language, then may God give us the gifts of tongues so that they might hear the gospel and be edified.

We have seen where there was sickness, and the elders of the church were called and there was anointing and prayer. At times God chose to miraculously heal. However, just because we (believers) have this wonderful gift of healing it does not necessarily mean that God wants all of us to be healed of every illness. The apostle Paul prayed three times to be healed from his recurring illness (2 Corinthians 12:7-12), yet God told him no. If he was not healed when he had healed many others, why would I think it needs to be different for me? So, it is with all the gifts that are given to the church; they are allowed by God to be exercised according to His will, not ours. It is absolutely essential for me and you to be a part of a local body so we will have the gifts of the Spirit working together through all the members, for the work of the church, in bringing unity, oneness, and edification, and for the ongoing work of the Church in calling men from a world of sin and calling them into His kingdom.

The Gift of Tongues

It is important to consider for a moment the spiritual gift of tongues and specifically the place it fills in the Kingdom of God. The Apostle Paul tells us they are given for a sign. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe –1 Corinthians 14:22.

It is not a sign to the believer that he really has the Holy Spirit, but it is a sign to the unbeliever that the gospel message is real. The classic example was on the day of Pentecost. We do not determine Peter’s credibility because he spoke in another language. We all would agree without any doubt, that Peter was born again, and that the many different languages were not for his approval but rather so that the ones hearing would know that this speaking in many different languages was supernatural. It would have taken a stubborn soul to scoff at the message being preached that day.

Recently, I was made aware of studies that have been done by recording the gibberish that comprises most of what is called tongues today. Interestingly, they found that English speakers used English syllables in repetition, and that Spanish speaking people used Spanish syllables, thus, they deducted that most of what is called tongues today is a counterfeit where the person, in their own language, repeats syllables of their native tongue in repetition. I believe that in many cases it is done innocently because of the vast amount of deception that follows the speaking in tongues.

What I understand as the real thing is the example of a lady in Canada, who only knew French and did not understand any English. This woman happened to come to a revival meeting where the revivalist was preaching in English with no French interpreter. She responded in repentance to the message and those who counseled with her asked her how she understood the message, which was in English. She responded that what she had heard was shared in the most beautiful French she had ever heard. Clearly a miracle took place so that she would hear the message of salvation and be able to respond to it. I am sure it was heartwarming to know how it was supernatural that she was able to hear it. I suspect there is a good possibility that at times, the one speaking in tongues may not even be aware of it. Surely, if God could confound the languages of those working on the tower of Babel, He can also cause the words of an English-speaking preacher to be converted into French words before entering the ears of a French-speaking hearer.

The reason we find in scripture for the gift of speaking in tongues, is twofold, and is for the unbeliever who comes among us. The first reason is so that he would hear the gospel message in his own language. The second reason is that when he hears it miraculously in his own language and the one speaking does not know his language, it is a sign for the unbeliever to cause him to acknowledge that the message he is hearing is of God, and by God.

In conclusion, we find that two of the main purposes of God giving gifts to the church, giving them severally as He wills, is for the unity and edification of the body of Christ, and for the unbeliever to hear and be persuaded of the gospel message. Let us seriously consider whether the spiritual gifts we have and those gifts that are evident in our churches are fulfilling the purpose for which they were given.

Saya ingin memperkenalkan artikel tentang Karunia Rohani ini dengan mengamati sebuah ayat yang menarik: Oleh sebab itu dikatakan: Ketika Ia naik ke tempat yang tinggi, Ia membawa tawanan-tawanan dan memberikan karunia-karunia kepada manusia –Efesus 4:8. Sepanjang sejarah, ketika seorang raja berperang melawan sebuah kota dan menaklukkannya, ia dan tentaranya pulang ke negeri, disambut oleh rakyatnya dengan gegap gempita. Mereka akan berarak melalui kota dengan semua rampasan perang, setelah itu sang raja akan membagikan hadiah dari barang-barang yang diambil dalam peperangan, memberikannya kepada rakyatnya.

Demikian pula, ketika Yesus disalibkan, melalui kematian dan kebangkitan-Nya, Dia mengalahkan musuh. Dia mengambil kuasa dari maut, dari neraka, dari kubur dan dari Setan sendiri bagi mereka yang bertobat dan percaya kepada-Nya. Ketika Dia pulang ke rumah (naik ke tempat yang tinggi) Dia memberi karunia kepada umat-Nya—Gereja. Di sini dalam Efesus, kita memiliki daftar ringkas karunia rohani: Dan Ia [Allah] memberikan sebagian menjadi rasul-rasul, sebagian nabi-nabi, sebagian pemberita-pemberita Injil, sebagian gembala-gembala dan pengajar-pengajar –Efesus 4:11.

Kita mengamati deskripsi yang lebih rinci tentang karunia-karunia ini yang diberikan kepada Gereja dalam 1 Korintus pasal 12 baik pada awal pasal maupun pada akhir pasal serta dalam Roma pasal 12 ayat 6 sampai 8. Dalam 1 Korintus kita melihat karunia-karunia berikut diberikan—firman hikmat, firman pengetahuan, iman, penyembuhan, mujizat, bahasa-bahasa, pembedaan roh, pelayanan, dan penguasaan. Lalu, dalam Roma, ada lebih banyak karunia yang ditambahkan ke daftar kita—pelayanan, penghiburan, kemurahan, memimpin, dan menunjukkan belas kasihan.

Jika saya tidak terlewat, ada total 19 karunia yang diberikan kepada gereja. Betapa kayanya karunia yang telah diberikan kepada gereja ketika Yesus naik ke tempat yang tinggi! Akan baik bagi kita untuk melakukan studi menyeluruh tentang masing-masing karunia ini agar kita dapat mengenalinya dalam jemaat kita. Satu hal yang dapat diamati adalah bahwa teman-teman Pantekosta kita telah mengambil beberapa karunia tertentu seperti mujizat, penyembuhan, dan berbicara dalam bahasa roh, dan menempatkannya di atas yang lain, menjadikannya suatu pembuktian apakah seseorang dilahirkan kembali, dibaptis dalam Roh Kudus, atau apakah mereka lebih rohani daripada mereka yang tidak memiliki karunia-karunia ini. Atau kita dapat mempertimbangkan bagaimana kaum evangelikal cenderung melakukan hal yang sama dengan karunia pewartaan Injil, yang telah masuk ke banyak gereja Anabaptis konservatif. Akhirnya, kita mungkin mengamati bagaimana sebagian dari kita gereja sederhana hanya mengambil karunia-karunia yang berhubungan dengan pemerintahan Gereja, menyerahkannya hanya kepada mereka yang ditahbiskan untuk memilikinya, sementara hampir semua karunia lainnya dibiarkan tidak diakui.

Kesemua ini membawa saya untuk menanyakan pertanyaan, “Haruskah kita mengangkat satu atau dua karunia di atas yang lain dan menekankannya, atau haruskah semua karunia diakui secara setara?” Satu-satunya kali yang saya lihat satu karunia diangkat di atas yang lain adalah dalam surat Paulus kepada orang Korintus pada ayat terakhir Bab 12, dan ayat pertama di bab 14, di mana ia mendorong mereka untuk menginginkan karunia yang paling utama yang, dengan pembacaan cermat, akan kita perhatikan merujuk pada nubuat. Ketika kita melanjutkan pembacaan cermat, kita menemukan bahwa nubuat seharusnya mendapat prioritas atas berbicara dalam bahasa roh karena tampaknya pemahaman orang Korintus tentang berbicara dalam bahasa roh sedang disalahgunakan dan Gereja mungkin tidak diteguhkan oleh perilaku mereka.

Karunia Rohani Tidak Boleh Membenarkan Perilaku Yang Tidak Takwa

Sebuah kata peringatan mungkin perlu disampaikan di sini. Ada penekanan oleh beberapa orang pada “mengetahui apa karunia rohani saya.” Saya pikir ini bisa baik, tetapi itu tidak boleh dilakukan sehingga menjadi alasan untuk memaafkan diri sendiri atas perilaku buruk karena “saya memiliki karunia ini dan bukan yang lain.” Misalnya, sang nabi mungkin memaafkan dirinya sendiri karena bersikap keras karena karunia yang dimilikinya adalah sebagai nabi; karena ia mungkin tidak memiliki karunia belas kasihan, orang lain bisa terluka secara tidak perlu. Kita semua mungkin memang memiliki karunia utama atau beberapa karunia utama. Sebanyak apapun kita berusaha untuk diperlengkapi dengan sebanyak mungkin karunia yang kita bisa, beberapa karunia tetap akan lebih dominan daripada yang lain.

Saya telah menanyakan kepada banyak orang karunia mana yang utama dalam kehidupan Tuhan kita Yesus dan jawaban singkatnya adalah bahwa Dia penuh dengan Roh Kudus dan berlebih-lebihan serta memiliki semuanya. Memang demikian, tetapi meskipun begitu, karena kita semua ingin menjadi seperti Yesus, mungkin kita harus berhenti memaafkan diri sendiri pada satu karunia terbatas dan mengejar supaya dilengkapi sedemikian rupa. Saya tahu, dan Anda tahu, bahwa dalam daging ini kita tidak akan menguasai semuanya dan namun kita harus terbuka terhadap semuanya. Dengan mengatakan itu, kita harus menyadari, kita dimaksudkan untuk saling bergantung; itulah sebabnya Yesus membagikan karunia-karunia ini masing-masing kepada tiap orang dan kita semua akan memiliki karunia utama atau karunia-karunia utama kita. Tetapi semua ini bekerja oleh satu dan Roh yang sama, membagi-bagi kepada tiap orang masing-masing seperti yang dikehendaki-Nya –1 Korintus 12:11. Namun demikian, mari berhati-hati agar kita tidak memaafkan perilaku yang salah, atau, di sisi lain, mengabaikan melakukan kebaikan, karena “yah, itu bukan karunia saya”.

Karunia Rohani Bukan Identitas Orang Kristen

Beberapa peringatan juga mungkin perlu ditempatkan ketika berusaha memahami karunia rohani. Identitas kita tidak seharusnya menjadi karunia yang kita miliki melainkan identitas kita adalah di dalam Kristus. Kita adalah anak Sang Raja; kita tidak terutama seorang nabi, pengajar, atau pemberita Injil. Namun, sebagai anak Sang Raja, kita telah diberi karunia oleh-Nya, untuk melakukan pekerjaan-Nya, dengan kuasa-Nya. Mengenali terlebih dahulu siapa kita di dalam Kristus akan menjaga kita dalam tempat yang indah dari kerendahan hati, tetapi jika identitas utama kita adalah “karunia ini yang kumiliki,” saya kira akan sulit untuk tidak jatuh ke dalam kecongkakan dan dengan demikian kita membuka diri kita kepada banyak jebakan dan bahaya.

Karunia Rohani Diberikan Oleh Tuhan, Bukan Dicari Oleh Manusia

Apakah ada peringatan tentang bagaimana kita mencari karunia ini? Apa artinya ketika Kitab Suci mengatakan bahwa Allah memberi karunia menurut kehendak-Nya? Misalnya, Allah juga menjadi saksi bersama mereka; Ia memberi tanda-tanda dan mujizat, dan karunia-karunia Roh Kudus menurut kehendak-Nya sendiri –Ibrani 2:4. Atau, Tetapi semuanya itu dikerjakan oleh satu dan Roh yang sama, yang membagi-bagi karunia itu kepada tiap-tiap orang secara khusus seperti yang dikehendaki-Nya –1 Korintus 12:11.

Apakah Anda memperhatikan dalam kedua ayat itu kehendak Allah sangat terlibat dalam pemberian karunia di dalam Gereja? Mungkin “mencari karunia Rohani” kita seharusnya dilakukan sendiri di dalam kamar doa, memohon kepada Tuhan untuk membuat saya rendah hati dan menganugerahi saya dengan karunia apa pun yang Ia kehendaki supaya saya menjadi alat yang berguna dalam tubuh jemaat yang saya bagian di dalamnya—“Bukan kehendakku, tetapi kehendak-Mulah yang terjadi”. Mungkin Dia telah memberi saya sebuah karunia yang tidak saya kenali atau gunakan, dan yang sebenarnya saya perlukan adalah mengobarkan karunia itu dan tidak mengabaikannya, melainkan menggunakannya di tempat yang saya isi dalam gereja. Mungkinkah jika saya terlalu giat mencari karunia rohani lain, saya justru mendapatkan tiruan?

Juga, sebaiknya disebutkan lagi secara langsung bahwa ketika ada pencarian terfokus terhadap karunia rohani biasanya ada masalah negatif yang timbul. Kadang-kadang beberapa karunia tertentu diangkat dan diajarkan sebagai lebih penting secara rohani, seperti berbicara dalam bahasa roh, mujizat, dan penyembuhan. Beberapa orang akan mempromosikan bahwa sedikit atau tidak ada nilai dalam pengajaran karunia rohani dan bahwa satu-satunya yang relevan pada zaman kita adalah yang berkaitan dengan pemimpin gereja yang ditahbiskan seperti pemerintahan, gembala, dan pengajar. Sementara beberapa orang menggunakan pemahaman karunia rohani mereka untuk menjadi individualistik dan mereka melihat sedikit nilai menjadi bagian dari suatu tubuh. Ini salah, karena pembacaan cermat terhadap Kitab Suci ini menunjukkan bahwa SEMUA karunia itu penting sehingga Allah dapat memakai semua karunia itu melalui kerja sama semua orang. Mungkinkah bahwa di mana karunia tertentu ditinggikan di atas yang lain, apakah itu berbicara dalam bahasa roh, penyembuhan, dan mujizat; atau jika itu pewartaan Injil; atau jika itu lebih cocok bagi mereka yang ditahbiskan di antara kita, bahwa mungkin ada elemen kesombongan yang tidak diakui di antara kita? Kita sangat rentan terhadap kekecewaan sehingga akan baik untuk memeriksa hati kita secara menyeluruh ketika mencari karunia rohani.

Karunia Rohani Tidak Termasuk Dalam Daftar Kualifikasi Alkitabiah Untuk Pemimpin Gereja

Paulus berkata kepada Timotius, Janganlah engkau lalai menggunakan karunia yang ada padamu, yang dianugerahkan kepadamu oleh nubuat dengan penumpangan tangan para penatua –1 Timotius 4:14. Mungkin daripada mencari suatu karunia, kita perlu berhenti mengabaikan karunia yang telah diberikan kepada kita. Daripada mencari sesuatu yang baru dan menarik, kita harus mengobarkan karunia yang kita miliki. Pernah terjadi bahwa orang-orang yang memegang jabatan ditangguhkan dari tugasnya, karena mereka tidak memiliki karunia untuk apa yang mereka ditahbiskan. Saya akan sangat lambat dan sangat berdoa sebelum mencopot seorang saudara yang ditahbiskan dari kantor karena alasan itu. Bukankah lebih baik berdoa supaya Allah menambahkan karunia yang telah diberikan kepadanya oleh penumpangan tangan? Menyimpulkan dengan cepat bahwa ia tidak memiliki karunia mungkin hanyalah jalan keluarnya yang mudah.

Kita tidak akan melakukan itu dalam perkawinan. Betapa seringnya terjadi bahwa istri lebih berbakat dalam kepemimpinan daripada suaminya? Menggugurkan perkawinan bukanlah pilihan, begitu pula menambahkan orang ketiga ke dalam ikatan perkawinan untuk menyeimbangkan yang dianggap kurangnya karunia yang tepat bukanlah pilihan. Kita sering melihat bahwa ketika doa dan Roh Kudus terlibat dalam situasi seperti ini, Allah memberikan kepada suami apa yang kurang padanya (1 Korintus 12:24-25), dan istri belajar untuk menundukkan karuniaannya dengan cara yang memungkinkan suaminya menjadi kepala rumah tangga yang saleh.

Tuhan juga dapat memberikan karunia yang diperlukan kepada mereka dalam perkawinan semacam itu dan dalam tim pelayanan semacam itu jika mereka merasa kekurangan. Sebab anggota-anggota yang tampak lemah tidak mempunyai kekurangan pada tubuh; tetapi Allah memberi lebih banyak kehormatan kepada anggota itu, supaya jangan terjadi perpecahan dalam tubuh, tetapi supaya anggota-anggota saling memperhatikan satu sama lain –1 Korintus 12:24-25. Adakah saatnya untuk mencopot seseorang dari jabatan karena kurangnya karunia? Mungkin ada, tetapi marilah kita sangat berhati-hati, lambat, teliti, dan penuh doa.

Dalam kasus kesulitan gereja yang tampaknya disebabkan oleh kurangnya karunia di antara yang ditahbiskan, kita perlu mempertimbangkan ayat-ayat berikut. Siapa di antara kamu yang bijak dan berpengetahuan? Hendaklah ia menunjukkan perbuatannya dengan perbuatan yang baik dalam kelemah-lembutan hikmat. Tetapi jika di hatimu ada iri hati yang pahit dan pertengkaran, janganlah kamu memegahkan diri, dan janganlah kamu mendustai kebenaran. Hikmat ini tidak turun dari atas, melainkan dari dunia, dari hawa nafsu, dan dari setan. Karena di mana ada iri hati dan pertengkaran, di sana ada kekacauan dan segala macam pekerjaan jahat. Tetapi hikmat yang dari atas adalah pertama-tama suci, lalu penuh damai sejahtera, lemah lembut, mudah diajak rujuk, penuh belas kasihan dan buah-buah yang baik, tanpa memihak dan tanpa munafik. Dan buah kebenaran ditaburkan di dalam damai oleh mereka yang membuat perdamaian. –Yakobus 3:13-18. Sangat jarang terjadi masalah gereja yang melibatkan kepemimpinan gereja ketika tidak ada kekurangan besar oleh satu atau lebih yang ditahbiskan untuk benar-benar hidup menurut kehendak dan hikmat Allah sebagaimana didefinisikan di sini.

Jawaban alkitabiah untuk menyelesaikan masalah gereja yang melibatkan pemimpin gereja ada tiga langkah. (1a) Para pemimpin yang bersangkutan harus merendahkan hati dalam pertobatan di hadapan Allah dan Firman-Nya, di hadapan para penatua lainnya, dan bila perlu di hadapan jemaat setempat. (1b) Jika situasi telah terlalu memburuk, maka kebijaksanaan pengawas dari luar harus dicari. (2) Para pemimpin yang mungkin kekurangan dalam karunia tertentu harus memohon kepada Allah melalui doa yang bersemangat, baik secara pribadi maupun oleh jemaat setempat, dan harus mencari penyediaan Allah untuk kemampuan melalui …penumpangan tangan para penatua –1 Timotius 4:14. (3) Kemudian SETELAH stabilitas dipulihkan, persekutuan setempat berada pada posisi yang baik untuk bersama-sama mencari kehendak Allah mengenai menahbiskan saudara lain untuk membantu.

Tujuan Tuhan atas Karunia Rohani

Saya melihat dua alasan utama mengapa karunia-karunia Roh diberikan kepada Gereja.

Alasan pertama adalah untuk keuntungan gereja. Dalam Efesus kita membaca: dan Ia memberikan… [berbagai karunia rohani kepada orang percaya] [kepada sebagian karunia ini dan kepada sebagian lain karunia yang berbeda] … Untuk melengkapi orang-orang kudus, untuk pekerjaan pelayanan, untuk membangun tubuh Kristus: –Efesus 4:11-12. 1 Korintus pasal 12 memiliki dialog panjang tentang bagaimana karunia-karunia itu harus dipergunakan sehingga menguntungkan tubuh Kristus (gereja setempat) dan khususnya pada ayat 25 bahwa tidak boleh ada perpecahan dalam tubuh, tetapi supaya anggota-anggota saling memperhatikan satu sama lain.

Ada mereka yang berkhotbah tentang kebutuhan memiliki karunia-rohani, mendorong karunia-karunia tertentu seperti pewartaan Injil, penyembuhan, mujizat, dan bahasa roh, dan dapat terlihat dalam banyak kasus bahwa pengajaran terfokus ini justru menyebabkan perpecahan daripada persatuan. Alkitab mengatakan bahwa karunia-karunia itu diberikan untuk menyatukan Gereja dan jika itu tidak terjadi, kita harus mempertimbangkan apakah itu asli atau palsu. Saya menyadari perpecahan terjadi karena banyak alasan, tetapi jika karunia-karunia di dalam tubuh tidak menyatukan tetapi membagi, kita sebaiknya mencari jawaban kepada Tuhan mengapa, karena karunia itu dimaksudkan untuk membawa persatuan, kesatuan, dan penguatan.

Alasan kedua adalah untuk keuntungan orang yang tidak percaya. Beberapa karunia diberikan sebagai tanda bagi orang yang tidak percaya. Jadi bahasa-bahasa itu adalah untuk suatu tanda, bukan bagi orang-orang yang percaya, melainkan bagi orang-orang yang tidak percaya; tetapi nubuat bukanlah untuk mereka yang tidak percaya, melainkan untuk mereka yang percaya –1 Korintus 14:22. Kita melihat bahwa di sepanjang Perjanjian Baru bahasa-bahasa, mujizat dan penyembuhan mengikuti pemberitaan Injil di tempat-tempat di mana Injil itu dibawakan kepada mereka yang belum pernah mendengarnya sebelumnya. Ini adalah cara yang digunakan Allah untuk memperkokoh dan meneguhkan di hati dan pikiran orang yang tidak percaya bahwa Injil ini pasti berasal dari Allah karena adanya manifestasi supranatural. Kita melihat bahwa bahasa-bahasa juga mengikuti penyebaran Injil sehingga semua dapat mendengarnya dalam bahasa mereka sendiri seperti pada hari Pentakosta.

Saya menganggap kedua hal ini sebagai dua alasan utama dan tujuan utama karunia-karunia. Kita hendaknya menilai karunia-karunia kita berdasarkan kedua alasan utama ini untuk memastikan bahwa kita memiliki yang asli dan menggunakannya sesuai tujuan pemberian.

Menarik bahwa dari 19 karunia yang kita pertimbangkan, kebanyakan dari ini akan paling baik dimanfaatkan dalam Gereja setempat. Ingat, Allah menggunakan gereja untuk menjangkau dunia. Beberapa karunia yang diberikan kepada gereja adalah untuk menjangkau dunia, misalnya, pemberita Injil memiliki panggilan yang lebih khas untuk menjangkau dunia. Karunia seperti penyembuhan, mujizat, dan berbicara dalam bahasa roh adalah beberapa karunia yang lebih lazim di garis depan penyebaran Injil. Ini bukan berarti karunia-karunia ini tidak pernah terlihat dalam gereja setempat. Doa saya adalah bahwa jika seseorang datang ke kebaktian kami yang tidak mengerti sepatah kata pun bahasa Inggris, dan tidak ada yang dapat menerjemahkan pemberitaan Firman ke dalam bahasa mereka, maka kiranya Allah memberi kami karunia bahasa roh sehingga mereka dapat mendengar Injil dan diteguhkan.

Kita pernah melihat saat ada penyakit, dan para penatua gereja dipanggil dan ada pengurapan dan doa. Kadang-kadang Allah memilih untuk menyembuhkan secara mujizat. Namun, hanya karena kita (orang percaya) memiliki karunia penyembuhan yang indah ini tidak serta-merta berarti Allah ingin kita semua disembuhkan dari setiap penyakit. Rasul Paulus berdoa tiga kali agar pulih dari penyakit yang berulang itu (2 Korintus 12:7-12), namun Allah berkata tidak. Jika ia tidak disembuhkan padahal ia telah menyembuhkan banyak orang lain, mengapa aku berpikir hal itu harus berbeda untukku? Demikian pula semua karunia yang diberikan kepada gereja; karunia-karunia itu diizinkan oleh Allah untuk dipergunakan menurut kehendak-Nya, bukan kehendak kita. Sangat penting bagi saya dan Anda menjadi bagian dari tubuh setempat supaya karunia-karunia Roh bekerja bersama melalui semua anggota, untuk pekerjaan gereja, membawa kesatuan, kesatuan pikiran, dan penguatan, serta untuk pekerjaan terus-menerus Gereja dalam memanggil manusia dari dunia dosa ke dalam kerajaan-Nya.

Karunia Bahasa Roh

Penting untuk mempertimbangkan sejenak karunia rohani berbicara dalam bahasa roh dan secara khusus tempat yang ditempatinya dalam Kerajaan Allah. Rasul Paulus mengatakan karunia itu diberikan sebagai tanda. Maka bahasa-bahasa itu adalah untuk suatu tanda, bukan bagi orang-orang yang percaya, melainkan bagi orang-orang yang tidak percaya; tetapi nubuat bukanlah untuk mereka yang tidak percaya, melainkan untuk mereka yang percaya –1 Korintus 14:22.

Itu bukan tanda bagi orang percaya bahwa ia sungguh memiliki Roh Kudus, melainkan tanda bagi orang yang tidak percaya bahwa pesan Injil itu nyata. Contoh klasik adalah pada hari Pentakosta. Kita tidak menilai kredibilitas Petrus karena ia berbicara dalam bahasa lain. Kita semua akan sepakat tanpa ragu, bahwa Petrus lahir baru, dan bahwa berbagai bahasa yang berbeda itu bukan untuk persetujuannya tetapi supaya mereka yang mendengar tahu bahwa berbicara dalam berbagai bahasa itu supranatural. Akan sulit bagi hati yang keras untuk mencemooh pesan yang disampaikan hari itu.

Belakangan ini, saya diberi tahu tentang studi yang telah dilakukan dengan merekam omong kosong yang menjadi bagian besar dari apa yang disebut bahasa roh hari ini. Menariknya, mereka menemukan bahwa penutur bahasa Inggris menggunakan suku kata bahasa Inggris secara berulang, dan penutur bahasa Spanyol menggunakan suku kata bahasa Spanyol, sehingga mereka menyimpulkan bahwa sebagian besar apa yang disebut bahasa roh hari ini adalah palsu di mana orang, dalam bahasanya sendiri, mengulang suku kata dari bahasa ibunya secara berulang. Saya percaya bahwa dalam banyak kasus ini dilakukan secara tidak sengaja karena banyaknya penipuan yang mengikuti praktik berbicara dalam bahasa roh.

Apa yang saya pahami sebagai hal yang asli adalah contoh seorang wanita di Kanada, yang hanya mengetahui bahasa Perancis dan tidak mengerti bahasa Inggris sama sekali. Wanita ini kebetulan datang ke suatu kebangunan rohani di mana pengkhotbah berkhotbah dalam bahasa Inggris tanpa penerjemah bahasa Perancis. Ia bertobat sebagai tanggapan atas pesan itu dan mereka yang menasihatinya bertanya bagaimana ia mengerti pesan yang berbahasa Inggris itu. Ia menjawab bahwa apa yang ia dengar disampaikan dalam bahasa Perancis yang paling indah yang pernah ia dengar. Jelas sebuah mujizat terjadi sehingga ia dapat mendengar pesan keselamatan dan menanggapinya. Saya yakin menghangatkan hati mengetahui betapa itu supranatural sehingga ia mampu mendengarnya. Saya curiga ada kemungkinan besar bahwa kadang-kadang orang yang berbicara dalam bahasa roh bahkan mungkin tidak menyadarinya. Pasti, jika Allah dapat membingungkan bahasa orang-orang yang membangun menara Babel, Ia juga dapat menyebabkan kata-kata seorang pengkhotbah berbahasa Inggris menjadi diubah menjadi kata-kata Perancis sebelum masuk ke telinga pendengar yang berbahasa Perancis.

Alasan yang kita temukan dalam Kitab Suci untuk karunia berbicara dalam bahasa roh adalah dua: untuk orang yang tidak percaya yang datang di antara kita. Alasan pertama adalah agar ia mendengar pesan Injil dalam bahasa ibunya. Alasan kedua adalah ketika ia mendengarnya secara ajaib dalam bahasa ibunya dan orang yang berbicara tidak mengetahui bahasanya, itu menjadi tanda bagi orang yang tidak percaya supaya ia mengakui bahwa pesan yang didengarnya berasal dari Allah, dan oleh Allah.

Kesimpulannya, kita menemukan bahwa dua tujuan utama Allah memberikan karunia kepada gereja, membagikannya masing-masing sesuai kehendak-Nya, adalah untuk kesatuan dan penguatan tubuh Kristus, dan agar orang yang tidak percaya mendengar dan diyakinkan akan pesan Injil. Marilah kita mempertimbangkan dengan sungguh apakah karunia-karunia rohani yang kita miliki dan karunia-karunia yang nampak di gereja kita memenuhi tujuan untuk yang karunia-karunia itu diberikan.

I grew up in the same church setting in which my parents were born and raised. However, by the time I was 10, my parents began to be concerned with the direction the young folks were going and wanted something different for their children. So, my parents got in touch with a church from another state, which helped them make connections with a small church that was located close to where we lived.

I was more of a quiet, strong-willed child and was quickly turning into a rebellious teenager. My parents did all they knew to do with me at the time. One of which was making the move to this new church since it had more of a godly youth environment. I had a hard time with this change. At our old church, I had friends that were on the same page as me and supported me in my rebellious ways, but at the new church I was more of the “bad guy” and didn’t fit in with the other young people.

Over the course of time that church dissolved, and my parents decided to move to another state, closer to a more stable church. So it was, that, when I was 14, we spent our first night in a different state, in a different house, on a different road, and with different neighbors. We went shopping in a different town and went to a different church, with people that I barely knew. I didn’t like change. I found it challenging to meet new people and make new friends. I struggled majorly with all these changes, so, I never bothered trying to plug in and be an active part in our new life. Instead, I slowly built walls around my life and heart, all the while growing colder and more rebellious.

As I grew older and harder, my parents tried to work with me, but I would have nothing to do with it. I eventually got a job and was introduced to country music and other worldly things. Since I enjoy work, I poured myself into it and worked long hours. That way I wouldn’t need to be around the family or church people, and I wouldn’t need to go to church activities. Thus, I became more removed and isolated from those around me.

The church people didn’t know how to relate to me; most of them just left me to myself. Deep down I was desperately longing for love and acceptance from my family and church. This caused me to spiral downward. I continued to stuff my feelings and build a wall around myself, all the while hardening my heart further. As time went on, I withdrew more and more from my family and the church. I felt more and more like a social misfit that no one knew what to do with. I decided I was going to run away and live my own life.

Somehow my parents got wind of this idea and tried to do all that they knew to do to help me, but I resented it. Looking back, I know without a doubt that they were doing it out of love and care, but there was a great lack in our relationship. Thus, I continued to grow harder and colder.

The summer I was 17, a visiting minister (‘Mike’) and his family came to our church for meetings. I knew them from years before and somehow through our interaction during the meetings my heart started to soften and open. I’m not quite sure why, but for some reason, I decided that I wanted to go spend the winter with them. So, my parents got in contact with them, and it was decided that I could stay with them for a few months.

My plan was to spend a few months away from everything and then I would return home when I was almost 18. Once I was 18, I was planning to leave home and do my own thing. I was certain no one could stop me because I would be of legal age. However, God obviously had different plans...

Somehow ‘Mike’ convinced me to go to along to a week of meetings in another state. While we were there, I don’t remember that the conviction was any stronger than any other time. However, one evening after the service he asked me if I wanted to become a Christian and have my sins forgiven. I don’t remember what I told him, but we talked for a while. He took me through the Bible, helping me to see what God says about it all; then we prayed. When we got up from praying, I can’t say that something major happened, but it was definitely the night that I found salvation! That night, something changed in my heart. I knew that I now wanted to do things God’s way. I knew that my end goal in life was to run the race well and to finish victoriously. That is what has helped me through the years.

On July 31, 2011, I was baptized upon the confession of my faith. The next number of years were definitely not easy. I would even say that at times it seemed to have been harder than in the years before my conversion. Out of respect to others, I don’t feel I can share everything that has happened over the years, but I will try to share several main points. You can imagine that with the walls I had built around myself and the comfort I had found in this, that the years following my conversion were full of ups and downs as I tried to relearn how to relate to other believers and to people in general.

Even though I had reached out to God for forgiveness of my sins and had committed my life to following Him, I had many old habits of relating to others in wrong ways that still needed to be sanctified. Things at home continued to improve but there was still room for progress, which added to the stress. As the years went by, my stress level continued to rise. I didn’t know what to do with it, so I resorted to taking high doses of NoDoz® with an energy drink before I went to bed, trying to get my nerves to relax enough so I could sleep (don’t try this at home, it is dangerous). The next day I would get up and face it all again. One year for most of the year I struggled with thoughts of not wanting to continue on with life. During this time, I had a very close friend who gave me much encouragement. I believe that the regular contact I had with this close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness all working together kept me from doing something that I would have later regretted.

I had another close friend who had also gone through a lot but seemed to be finding God’s answers to life’s struggles. We would go out for supper, spending time together talking about life’s struggles. I remember times that I would leave his car and tears would be streaming down his face because he wasn’t sure if I was going to make it. Then he went to the mission field for two years to teach English.

I’m not sure what all was going on in his life but one day we got word that he was missing. Eventually we heard from him; he was okay and was living back in the states again. My heart was torn… One of the few friends that I had, had now turned his back on what he had once believed and on that which he had once tried to convince me of. Yet here I was, still struggling… Why not just give up fighting…? Why not just go live the easy life…? As time went on, I continued to long for love and acceptance. At times the struggle, the aching, and the longing seemed almost unbearable. But I knew deep down that giving up was not what I wanted. It would not get the end result that I wanted. Once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on.

Another young man started taking an interest in my life and we eventually became close friends. He and his wife were a great encouragement to me. Then due to some disagreements with the church, they became dissatisfied and left the church. They threw aside a lot of what they had once stood for. So here I was once again with a close friend that had turned his back on what he had once stood for. What’s the use? Why does life need to be so hard? Maybe I should also give up… But I didn’t want to totally throw God out. Maybe I could find a church that was less strict. Once again, I came to my senses and realized that’s not really what I wanted. That direction wouldn’t take me where I wanted to go. So once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on. At the time it was tough, but looking back, I see I have learned a lot by all I have gone through.

In the fall of 2015, I went to Washington state due to a work opportunity. At the time I went, there were things going on at my home church that I was struggling with. Because of all the stress that I was facing, I was feeling quite discouraged about Church life, Christianity, and life in general. I wasn’t wanting to throw my Christianity away, but I was wondering, “Is this really what it’s all about?” “Why can’t people just get along?” Is this really what God had in mind for His people? If we are “little Christs” like we claim to be, shouldn’t we be able to get along? Shouldn’t we be the ones that are joyful and full of life?

I went to Washington with these kinds of thoughts on my mind. While there, I attended a church that was both Biblical and spiritually minded. It’s hard to explain all that went on in my mind, heart, and life during those six months. But I left there and went back home with a renewed strength and vision.

We should be the light of the world! We should have something to offer others! We should be able to get along with one another! Yes, we do go through hard times individually and collectively as a church, but if we fight the good fight of faith, if we finish our course, if we keep the faith, there is laid up for each of us a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only but unto all them also that love his appearing. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing –2 Timothy 4:7-8.

June 15, 2018, at 4:40 pm. the scream of the emergency services’ pager split the peaceful afternoon as it crackled to life. “One-car rollover on ‘Gingko Avenue’, possible entrapment,” was the repeated dispatch. As we walked onto the scene, there sat a young girl who appeared to be in her mid-twenties and was visibly banged up. With blood and tears streaming down her face, she repeated these phrases, “I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die… I may never see my baby again.” As seconds turned to minutes, the paramedics tried to calm her anxious nerves. We searched the mangled car and surrounding area for the supposed missing baby. All the while she sat there with lines of worry and fear. She had tears and blood streaming down her face, as she repeated, “I may never see my baby again… I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die.”

As first responders, all we found was a car seat that wasn’t fastened in, with no evidence of a baby anywhere. As the ambulance crew strapped her to the stretcher and loaded her in the ambulance, she was still repeating, “Where’s my baby…? I’m not ready to die… I don’t want to die… I may never see my baby again.”

As I left the scene that evening, with that image and those phrases running through my mind, I was struck with two sober thoughts. If that was me, miraculously surviving an accident and sitting there beside my vehicle, barely coherent, with blood streaming down my face, what would I be saying? What would the paramedics and rescue team remember me by? Would I be ready to die? Would I be clear before God?

As Christians, when is the last time we helped someone prepare their soul for death? As believers who have been redeemed from the misery and chaos of a life of sin (see 1 Corinthians 6:9-11), we should …be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh [us] you a reason of the hope that is in [us] you with meekness and fear: –1 Peter 3:15.

In the fall of 2018, God opened the door for me to move to a church in a different state where I have found stability. It was here that God brought a godly young lady into my life, and we were married on November 30, 2019. Being married and having brothers who surrounded me with discipleship, compassion, and prayerful support helped me to grow in the Lord in many ways.

Being here has awakened within me a renewed vision to be the light of the world. Today, I am thankful that God did not let me go. As I kept fighting the spiritual fight, God kept giving me the strength and wisdom to do the next right thing. With each victory, my strength has grown stronger. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you… –James 4:8. I thank God for giving me victory and for helping me find my ultimate source of love, security, and purpose—my Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

我在与我父母同一的教会环境中长大，我父母也是在那个地方出生并成长的。然而，到我十岁的时候，我父母开始对年轻一代的走向感到担忧，并希望为他们的孩子寻找不同的环境。因此，我父母与另一个州的一间教会取得了联系，这帮助他们与一间靠近我们居住地的小教会建立了联系。

我小时候比较安静，也很有主见，很快就变成一个叛逆的青少年。我父母用尽他们当时所知道的一切方法来对付我。其中一条就是搬到这间新的教会，因为那里有更敬虔的青年环境。对于这种改变，我很难接受。在我们旧的教会里，我有志趣相投、支持我叛逆行为的朋友，但在新教会里我反而成了“坏人”，无法融入其他年轻人之中。

随着时间的推移，那间教会解散了，我父母决定搬到另一个州，靠近一家更稳固的教会。于是，当我十四岁时，我们在另一个州、另一所房子、另一条路以及不同的邻居家度过了第一个夜晚。我们到另一个城镇购物，去了一间我几乎不认识人的教会。我不喜欢改变。我发现结识新朋友并建立新关系很有挑战性。我在这些变化中苦苦挣扎，所以我从未费心去投入并成为我们新生活中的积极一员。相反，我慢慢在我的生活和心里筑起了墙，与此同时变得越来越冷漠和更叛逆。

随着我变得年长且更铁石心肠，我父母尝试与我沟通，但我什么也不愿意接受。我最终找到了一份工作，并接触到乡村音乐和其他世俗事物。因为我喜欢工作，我把自己投入其中，长时间工作。这样我就不需要和家人或教会的人在一起，也不需要参加教会活动。因此，我与周围人的关系变得更加疏远和孤立。

教会里的人不知道如何与我相处；他们大多数人都让我独自一人。内心深处，我极度渴望来自家人和教会的爱与接纳。这使我开始走下坡路。我继续压抑自己的感受，在自己身上筑起一堵墙，同时更进一步地硬化我的心。随着时间推移，我越来越从家人和教会中撤退。我愈发觉得自己是个社会不合群的人，没人知道该怎样对付我。我决定要离家出走，过我自己的生活。

不知怎么的，我父母知道了这个想法并尽他们所知去帮助我，但我对此心存怨恨。回过头来看，我毫无疑问地知道他们是出于爱和关心这么做的，但我们之间确实存在很大的缺失。因此，我继续变得更硬、更冷漠。

在我十七岁那年夏天，一位来访的传道人（“迈克”）和他的家人来到我们的教会开会。我多年前就认识他们，不知为何，在会期间通过与他们的互动，我的心开始软化并打开。我说不上来为什么，但出于某种原因，我决定想去和他们一起过冬。于是，我父母与他们联系，决定让我能与他们住上几个月。

我的计划是离开几个月，然后在接近十八岁时回家。一旦我满十八，我就打算离家去做自己的事。我很确信没人能阻止我，因为那时我将达到法定年龄。然而，上帝显然有不同的计划……

不知怎么的，“迈克”说服我随他去另一个州参加为期一周的会。我们在那里的时候，我记不得那次的悔改感比其他时候更强。但有一晚上会后，他问我是否想成为基督徒并蒙赦免我的罪。我不记得我当时怎么回答，但我们谈了很久。他带我查考圣经，帮助我看见神对这一切的说法；然后我们祷告。当我们祷告结束站起来时，我不能说发生了什么重大的异象，但那绝对是我得救的夜晚！那天晚上，我的心发生了变化。我知道我现在想按着神的方式行事。我知道我人生的终极目标是要跑好这场赛跑并得以得胜。这就是多年来扶持我的力量。

在2011年7月31日，我在信仰的认罪上受洗。接下来的几年绝对不容易。我甚至会说有时似乎比我信主前的那些年还要艰难。出于对他人的尊重，我不觉得我可以分享这些年来发生的一切，但我会尽量分享几个要点。你可以想像，鉴于我在自己身上筑起的墙以及我在其中找到的安慰，信主之后的那些年充满了起伏，我努力重新学习如何与其他信徒以及一般人建立关系。

尽管我向神求得了罪的赦免，并且委身跟随他，我与人相处的许多旧习惯仍然需要被成圣。家中的情况持续改善，但仍有进步的空间，这也增加了压力。随着岁月流逝，我的压力水平不断上升。我不知道如何处理，于是我诉诸在睡前大量服用NoDoz®并喝能量饮料，企图让神经放松以便入睡（不要在家尝试，这很危险）。第二天我又起床继续面对一切。有一年大部分时间里，我都在与不想继续活下去的想法挣扎。在那段时间，我有一位非常要好的朋友，他给了我许多鼓励。我相信，常与这位密友保持联系、别人的祷告以及神的信实，共同作用，阻止我做出将来会后悔的事。

我还有另一位要好的朋友，他也经历了许多事，但似乎找到了神对人生挣扎的答案。我们常一起出去吃晚餐，一起谈论人生的挣扎。我记得有几次我从他的车上下车时，他的眼泪顺着脸颊流下，因为他不确定我是否能挺过去。后来他去了宣教地教英语，为期两年。

我不确定他生命中发生了什么，但有一天我们得到消息说他失踪了。最终我们从他那里听到了消息；他没事，已经回到本土生活。我的心碎成两半……我为数不多的朋友之一，现在背弃了他曾经信仰的东西，以及他曾经试图说服我的信念。然而我仍在挣扎……为什么不干脆放弃奋斗呢……？为什么不去过轻松的生活呢……？随着时间流逝，我仍渴望爱与接纳。有时那种挣扎、那种痛楚与渴望几乎令人难以承受。但我内心深处知道，我并不想放弃。放弃不会带来我想要的结果。再一次，靠着与我密友的鼓励与经常联系、别人的祷告以及神的信实，我继续坚持下去。

另有一位年轻人开始关心我的生命，我们最终成了亲密朋友。他和他的妻子对我很有激励作用。后来由于与教会的一些分歧，他们感到不满并离开了教会。他们抛弃了许多曾经所坚持的事。于是我又一次面对一位背弃曾经立场的亲密朋友。有什么用呢？为什么生活要这么艰难？也许我也该放弃……但我并不想完全把神赶走。也许我可以找一间不那么严格的教会。再一次，我醒悟到那并非我真正想要的方向。那条路不会把我带到我想去的地方。因此，靠着与我密友的鼓励与经常联系、别人的祷告以及神的信实，我继续坚持下去。那时很艰难，但回头看，我看见自己从所经历的一切中学到了许多。

2015年秋天，我因工作机会去了华盛顿州。那时我在家乡教会中正为一些事苦苦挣扎。因为面临的种种压力，我对教会生活、基督教以及生活整体感到颇为沮丧。我不想丢弃我的基督徒身份，但我在想：“这真的是生活的全部吗？”“为什么人们不能相处融洽？”这真的是神为祂子民所设想的吗？如果我们像所宣称的那样是“小基督”，难道我们不应该彼此和睦吗？难道我们不该成为充满喜乐与生命的人吗？

带着这样的思虑我去了华盛顿。在那里，我参加了一间既合乎圣经又属灵的教会。在那六个月中，我心里、心灵与生命里发生的种种很难用言语说明。但我从那里离开，回到家时带着更新的力量与异象。

我们该成为世上的光！我们该有东西可以给他人！我们该彼此和睦！是的，我们个人和作为教会都会经历艰难时刻，但若我们奋力为信仰争战，跑尽自己的路程，持守信心，必为我们众人存留那公义的冠冕，到了那日公义的审判者要把它赐给我；不但赐给我，也要赐给凡爱他显现的人。我已经打过美好的仗，我已经跑尽了路程，我已经守住了信心；从今以后有公义的冠冕为我存留，就是公义的审判者到了那日要把它赐给我；不但赐给我，也要赐给凡爱他显现的人。— 提摩太后书 4:7-8。

2018年6月15日下午4:40，紧急救援人员的呼叫器在寂静的下午划破长空，“单车翻覆，地点‘银杏大道’，可能有人受困，”调度一遍又一遍地通报。当我们走近现场时，坐着一位看似二十多岁的年轻女子，身上可见多处擦伤。血与泪顺着她的脸流下，她反复说着这些话：“我不想死……我还没准备好去死……我可能再也见不到我的宝宝了。”随着时间一秒秒过去，急救人员尽力安抚她紧张的神经。我们在扭曲的车内及周围地区寻找所谓失踪的婴儿。与此同时她坐在那里，面容上满是忧虑与恐惧的线条。泪与血顺着她的面颊流下，她重复道：“我可能再也见不到我的宝宝了……我不想死……我还没准备好去死。”

作为第一响应者，我们只在车内发现了一个没有拴好的儿童安全座椅，周围并没有任何婴儿的迹象。当救护队把她固定在担架上并抬上救护车时，她仍旧重复着：“我的宝宝在哪里……？我还没准备好去死……我不想死……我可能再也见不到我的宝宝了。”

那天晚上当我离开现场，脑海里不断浮现那画面与那些话语，我被两种清醒的思考所触动。如果那是我，奇迹般从事故中生还，坐在车旁，几乎神志不清，血顺着我的脸流，我会说什么？急救人员与救援队会记住我的什么？我是否已准备好面对死亡？我在神面前是否清清楚楚？

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

作为基督徒，我们上一次帮助某人预备灵魂面对死亡是什么时候？作为从罪的痛苦与混乱中得救的信徒（见 哥林多前书 6:9-11），我们应当……常常竭力以温柔敬畏的心回答那询问我们盼望缘由的人：— 彼得前书 3:15。

2018年秋天，上帝为我开了门，让我搬到另一个州的一间教会，在那里我找到了稳定。正是在那里，上帝把一位敬虔的年轻女子带进了我的生命，我们于2019年11月30日结婚。婚姻以及弟兄们围绕着我、对我施以门徒训练、怜悯与代祷的支持，帮助我在主里在许多方面成长。

在这里唤醒了我再次成为世上之光的异象。今天，我感谢神没有放弃我。当我持续为属灵争战时，神不断赐我力量与智慧去做下一件正确的事。每一次得胜，我的力量就越发坚固。靠近神，神就必靠近你……— 雅各书 4:8。我感谢神赐我得胜，并帮助我找到我最终的爱、安全与目标的源头——我的主和救主，耶稣基督。

Jehoshaphat was in trouble. He had just heard the news that a great multitude was coming to fight against him. At that moment he did what all of us naturally do when a multitude of problems come against us. He was afraid. How well I know the feeling of fear, the dread that grips my heart at times. Sometimes it’s the big things, like being misunderstood and misused, or the fear and pain of sickness, or the death of a loved one. Sometimes it’s small things, like loneliness on a Sunday afternoon. This is not comfortable, God, and I’m afraid.

Jehoshaphat laid his fear aside, set himself to seek the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout all the land of Judah – verse 3. Even in this seemingly impossible situation of having thousands of men on their way to destroy him and his people, he fell before the Lord and acknowledged His perfect, omnipotent rule. And [he] said, O LORD God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee? –verse 6.

The choice is mine. I wrestle with my own fearful thoughts, turning them over and over in my mind as if hoping to change the situation with my messy and fearful concoctions. Clinging to my fear gives me a feeling of being in control. But it is killing me from the inside out, even without the dreaded “what ifs” becoming reality. Finally, I let go and fall exhausted at my Lord’s feet, and my heart echoes the words of Jehoshaphat, the king of Judah.

In humble entreaty, Jehoshaphat acknowledges their weakness and need for God’s power. O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee. –verse 12.

Yes, God, I am nothing in the grand scheme of things. I have no power, not even to be the fruitful worker in Your kingdom that I always dreamed of being. I can’t fight this battle.

Jehoshaphat realized that he alone, as one man, had no strength. He called all the people of Judah together, And all Judah stood before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives, and their children –verse 13. They knew the strength in unity. As they stood before the Lord, waiting for Him to speak, the Spirit of the Lord came down and God gave them the words of help and hope that they were desperate for.

…Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s –verse 15. Often I try to fight my battles inside of myself rather than making myself vulnerable to others. But, as soon as I invite others into my life and into my battles, I find the strength of God through His people. When we are confused and disillusioned, we need the people of God. When we all pray together, we will get an answer to our prayer for direction.

Jehoshaphat heard the next directive from God. Tomorrow go ye down against them … Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the LORD … fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the LORD will be with you –verses 16-17. These words comfort my heart. Often the easiest thing to do is try to fix things, to quickly come up with a remedy of some sort to get myself out of this dilemma, to try to convince myself that everything will be okay. But God tells my heart to sit still without fear and let Him do the fighting. This takes more spiritual muscle than all the action, all the doing, and all the worrying; plus, it accomplishes a lot more.

And Jehoshaphat bowed his head with his face to the ground: and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell before the LORD, worshipping the LORD –verse 18. If I obey and trust instead of worry and sit still instead of jumping into the middle of things, then I will see God do miracles. No, not always in changing my circumstances or removing all the hard things, but He does a miracle in my own soul which changes my focus and attitude. And that causes me to worship because it’s a miracle which only the all-mighty, all-powerful God can do.

Do you think any of them slept that night? They knew a fearsome army was on its way to destroy them and yet… they had heard God speak. Just perhaps there was a joyful expectation in their hearts and an eager anticipation to see how God was going to win this battle. When I learn to practice trust in the little things and the big things that pile into my life, I will soon learn to have a heart of excited expectation, because I know He is going to do something! He is going to give me a way out. Even if the worst happens, He will show my heart the way of peace and He has promised to be with me through it all. And after all, the ultimate victory is already won, so what do all these infractions really have to do with my peace and joy? Nothing.

Morning dawned; it was the day God had told them to go out against these enemies. They arose with no delay. They all knew obedience was paramount in receiving God’s blessing that day. And as they went out of the city, Jehoshaphat exhorted them. And they rose early in the morning, …and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, …Believe in the LORD your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper. And… he appointed singers unto the LORD, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army… – verses 21-20. He appointed singers to sing as they went, proclaiming to everyone and to the opposing army that they were on the Lord’s side.

I would have liked to see that huge army going out of the city, singing. They were facing a daunting task and one that would have made the strongest man tremble, but they were singing. And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set… [an ambush] against the children of Ammon, [and] Moab, …which were come against Judah; and they were smitten …every one helped to destroy another –verses 22-23.

The people of Judah went to their watch tower and in amazement saw that their enemies had destroyed each other, and they saw nothing but an army of dead bodies. When a fearsome battle is set in array against me, I can still make the decision to trust and sing. Singing is a deliberate act of worship; it reminds our own souls and the souls of everyone listening that the Lord, He is God. He is the One in complete charge of my circumstances, of my tiny world, and all its problems. Suddenly the enemies are dead. The circumstances may not have changed, but the battle is finished in my soul.

The army of Judah spent the next three days gathering the riches and spoils from the dead bodies of their enemies, collecting so much that they couldn’t carry it all away with them. Astonishing! But that is how it is every time. My spirit benefits from the hard things that I endure successfully. Each victory allows me to collect ‘spoils’ which will profit me for the rest of my life. My heart is full of blessing, of being cared for, and being carried by a Heavenly Father. The “armies of Moab and Ammon” have brought blessing instead of ruin.

They came again to their homes in Jerusalem with singing, and harps, and trumpets, overloaded with all their spoil. The fear of God fell on all the kingdoms of the land when they heard how God had fought this huge battle, then Jehoshaphat’s realm was quiet. Peace reigned.

The peace of knowing that all I really need is God and His working in my life is the ultimate peace. This broken world can bring all manner of pain, sickness, and disappointments, but God brings rest to the heart that was once so full of tumult and fear. There is rest ‘round about’ and all the ‘kingdoms of the land’ will be amazed and curious at the strength that is within us, because it is the strength that no one can match—the strength of our amazing God.

Giosafat era nei guai. Aveva appena saputo che una grande moltitudine veniva per combattere contro di lui. In quel momento fece ciò che tutti noi facciamo naturalmente quando una moltitudine di problemi si presenta: ebbe paura. Quanto conosco bene la sensazione di paura, il terrore che a volte afferra il mio cuore. Talvolta sono le cose grandi, come essere fraintesi e sfruttati, o la paura e il dolore della malattia, o la morte di una persona cara. Talvolta sono piccole cose, come la solitudine in un pomeriggio di domenica. Questo non è confortevole, Dio, e ho paura.

Giosafat mise da parte la sua paura, si dispose a cercare il Signore e proclamò un digiuno in tutto il paese di Giuda – versetto 3. Anche in questa situazione apparentemente impossibile, con migliaia di uomini diretti a distruggerlo insieme al suo popolo, si prostrò davanti al Signore e riconobbe il Suo governo perfetto e onnipotente. E disse: O SIGNORE, Dio dei nostri padri, non sei tu Dio nei cieli? Non regni tu su tutti i regni delle nazioni? Nella tua mano non è forse potere e forza, e nessuno può resisterti? – versetto 6.

La scelta è mia. Lotto con i miei pensieri paurosi, rigirandoli nella mente come se sperassi di cambiare la situazione con le mie confuse e timorose elucubrazioni. Aggrapparmi alla paura mi dà una sensazione di controllo. Ma mi sta uccidendo dall’interno, anche senza che i temuti “e se” diventino realtà. Alla fine, lascio andare e cado esausto ai piedi del mio Signore, e il mio cuore fa eco alle parole di Giosafat, il re di Giuda.

Con umile supplica, Giosafat riconosce la loro debolezza e il bisogno del potere di Dio. O nostro Dio, non giudicherai tu loro? Noi non abbiamo forza contro questa grande moltitudine che viene contro di noi; né sappiamo che fare; ma i nostri occhi sono rivolti a te. – versetto 12.

Sì, Dio, io non sono niente nel grande disegno delle cose. Non ho potere, neppure per essere il lavoratore fecondo nel Tuo regno che ho sempre sognato di essere. Non posso combattere questa battaglia.

Giosafat si rese conto che lui da solo, come un uomo, non aveva forza. Radunò tutto il popolo di Giuda, E tutto Giuda stette davanti al SIGNORE, con i loro piccoli, le loro mogli e i loro figli – versetto 13. Conoscevano la forza dell’unità. Mentre stavano davanti al Signore in attesa che Lui parlasse, lo Spirito del Signore scese e Dio diede loro le parole di aiuto e speranza di cui erano disperatamente bisognosi.

…Non temete e non siate smarriti per questa grande moltitudine; la battaglia non è vostra, ma di Dio – versetto 15. Spesso cerco di combattere le mie battaglie dentro di me invece di rendermi vulnerabile agli altri. Ma, appena inserisco gli altri nella mia vita e nelle mie battaglie, trovo la forza di Dio attraverso il suo popolo. Quando siamo confusi e disillusi, abbiamo bisogno del popolo di Dio. Quando tutti preghiamo insieme, otterremo una risposta alla nostra preghiera per la direzione.

Giosafat ascoltò la direttiva successiva da Dio. Domani scenderete contro di loro … Non dovrete combattere in questa battaglia: disponetevi, state fermi e vedrete la salvezza del SIGNORE … non temete e non siate smarriti; domani uscite contro di loro: poiché il SIGNORE sarà con voi – versetti 16-17. Queste parole confortano il mio cuore. Spesso la cosa più semplice da fare è cercare di sistemare le cose, inventare in fretta un rimedio per tirarmi fuori da questo dilemma, convincermi che tutto andrà bene. Ma Dio dice al mio cuore di stare fermo senza timore e lasciarLo combattere. Questo richiede più forza spirituale di tutta l’azione, tutto il fare e tutto il preoccuparsi; inoltre, ottiene molto di più.

E Giosafat chinò la testa con il volto a terra: e tutto Giuda e gli abitanti di Gerusalemme si prostrarono davanti al SIGNORE, adorando il SIGNORE – versetto 18. Se obbedisco e confido invece di preoccuparmi e sto fermo invece di precipitare nel mezzo delle cose, allora vedrò Dio compiere miracoli. No, non sempre cambiando le mie circostanze o rimuovendo tutte le difficoltà, ma compie un miracolo nella mia stessa anima che cambia il mio focus e il mio atteggiamento. E questo mi porta ad adorare perché è un miracolo che solo l’onnipotente, il Dio tutto-potente può operare.

Pensate che qualcuno di loro abbia dormito quella notte? Sapevano che un esercito temibile stava per distruggerli eppure… avevano udito la voce di Dio. Forse c’era una gioiosa aspettativa nei loro cuori e un’ansiosa attesa di vedere come Dio avrebbe vinto quella battaglia. Quando imparo a praticare la fiducia nelle piccole cose e nelle grandi che si accumulano nella mia vita, imparerò presto ad avere un cuore di entusiastica aspettativa, perché so che Lui farà qualcosa! Mi darà una via d’uscita. Anche se dovesse accadere il peggio, mostrerà al mio cuore la via della pace e ha promesso di essere con me in tutto. E dopo tutto, la vittoria finale è già stata vinta, quindi cosa hanno a che fare tutte queste infrazioni con la mia pace e gioia? Nulla.

Sorsero il mattino; era il giorno in cui Dio aveva detto loro di uscire contro questi nemici. Si alzarono senza indugio. Tutti sapevano che l’obbedienza era fondamentale per ricevere la benedizione di Dio quel giorno. E mentre uscivano dalla città, Giosafat li esortò. E si levarono di buon mattino, …e mentre uscivano, Giosafat stette e disse, …Credete nel SIGNORE vostro Dio, e sarete saldi; credete ai suoi profeti, e prospererete. E… egli nominò cantori al SIGNORE, i quali dovessero lodare la bellezza della santità, mentre procedevano davanti all’esercito… – versetti 21-20. Egli nominò cantori a cantare mentre uscivano, proclamando a tutti e all’esercito avversario che erano dalla parte del Signore.

Mi sarebbe piaciuto vedere quel grande esercito uscire dalla città cantando. Affrontavano un compito impressionante che avrebbe fatto tremare l’uomo più forte, eppure cantavano. E quando cominciarono a cantare e lodare, il SIGNORE mise… [un’imboscata] contro i figli di Ammon, [e] Moab, …che erano venuti contro Giuda; e furono sconfitti …ognuno aiutava a distruggere un altro – versetti 22-23.

Il popolo di Giuda salì alla loro torre di vedetta e con stupore vide che i loro nemici si erano distrutti a vicenda, e non videro altro che un esercito di cadaveri. Quando una battaglia temibile è schierata contro di me, posso comunque decidere di fidarmi e cantare. Cantare è un atto deliberato di adorazione; ricorda alla nostra anima e alle anime di tutti coloro che ascoltano che il Signore, Lui è Dio. È Colui che ha il controllo completo delle mie circostanze, del mio piccolo mondo e di tutti i suoi problemi. Improvvisamente i nemici sono morti. Le circostanze potrebbero non essere cambiate, ma la battaglia è finita nella mia anima.

L’esercito di Giuda trascorse i tre giorni successivi a raccogliere ricchezze e bottino dai corpi dei loro nemici, raccogliendo così tanto che non poterono portar via tutto. Stupefacente! Ma è così ogni volta. Il mio spirito trae beneficio dalle cose difficili che sopporto con successo. Ogni vittoria mi permette di raccogliere “bottino” che mi servirà per il resto della vita. Il mio cuore è pieno di benedizione, di essere curato e portato da un Padre celeste. Gli “eserciti di Moab e Ammon” hanno portato benedizione invece che rovina.

Tornarono nelle loro case a Gerusalemme cantando, con arpe e trombe, sovraccarichi di tutto il loro bottino. Il timore di Dio cadde su tutti i regni del paese quando udirono come Dio aveva combattuto quella grande battaglia, quindi il regno di Giosafat fu tranquillo. Regnò la pace.

La pace del sapere che tutto ciò di cui ho veramente bisogno è Dio e la Sua opera nella mia vita è la pace suprema. Questo mondo spezzato può portare ogni genere di dolore, malattia e delusioni, ma Dio porta riposo al cuore che un tempo era così pieno di tumulto e paura. C’è riposo “intorno” e tutti i “regni della terra” saranno stupiti e curiosi della forza che è in noi, perché è la forza che nessuno può eguagliare—la forza del nostro stupendo Dio.
