Ο Ιωσαφάτ βρισκόταν σε δυσκολία. Μόλις άκουσε τα νέα ότι ένα μεγάλο πλήθος ερχόταν να πολεμήσει εναντίον του. Εκείνη τη στιγμή έκανε αυτό που όλοι μας φυσικά κάνουμε όταν ένα πλήθος προβλημάτων έρχεται εναντίον μας. Φοβήθηκε. Πόσο καλά γνωρίζω το αίσθημα του φόβου, τον τρόμο που σφίγγει την καρδιά μου κάποιες φορές. Μερικές φορές είναι τα μεγάλα πράγματα, όπως το να παρερμηνευτώ και να με καταχραστούν, ή ο φόβος και ο πόνος της αρρώστιας, ή ο θάνατος ενός αγαπημένου προσώπου. Μερικές φορές είναι μικρά πράγματα, όπως η μοναξιά ένα απόγευμα Κυριακής. Αυτό δεν είναι άνετο, Θεέ μου, και φοβάμαι.

Ο Ιωσαφάτ άφησε τον φόβο του, αποφάσισε να ζητήσει τον Κύριο και κήρυξε νηστεία σε όλη τη γη του Ιούδα – στίχος 3. Ακόμη και σε αυτήν την εμφανώς αδύνατη κατάσταση, με χιλιάδες άντρες να κατευθύνονται να τον καταστρέψουν αυτόν και τον λαό του, έπεσε μπροστά στον Κύριο και αναγνώρισε την τέλεια, παντοδύναμη κυριαρχία Του. Και είπε, Ω Κύριε, Θεέ των πατέρων ημών, δεν είσαι συ Θεός στον ουρανό; και δεν κυβερνάς σὺ όλα τα βασίλεια των εθνών; και δεν είναι στην χείρα σου δύναμις και ισχύς, ώστε να μην είναι κανείς δυνατός να σου αντισταθεί; – στίχος 6.

Η επιλογή είναι δική μου. Παλεύω με τις δικές μου φοβισμένες σκέψεις, γυρίζοντάς τες ξανά και ξανά στο μυαλό μου σαν να ελπίζω να αλλάξω την κατάσταση με τις ατακτοποίητες και φοβισμένες μου εφεύρεσεις. Το να σφίγγω τον φόβο μου μου δίνει ένα αίσθημα ελέγχου. Αλλά με σκοτώνει από μέσα, ακόμη και χωρίς τα φοβερά «τι θα γινόταν αν» να γίνουν πραγματικότητα. Τελικά, αφήνω και πέφτω εξαντλημένος στα πόδια του Κυρίου μου, και η καρδιά μου αντηχεί τα λόγια του Ιωσαφάτ, του βασιλιά του Ιούδα.

Με ταπεινή ικεσία, ο Ιωσαφάτ αναγνωρίζει την αδυναμία τους και την ανάγκη για τη δύναμη του Θεού. Ω Θεέ μας, θέλεις να μην κρίνεις αυτούς; διότι δεν έχουμε δύναμη εναντίον αυτού του μεγάλου όχλου που έρχεται κατά μας· ούτε ξέρουμε τι να κάνουμε· αλλά τα μάτια μας είναι σε σένα. – στίχος 12.

Ναι, Θεέ, δεν είμαι τίποτα στο μεγάλο σχέδιο των πραγμάτων. Δεν έχω δύναμη, ούτε καν να είμαι ο παραγωγικός εργάτης στη Βασιλεία Σου που πάντα ονειρευόμουν να είμαι. Δεν μπορώ να πολεμήσω αυτή τη μάχη.

Ο Ιωσαφάτ κατάλαβε ότι μόνος του, ως ένας άνθρωπος, δεν είχε δύναμη. Συγκέντρωσε όλον τον λαό του Ιούδα, Και όλος ο Ιούδας στάθηκε μπροστά στον Κύριο, με τα μικρά τους, τις γυναίκες τους και τα παιδιά τους – στίχος 13. Γνώριζαν τη δύναμη στην ενότητα. Καθώς στάθηκαν μπροστά στον Κύριο, περιμένοντας Αυτόν να μιλήσει, το Πνεύμα του Κυρίου κατέβηκε και ο Θεός τους έδωσε τα λόγια βοήθειας και ελπίδας που απεγνωσμένα χρειάζονταν.

…Μη φοβηθείτε και μη ταραχθείτε εξαιτίας αυτού του μεγάλου όχλου· διότι η μάχη δεν είναι δική σας, αλλά του Θεού – στίχος 15. Συχνά προσπαθώ να παλέψω τις μάχες μου μέσα μου αντί να κάνω τον εαυτό μου ευάλωτο σε άλλους. Αλλά μόλις προσκαλέσω άλλους στη ζωή μου και στις μάχες μου, βρίσκω τη δύναμη του Θεού μέσω του λαού Του. Όταν είμαστε μπερδεμένοι και απογοητευμένοι, χρειαζόμαστε τον λαό του Θεού. Όταν όλοι προσευχόμαστε μαζί, θα λάβουμε μια απάντηση στην προσευχή μας για κατεύθυνση.

Ο Ιωσαφάτ άκουσε την επόμενη οδηγία από τον Θεό. Αύριον καταβήτε εναντίον τους … Ουκ έξεσται υμίν να πολεμήσητε εν τη μάχη ταύτη· σταθήτε, και ίδετε την σωτηρίαν του Κυρίου … μη φοβηθείτε, μηδέ αποσταιθείτε· αύριον εκπορευθήσεσθε προς αυτούς· διότι ο Κύριος θέλει είναι μετά υμών – στίχοι 16-17. Αυτά τα λόγια παρηγορούν την καρδιά μου. Συχνά το πιο εύκολο είναι να προσπαθήσω να διορθώσω τα πράγματα, να βρω γρήγορα κάποια λύση για να βγω απ' αυτήν τη δυσκολία, να προσπαθήσω να πείσω τον εαυτό μου ότι όλα θα πάνε καλά. Αλλά ο Θεός λέει στην καρδιά μου να καθίσει ήσυχα χωρίς φόβο και να Τον αφήσει να κάνει τον αγώνα. Αυτό απαιτεί περισσότερους πνευματικούς μύες από όλη τη δράση, όλη τη δραστηριότητα και όλη τη ανησυχία· επίσης, επιτυγχάνει πολύ περισσότερα.

Και ο Ιωσαφάτ έγειρε το πρόσωπόν του στο έδαφος· και όλος ο Ιούδας και οι κάτοικοι των Ιερουσαλήμ έπεσαν μπροστά στον Κύριο, λατρεύοντες τον Κύριο – στίχος 18. Αν υπακούσω και εμπιστευθώ αντί να ανησυχώ και καθίσω ακίνητος αντί να ριχτώ στη μέση των πραγμάτων, τότε θα δω τον Θεό να κάνει θαύματα. Όχι, όχι πάντα αλλάζοντας τις περιστάσεις μου ή αφαιρώντας όλα τα δύσκολα, αλλά κάνει ένα θαύμα στην ψυχή μου που αλλάζει την εστίαση και τη στάση μου. Και αυτό με οδηγεί στη λατρεία επειδή είναι ένα θαύμα που μόνο ο παντοδύναμος, ο παντοκρατόρ μπορεί να κάνει.

Νομίζεις ότι κανείς απ' αυτούς κοιμήθηκε εκείνη τη νύχτα; Ήξεραν ότι ένας φοβερός στρατός ερχόταν να τους καταστρέψει και όμως… είχαν ακούσει τον Θεό να μιλά. Ίσως υπήρχε μια χαρούμενη προσδοκία στις καρδιές τους και μια ανυπόμονη αναμονή να δουν πώς ο Θεός θα κερδίσει αυτή τη μάχη. Όταν μάθω να εξασκώ την εμπιστοσύνη στα μικρά και στα μεγάλα πράγματα που σωρεύονται στη ζωή μου, σύντομα θα μάθω να έχω μια καρδιά γεμάτη ενθουσιώδη προσμονή, γιατί ξέρω ότι Αυτός θα κάνει κάτι! Θα μου δώσει διέξοδο. Ακόμη και αν συμβεί το χειρότερο, θα δείξει στην καρδιά μου τον δρόμο της ειρήνης και έχει υποσχεθεί να είναι μαζί μου σε όλα. Και, τελικά, η ύστατη νίκη έχει ήδη κερδηθεί, οπότε τι έχουν να κάνουν όλα αυτά τα επεισόδια με την ειρήνη και τη χαρά μου; Τίποτα.

Η αυγή ήρθε· ήταν η μέρα που ο Θεός τους είπε να βγουν εναντίον αυτών των εχθρών. Σηκώθηκαν χωρίς καθυστέρηση. Όλοι ήξεραν ότι η υπακοή ήταν πρωταρχική για να λάβουν την ευλογία του Θεού εκείνη την ημέρα. Και καθώς έβγαιναν από την πόλη, ο Ιωσαφάτ τους παρότρυνε. Και σηκώθηκαν νωρίς το πρωί, …και καθώς προχωρούσαν, ο Ιωσαφάτ στάθηκε και είπε, …Πιστεύετε στον Κύριον τον Θεόν σας, και θα σταθείτε· πιστεύετε στους προφήτες του, και θα ευοδωθήτε. Και… διόρισε ψαλμωδούς προς τον Κύριο, οι οποίοι θα υμνολογούσαν την ομορφιά της αγιότητας, καθώς προπορεύονταν του στρατού… – στίχοι 21-20. Διόρισε ψάλτες να ψάλλουν καθώς προχωρούσαν, διακηρύσσοντας σε όλους και στον αντιπάλων στρατό ότι ήταν με το μέρος του Κυρίου.

Θα ήθελα να δω εκείνον τον τεράστιο στρατό να βγαίνει από την πόλη, τραγουδώντας. Αντιμετώπιζαν ένα τρομακτικό έργο και ένα που θα έκανε τον πιο δυνατό άνδρα να τρέμει, αλλά τραγουδούσαν. Και όταν άρχισαν να ψάλλουν και να δοξολογούν, ο Κύριος έθεσε… [ενέδρα] κατά των παιδιών Αμμών και Μωάβ… που είχαν έρθει εναντίον του Ιούδα· και πατήθηκαν …ο ένας βοήθησε να καταστραφεί ο άλλος – στίχοι 22-23.

Ο λαός του Ιούδα ανέβηκε στον πύργο προσκοπής του και με θαυμασμό είδε ότι οι εχθροί του είχαν καταστρέψει ο ένας τον άλλο, και δεν είδαν τίποτε άλλο παρά έναν στρατό νεκρών σωμάτων. Όταν μια φοβερή μάχη στήνεται εναντίον μου, μπορώ ακόμα να πάρω την απόφαση να εμπιστευθώ και να τραγουδήσω. Το τραγούδι είναι μια σκόπιμη πράξη λατρείας· υπενθυμίζει στην ίδια μας την ψυχή και στις ψυχές όλων όσων ακούν ότι ο Κύριος, Αυτός είναι ο Θεός. Αυτός είναι ο Ελεγκτής των περιστάσεών μου, του μικρού μου κόσμου και όλων των προβλημάτων του. Ξαφνικά οι εχθροί είναι νεκροί. Οι περιστάσεις μπορεί να μην έχουν αλλάξει, αλλά η μάχη τελείωσε στην ψυχή μου.

Ο στρατός του Ιούδα πέρασε τις επόμενες τρεις μέρες συγκεντρώνοντας πλούτη και λάφυρα από τα νεκρά σώματα των εχθρών τους, μαζεύοντας τόσο πολύ που δεν μπορούσαν να το κουβαλήσουν όλο μαζί τους. Εκπληκτικό! Αλλά έτσι είναι κάθε φορά. Το πνεύμα μου ωφελείται από τα δύσκολα που αντέχω επιτυχώς. Κάθε νίκη μου επιτρέπει να συγκεντρώσω «λάφυρα» που θα με ωφελήσουν για την υπόλοιπη ζωή μου. Η καρδιά μου είναι γεμάτη ευλογία, με το να με φροντίζει και να με κουβαλά Πατέρας Ουράνιος. Οι “στρατοί των Μωάβ και Αμμών” έφεραν ευλογία αντί για καταστροφή.

Επέστρεψαν στα σπίτια τους στην Ιερουσαλήμ με τραγούδι, με άρπες και σάλπιγγες, φορτωμένοι με όλα τα λάφυρά τους. Ο φόβος του Θεού έπεσε σε όλα τα βασίλεια της γης όταν άκουσαν πώς ο Θεός είχε πολεμήσει αυτήν την τεράστια μάχη, και τότε η βασιλεία του Ιωσαφάτ ήταν ήσυχη. Επέβαλε ειρήνη.

Η ειρήνη του να ξέρεις ότι το μόνο που πραγματικά χρειάζομαι είναι ο Θεός και το έργο Του στη ζωή μου είναι η υπέρτατη ειρήνη. Αυτός ο σπασμένος κόσμος μπορεί να φέρει κάθε είδους πόνο, αρρώστια και απογοητεύσεις, αλλά ο Θεός φέρνει ανάπαυση στην καρδιά που κάποτε ήταν τόσο γεμάτη αναταραχή και φόβο. Υπάρχει ανάπαυση «περίξ» και όλα τα «βασίλεια της γης» θα είναι θαυμασμένα και περίεργα για τη δύναμη που είναι μέσα μας, επειδή είναι η δύναμη που κανείς δεν μπορεί να ανταγωνιστεί—η δύναμη του θαυμαστού Θεού μας.

The history of our world has been defined by its conflicts. From the earliest disputes of Cain and Abel to the military operations of the twenty-first century, humanity has never ceased to attack one another. Peacetime is simply a waiting period for the next battle; treaties and ceasefires are only delays in the violence.

The wars of the spiritual realm have been equally as long and as brutal as the physical wars. These battles have reached us from the earliest dawn of time, where they originated in the hearts of Adam and Eve. The struggle against temptation and rebellion is present in each of us, whether it is acknowledged or not. Few emerge victorious into a true peace, and even that peace is a watchful peace that can be shattered in a moment of wavering.

The following account is but a brief spark in this trying fire of strife.

The year was 1942, and all across the world there raged a war the likes of which had never been seen before. Destruction and carnage had become commonplace, none more so than in the Pacific theater. There, speckled amongst the vast blue expanse of the Pacific Ocean, its tropical islands hosted battles of unparalleled ferocity and savagery. Suicide charges, artillery annihilation, and arial bombardments made life for the common soldier a living nightmare. At any moment a banzai charge (a typically nocturnal all-out attack of massed infantry yelling at the top of their voices as they charged) might split the night air into a rush of charging enemies whipped into a killing frenzy. A wayward shell, some weighing as much as a small car, could fall from the sky with deadly results. Death was ever present, claiming lives seemingly at random.

Four thousand miles to the east, another battle was raging. This one was as deadly as the first, encompassing hundreds of young men in an all-out struggle for their spiritual survival. Instead of the physical fighting on the Oriental islands of the Far East, this battle would be fought in the hearts and minds of those involved in this battle. Instead of machine guns and grenades, they would be armed with the sharpest of two-edged swords (The Holy Scriptures), guided by a power (The Holy Spirit) greater than any naval fleet.

These young men were called to a term of service in the physical warfare that was raging. Two years earlier, the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 had been passed before the United States entered the war. This Act required all men between the ages of eighteen and forty-five to register for the draft. Those selected were expected to serve a one-year term. Once war was declared, this term would be extended until the end of the fighting.

To these young men, this draft and the current war prompted their memories of stories of a similar war and a similar draft, scarcely a generation prior, that had called away their fathers to the training camps of the United States military. There, the older generation had been subjected to all manner of malicious maltreatment. At that time, it was expected that all able-bodied young men would not only be willing, but also eager, to serve their country in battle against the enemy. This prevailing sentiment had brought about a general anger and animosity towards the conscientious objectors of the First World War. Pressure was applied to make them join in the drills and decorum of the armed forces, and penalties of various kinds could be and were enforced against those that refused. So severe were the punishments that many suffered physically, and several were killed by the treatment they received.

In like manner to their fathers, these young men were being called to serve their earthly country by bearing arms. Draftees were to report to their local recruiting office, where they would be organized and shipped to one of several training camps around the country. There they were to be molded into soldiers, prepared to kill their fellow man, and then sent overseas for that purpose. Yet their faith decreed otherwise.

Fortunately, they were not the only ones who remembered the First World War. In the two and a half decades since that war, both Mennonites and various concerned individuals had been at work, ensuring that if the need arose, there would be an option that could satisfy the government’s requirements of service while not going against the principles and convictions of conscientious objectors. Thus were born various organizations and programs that afforded an exemption to military duty. Conscientious objectors were placed in various service roles through these programs. They served in hospitals, built roads and irrigation canals, and provided labor for conservation efforts. In this way they could fulfill the law without breaking the Law (see Mark 12:17).

Despite the bureaucratic acceptance of the conscientious objectors’ (COs) convictions, and their subsequent alternate service, public feeling often still ran hot against, not only the nonresistant Mennonites and Amish, but against any conscientious objectors. Individuals who refused to fight could expect that not only would they personally be brought under pressure, but that their families and friends would also be scrutinized. Some of their families were shunned or looked down on, with the local community boycotting their businesses. In some cases, local law enforcement would turn a blind eye to the mistreatment of non-resistant people within their jurisdiction. In extreme instances, patriotic fervor would boil over, resulting in mob violence, property damage, and in a few rare instances, direct attacks against the perceived slackers.

Although most of Europe and its allies had been embroiled in this war since Hitler’s invasion of Poland in September of 1939, the United States did not join in the initial dispute. While the German army stormed through Europe, the early years of the war in the Pacific were dominated by Japan, who had already invaded China as early as 1937. The United States remained neutral during this time, motivated by a general feeling of isolationism. This would all change on the morning of December 7, 1941, as the Japanese Navy launched a surprise attack on the United States, attacking ships moored in Pearl Harbor, the home of the United States Pacific fleet. Retaliation was swift, and war was declared on Japan and its allies. Japan redoubled their offensive, sweeping over the island nations scattered across the Pacific. The Japanese commitment to the war was personal and intense. Honor, even in death, was esteemed higher than life. The emperor was worshiped as infallible, and Japanese soldiers hurled themselves into battle in his name, even in the face of overwhelming odds. Spurred by its fanaticism and an efficient, well-supplied attack force, Japan set its sights on the Philippines. There its army was met by a force vastly inferior to their own.

Meanwhile, at their various stations throughout the country, the COs were facing their own attack. They had been afforded the relief of not needing to fight a physical fight. With this exception came unforeseen opportunities for serving the suffering individuals under their care. Throughout their various ministries, they would encounter all manner of people. Each encounter was another opportunity to show a Christian’s peace and love in the midst of the on-going war, especially in the mental institutions and hospitals that employed some of the COs. The state of the mental hospitals at the time was deplorable. Patients were treated roughly, or simply neglected. Troublesome ones would be bound in strait jackets for weeks or forced to live in their own filth. Food and sanitation did not begin to meet the needs represented. Several of the young men brought attention to the situation of the mentally handicapped, through writing to newspapers or detailing their observations about the abuse to their contacts at home. These actions led to growing public awareness and concern about the treatment of the disabled, which would be the catalyst for change in the care of those unable to care for themselves.

Unfortunately, the opportunity to serve came at a cost. The COs were young and separated from their church and family. Ungodly influences abounded around them. Because they were separated from their churches and families, these influences weighed more heavily on the young men’s minds than they would have at home. The battle was still being waged, and now more than ever they had to lean on God as their strength, support, and defense.

In the Pacific, Japan moved in for an overpowering assault of the Philippines. The island nation had long been preparing its defenses, and now it would be tested by the impetus of the Japanese invaders. This defending army was a product of the training and leadership of General George A. MacArthur. MacArthur was somewhat of a prodigy of the United States military, emerging from his service in World War I as the youngest divisional commander in the Army. Since then, his time between the Wars had been spent largely in the Philippines, whose beaches and jungles he was now defending. In the months leading up to the invasion, he requested reinforcements, updated equipment, and sufficient materials to withstand an attack. Because the focus of the United States at the time was squarely focused on winning the war in Europe first, his requests were denied, and he was therefore out-manned and out-gunned. Nonetheless, MacArthur dug in and prepared to defend against the inevitable landings and subsequent inward crawl of the invaders. His troops suffered massive casualties in their slow retreat. Although defeat soon became apparent, the General refused to leave the island. Not until the time when the island was all but taken, was he finally persuaded to slip through enemy lines, evacuating to Batchelor Field, Australia. Here it was that he made a solemn promise to those he had left behind: “I shall return.”

The COs, now spread across numerous projects and fields of service, faced an equally diverse set of challenges. Instead of the steady guidance of their home congregations, they were now under the leadership of government appointed directors. Their camp schedules kept them at work, up to six days a week. Sundays were generally reserved for worship services. The influence of a world at war all around them had set in. Harry Litwiller, a Mennonite youth in Canada, was one of those who fell to the influences of the world. He was put into the army, where he quickly filed for CO status. While his request was being processed, he picked up gambling and drinking from other recruits. Word of his new habits soon made their way to his military superiors, and his request was denied. Churches prayed, wrote letters, and otherwise made efforts to support the young men in their trials. They could not know it, but their time of testing would soon be drawing to a close.

Finally, the year was 1945. The last months of the war had seen the conscription of young boys and old men into the German Army as Hitler made a last desperate stand, caught between the allied armies of the Eastern and Western fronts. Unable to continue, the Germans sued for peace. Now that the war was over in Europe, the tide of war shifted to the Pacific. America rallied, propelled by its greater industrial capacity and natural resources, causing the Japanese advance to grind to a halt—thus, the American counter-offensive began. Slowly, island-hopping across the ocean, General MacArthur drew ever closer to Japan.

MacArthur had not forgotten his promise to the Filipino people. In his four years of absence, battles had been fought over the smallest of atolls—coral islands just large enough for an airstrip and a garrison. Even as the Japanese were uprooted from these strongholds, they maintained a solid footing in the Philippines. The island nation had suffered through the years of the enemy occupation. It was home to prison camps— housing prisoners of war and those accused of aiding the allies.

Time was now running out for the Japanese. Spread thin—with troops, equipment, and resources dwindling—they fought a desperate defensive campaign. On October 24, 1944, an Allied force landed on the eastern coast of the island of Leyte. The battle for the Philippines would last for two months, but at its end MacArthur emerged victorious. Many months earlier he had overseen the island’s surrender, now he commanded its repossession. His promise was fulfilled.

The war dragged on. In Europe, it was over, but the Pacific was yet to be won. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who had led the nation through the war, sickened and died. His vice president, Harry S. Truman, was sworn into office. His first decision was one unlike anything he could have ever imagined. Should he expend hundreds of thousands of lives to take Japan by land, or make them a gruesome example of a newly developed atomic bomb being dropped from the relative safety of the air? Truman deliberated and made his choice.

The war ended in the blink of an eye. The devastation of a pair of atomic bombs shocked Japan into surrender. They sued for peace, and peace was given. Except for the formalities, the war was over. Over, but the temporary peace was bought with an astronomical price of human life. Millions would never return to their grieving families.

For the COs, it was a return to a new normal. They were returning to their families, their churches, and their homes. But the war had changed them. Months and years had been spent away from spiritual oversight. Many would settle into their communities, raising their families and living out their Christian faith. Yet there had been casualties, with some, like Harry Litwiller, having given up their faith. The battle had been fierce, and not all its contestants had been wearing the full biblical armor available to them.

Both MacArthur and the victorious COs persevered to the end. Each believed in their cause, MacArthur in the devastation and destruction of war, and the COs in the redemption and peace of a fully surrendered life. They parallel each other here only in the fact that they both fought. The crucial difference is in what they fought for, and how they fought for it.

우리 세계의 역사는 갈등에 의해 규정되어 왔다. 가인과 아벨의 초기 다툼에서부터 21세기의 군사 작전에 이르기까지, 인류는 서로를 공격하는 일을 멈춘 적이 없다. 평화 시기는 단지 다음 전투를 기다리는 기간일 뿐이며, 조약과 정전은 폭력을 지연시키는 장치에 불과하다.

영적 영역의 전쟁도 육체적 전쟁만큼 오래되고 잔혹했다. 이러한 전투는 인간 최초의 때, 아담과 하와의 마음에서 비롯되어 우리에게 이르렀다. 유혹과 반역에 대한 싸움은 인정하든 하지 않든 우리 각자에게 존재한다. 참된 평화로 승리하여 나아가는 사람은 드물고, 그 평화라도 흔들림의 순간에 산산이 부서질 수 있는 경계하는 평화이다.

다음 이야기는 이 시련의 불길 속에서 번지는 짧은 불꽃에 불과하다.

그 해는 1942년이었다. 전 세계 곳곳에서 이전에 볼 수 없었던 전쟁이 맹렬히 일어나고 있었다. 파괴와 학살이 일상이 되었고, 태평양 전구에서는 그 정도가 더욱 심했다. 광활한 태평양의 푸른 바다 위에 점점이 박힌 열대 섬들에서는 전례 없는 격렬하고 야만적인 전투가 벌어졌다. 자살 돌격, 포병의 파괴, 공습은 평범한 병사들의 삶을 악몽으로 만들었다. 언제든 밤공기를 가르며 함성을 지르며 돌격하는 적들이 분노에 사로잡힌 살육의 소용돌이를 일으킬 수 있었다. 때로는 작은 자동차만큼 무거운 포탄 하나가 하늘에서 떨어져 치명적인 결과를 낳았다. 죽음은 늘 존재하여 아무렇게나 생명을 빼앗는 것처럼 보였다.

동쪽으로 사천 마일 떨어진 곳에서도 또 다른 전투가 벌어지고 있었다. 이 전투는 첫 번째 전투만큼 치명적이었고, 수백 명의 젊은이들이 영적 생존을 위한 총력전 속에 있었다. 극동의 섬들에서 벌어지는 육체적 전투 대신, 이 싸움은 관련된 이들의 마음과 정신 속에서 치러질 것이었다. 기관총과 수류탄 대신 그들은 가장 날카로운 양날의 검(성경)을 들고 싸우며, 어떤 함대보다 더 큰 능력(성령)의 인도하심을 따랐다.

이 젊은이들은 물리적 전쟁터에서의 복무에 소집되었다. 그로부터 이년 전, 1940년의 선택적 훈련·복무법(Selective Training and Service Act)이 통과되어 미국이 전쟁에 참전하기 전에 이미 시행되었다. 이 법은 18세에서 45세 사이의 모든 남성이 징집 등록을 하도록 요구했다. 선발된 자들은 1년의 복무를 할 것으로 예상되었다. 전쟁이 선포되면 그 복무 기간은 전투가 끝날 때까지 연장되었다.

이들 젊은이들에게 이 징병과 현재의 전쟁은 거의 한 세대 전, 자신들의 아버지들을 미군 훈련소로 불러들였던 비슷한 전쟁과 징집의 이야기를 떠올리게 했다. 당시의 기성세대는 온갖 악의적인 박해를 겪었다. 그때는 모든 건장한 젊은이가 나라를 위해 기꺼이, 심지어 열렬히 싸우기를 기대했었다. 이러한 분위기는 제1차 세계대전 당시 양심적 반전주의자들에 대한 일반적인 분노와 적대감을 낳았다. 그들에게 군대의 훈련과 예절에 참여하도록 압력이 가해졌고, 거부한 자들에겐 여러 형태의 처벌이 가해졌다. 처벌은 심각하여 많은 이들이 신체적 고통을 겪었고, 일부는 받은 처우로 인해 목숨을 잃기도 했다.

이들 아버지들과 마찬가지로, 이 젊은이들도 무기를 들고 조국을 위해 복무하도록 요청받았다. 징집자들은 지역 징집 사무소에 보고하여 전국의 여러 훈련소 중 한 곳으로 조직되어 발송되었다. 그곳에서 그들은 병사로 단련되어 동포를 죽이도록 준비된 뒤, 그 목적을 위해 해외로 보내졌다. 그러나 그들의 신앙은 달랐다.

다행히도 그들이 제1차 세계대전을 기억하는 유일한 이들은 아니었다. 그 전쟁 이후 25년 반 동안, 메노나이트와 여러 관련 단체들이 활동하여 필요할 경우 정부의 복무 요구를 충족시키면서도 양심적 병역거부자의 원칙과 양심을 침해하지 않는 선택지가 제공되도록 준비해 두었다. 그리하여 여러 단체와 프로그램이 생겨 군 복무 면제를 제공하게 되었다. 양심적 병역거부자들은 이러한 프로그램을 통해 다양한 봉사 역할에 배치되었다. 병원에서 근무하고, 도로와 관개 운하를 건설하며, 보전 사업을 위한 노동을 제공했다. 이렇게 그들은 율법을 어기지 않고 법을 이행할 수 있었다(마가복음 12:17 참조).

관료적 차원에서 양심적 병역거부자(CO)들의 신념과 대체 복무가 받아들여졌음에도 불구하고, 여론은 메노나이트와 아미시의 비저항 원리뿐 아니라 모든 양심적 병역거부자들에게 종종 적대적이었다. 싸우기를 거부한 이들은 자신뿐 아니라 가족과 친구들도 압력을 받는 것을 예상할 수 있었다. 일부 가족은 배척당하거나 경시되었고, 지역 사회는 그들의 사업을 보이콧하기도 했다. 어떤 경우에는 지방 법 집행 기관이 관할 구역 내 비저항자들에 대한 학대를 묵인하기도 했다. 극단적인 경우에는 애국적 열기가 폭발하여 폭도에 의한 폭력, 재산 파손, 그리고 드문 경우에는 게으르다고 여겨진 자들에 대한 직접적인 공격이 일어나기도 했다.

비록 대부분의 유럽과 그 연합국은 1939년 9월 히틀러의 폴란드 침공 이래 전쟁에 휘말려 있었지만, 미국은 초기 분쟁에 즉각 참여하지 않았다. 독일군이 유럽을 휩쓸며 진군하는 동안, 태평양 전선 초반에는 이미 1937년 중국을 침공했던 일본이 주도권을 쥐고 있었다. 미국은 당시 전반적인 고립주의 정서에 의해 중립을 유지했다. 이 상황은 1941년 12월 7일 아침 일본 해군이 기습적으로 미국의 태평양 함대가 정박해 있던 진주만(Pearl Harbor)을 공격하면서 바뀌었다. 보복은 신속했고, 일본과 그 동맹국에 대한 선전포고가 이루어졌다. 일본은 공세를 강화하여 태평양에 흩어진 섬나라들을 휩쓸었다. 일본의 전쟁에 대한 헌신은 개인적이고 강렬했다. 명예는 죽음 속에서도 생존보다 더 높이 여겨졌고, 천황은 오류가 없는 존재로 숭배되었으며, 일본 병사들은 압도적인 역경 앞에서도 그의 이름으로 전투에 몸을 던졌다. 광신적 열정과 효율적이며 보급이 잘된 공격력에 힘입어 일본은 필리핀을 정조준했다. 그곳에서 그들의 군대는 자신들보다 훨씬 열세인 병력과 맞닥뜨렸다.

한편, 전국 각지의 배치에서 CO들은 자신들만의 공격을 받고 있었다. 그들은 육체적 전투에서 벗어나는 안도는 얻었지만, 그 예외로써 그들이 돌보는 고통받는 이들을 섬길 기회가 생겼다. 다양한 사역을 통해 그들은 모든 종류의 사람들을 만났다. 각 만남은 참된 그리스도인의 평화와 사랑을 전쟁 중에도 보여줄 또 하나의 기회였다. 특히 일부 CO들이 근무한 정신 병원과 병원에서는 더욱 그랬다. 당시 정신 병원의 상태는 통탄할 지경이었다. 환자들은 거칠게 취급되거나 단순히 방치되었으며, 문제 있는 이들은 몇 주 동안 스트레이트 재킷에 묶이거나 자기 오물 속에 살도록 강요받았다. 음식과 위생 상태는 그 필요를 충족시키지 못했다. 몇몇 젊은이들은 신문에 편지를 쓰거나 고향의 지인들에게 학대에 대한 관찰을 자세히 전하는 방식으로 정신 장애인들의 처지를 알렸다. 이러한 행동들은 장애인에 대한 처우에 대한 공중의 인식과 우려를 불러일으켰고, 스스로를 돌볼 수 없는 이들의 돌봄에 변화를 촉진하는 촉매가 되었다.

유감스럽게도 그 섬김의 기회는 대가를伴했다. CO들은 젊었고 교회와 가족으로부터 떨어져 있었다. 그들 주위에는 신앙에 합당하지 않은 영향들이 만연했다. 교회와 가족으로부터 분리되어 있었기 때문에 이러한 영향들이 고향에 있을 때보다 젊은이들의 마음에 더 무겁게 작용했다. 싸움은 여전히 계속되어, 그 어느 때보다도 그들은 힘과 버팀목이자 방패되시는 하나님께 의지해야 했다.

태평양에서는 일본이 필리핀을 압도적 공세로 밀어붙였다. 섬나라는 오랫동안 방어를 준비해 왔으며, 이제 일본 침략자들의 기세로 시험을 받게 되었다. 이 방어군은 조지 A. 맥아더(General George A. MacArthur)의 지휘와 훈련의 산물이었는데, 그는 제1차 세계대전 당시 육군에서 최연소 사단장으로 떠오른 미군의 일종의 신동이었다. 그 후 전간기 동안 그는 대부분을 필리핀에서 보내며 그 해변과 정글을 지키는 임무에 관여했다. 침공이 임박한 수개월 동안 그는 증원군과 최신 장비, 공격을 견딜 수 있는 충분한 물자를 요청했으나, 당시 미국의 초점은 먼저 유럽 전쟁에서 승리하는 데 맞춰져 있었기에 그의 요청은 거부되었고 그는 병력과 화력에서 열세에 놓였다. 그럼에도 맥아더는 진지를 구축하고 불가피한 상륙과 내륙 침투를 막기 위해 준비했다. 그의 부대는 느린 후퇴 과정에서 막대한 사상자를 냈다. 패배가 분명해질 때조차 장군은 섬을 떠나기를 거부했다. 섬이 거의 빼앗길 즈음에야 그는 간신히 적선을 뚫고 빠져나가 호주 배첼러 필드(Batchelor Field)로 대피했다. 그곳에서 그는 남겨둔 이들에게 엄숙히 약속했다. “나는 돌아오겠다.”

지금은 여러 프로젝트와 봉사 분야에 흩어져 있던 CO들도 다양한 도전과 맞닥뜨렸다. 고향 교회의 꾸준한 인도 대신 정부가 임명한 감독관들 아래 놓였다. 캠프 일정은 그들을 주당 최대 여섯 날까지 일하게 했다. 일요일은 일반적으로 예배를 위한 날로 남겨졌다. 전 세계적 전쟁의 영향이 그들 주위에 자리 잡았다. 캐나다의 메노나이트 청년 해리 리트윌러(Harry Litwiller)는 세속적 영향에 빠진 이들 중 하나였다. 그는 군대에 편입되었고 곧 CO 지위를 신청했다. 심사가 진행되는 동안 그는 다른 신병들로부터 도박과 음주를 배웠다. 그의 새로운 습관 소문은 곧 상관들에게 전해졌고 그의 신청은 거부되었다. 교회들은 기도하고 편지를 쓰며 젊은이들을 지원하려 애썼다. 그들은 알지 못했지만, 이들의 시련의 시간은 곧 끝나가고 있었다.

마침내 1945년이 되었다. 전쟁의 마지막 몇 달 동안, 히틀러는 동·서부 연합군에 끼어 막다른 상황에서 젊은 소년들과 노인들을 독일군에 징집하였다. 더 이상 버티지 못한 독일은 항복을 청했다. 유럽에서 전쟁이 끝나자 전세는 태평양으로 옮겨갔다. 미국은 더 큰 산업적 능력과 천연 자원에 힘입어 결집했고, 일본의 진격은 멈추기 시작했다. 이로써 미국의 반격이 시작되었다. 해상을 건너 섬을 하나하나 점령하며 맥아더 장군은 일본에 점점 더 가까이 다가갔다.

맥아더는 필리핀 사람들에게 한 약속을 잊지 않았다. 그의 4년 부재 동안 매우 작은 산호섬—비행장과 주둔부대만 수용할 수 있는 환초들—에 대한 전투들이 벌어졌다. 일본군이 이러한 거점에서 축출되었을 때에도 필리핀에서는 여전히 견고한 발판을 유지하고 있었다. 그 섬나라는 적의 점령 기간을 겪었고, 포로 수용소들이 있어 전쟁 포로들과 연합국을 도운 혐의로 기소된 자들을 수용하고 있었다.

이제 일본에게 남은 시간은 얼마 없었다. 병력과 장비, 자원이 고갈된 채 얇게 분산된 그들은 필사적인 방어전을 벌였다. 1944년 10월 24일 연합군은 레이테 섬의 동해안에 상륙했다. 필리핀을 둘러싼 전투는 두 달 동안 계속되었지만, 결국 맥아더는 승리를 거두었다. 몇 달 전 그는 이미 섬의 항복을 감독했고, 이제는 그 섬을 되찾는 사령관이었다. 그의 약속은 이행되었다.

전쟁은 질질 끌렸다. 유럽에서는 끝났지만 태평양은 아직 승리하지 못했다. 국민을 전쟁으로 이끌었던 프랭클린 D. 루스벨트 대통령은 병환으로 사망했고, 부통령 해리 S. 트루먼이 취임했다. 그의 첫 결정은 그가 상상할 수 있는 어떤 것과도 달랐다. 일본을 육지로 점령하기 위해 수십만의 생명을 희생시킬 것인가, 아니면 상대적으로 공중의 안전에서 새로 개발된 원자폭탄을 투하하여 그들을 끔찍한 본보기로 만들 것인가? 트루먼은 숙고 끝에 결정을 내렸다.

전쟁은 눈 깜짝할 사이에 끝났다. 두 발의 원자폭탄이 일본을 충격으로 몰아넣었고, 일본은 항복을 청했다. 평화가 청원되었고 평화가 주어졌다. 형식적인 절차를 제외하면 전쟁은 끝났다. 끝났지만, 그 일시적 평화는 천문학적인 인명 비용으로 사들여졌다. 수백만이 그들의 슬퍼하는 가족에게 돌아오지 못했다.

CO들에게는 새 일상으로의 복귀가 찾아왔다. 그들은 가족과 교회, 집으로 돌아갔다. 그러나 전쟁은 그들을 변화시켰다. 몇 달, 몇 해 동안 영적 감독 아래 있지 못했다. 많은 이들이 공동체에 정착하여 가정을 이루고 그리스도인 신앙을 살아냈다. 그러나 희생자도 있었고, 해리 리트윌러처럼 신앙을 포기한 이들도 있었다. 싸움은 치열했고, 그 모든 이들이 성경이 제공하는 온전한 군장을 갖추고 있지 않았던 것은 아니다.

맥아더와 승리한 CO들 모두 끝까지 견뎌냈다. 각자는 자신이 믿는 대의를 위해 싸웠다—맥아더는 전쟁의 파괴와 파멸을 위해, CO들은 온전히 항복된 삶의 구속과 평화를 위해. 두 집단은 여기에서 오직 둘 다 싸웠다는 점에서만 평행을 이룬다. 결정적 차이는 그들이 무엇을 위해, 그리고 어떻게 싸웠는지에 있다.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Jesus was in His hometown of Nazareth. It was on the Sabbath, and He stood to read the scripture as He had in the past. This Sabbath He read from Isaiah 61. When He finished, He said, …This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears –Luke 4:21.

This marked the beginning of Jesus’ earthly ministry. In this first sermon He described the nature of His ministry. Notice the many references in this passage to healing: healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, and liberty to the bruised. Jesus came to provide a remedy for our brokenness. He came to repair the damage that sin has brought into humanity.

In this article we will look at the possibility for healing that is found in Jesus. Healing is a process that requires inner restoration with outside remediation. Physical healing begins at the cellular level and restores physical function. Spiritual healing begins at the heart level and restores us to fullness of life. Jesus said, …I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly – John 10:10.

As Jesus walked the dusty paths of Judea, He encountered many who needed physical healing. It was His ability to heal that drew many to seek Him out and to follow him. Many brought their friends and family to Him for healing. There is in all of us a desire for healing and wholeness. In the garden of Eden, mankind was created to be whole. When we are not whole, we seek every possible cure. So, crowds gathered around Jesus hoping for healing.

One day as Jesus was journeying through Jericho, a blind man, Bartimaeus, heard that He was approaching. Hope sprang up in his breast. He began to call out to Jesus, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.” They tried to silence him, but he called the louder, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.”

He cast his coat aside and blindly rushed into the street. Jesus said to him, “What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?” He said, “Lord, that I might receive my sight.” Jesus’ response to this simple faith was, “Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.” Immediately, he received his sight, and followed Jesus. This is just one example of Jesus’ healing ministry. The examples are many. He healed lepers. He healed paralytics. He healed men and women of unclean spirits.

Does Jesus still heal in our day? I would like to answer that question by sharing my own journey of healing. I realize that not all are healed. Even in Jesus’ day, not all were healed. But I want to share my journey of healing to demonstrate the interconnectedness of the physical and the spiritual.

I was diagnosed with cancer in May of 2020. Hearing a doctor say, “You have millions of cancer cells in your body”, brought me face to face with my mortality like never before. Oh, I knew that someday I would die, but that was always somewhere in the far distant future. Now I needed to face the fact that I had a disease growing within me which had the potential to destroy my body.

Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:14-16.

I have always been a strong advocate of anointing with oil. Just like we are taught in the book of James, I called for the elders of the church and asked them to anoint me with oil. In the biblical teaching of God healing through the anointing with oil there are a number of things that are expected of those seeking the healing. There is: call[ing] for the elders of the church, the prayer of faith, pray[ing] one for another, Confess[ing] your faults one to another, the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man… and the list goes on. So, one of the necessities to seek healing through the anointing with oil is the clearing of the heart of any known, unconfessed sin. Hence, I searched my heart and cleansed my heart of anything that would hinder God’s healing of my body.

Notice the close correlation in this passage between the physical and the spiritual. I found in my journey of healing that the one affects the other. Physical healing begins with spiritual healing. A few drops of oil have no therapeutic benefit. This anointing with oil is primarily a spiritual exercise. If we practice this ordinance as James offered it, we cleanse our hearts inwardly and then we ask God for physical healing.

This was my first step to healing, but a long journey lay ahead. We consulted with multiple doctors and eventually we chose a treatment protocol that included radiation and hormone therapy. This treatment weakened me physically and made me feel my humanity. It made me more dependent on God and others and less confident in my own abilities. Living with weakness caused me to draw my strength from my Heavenly Father Who is the source of strength. I relied heavily on the encouragement and support that my wife and family offered.

There are some lessons that can only be learned through human weakness. It was for this reason that Paul was given a thorn in the flesh. He sought the Lord three times for healing. God’s answer came back always the same, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my strength is made perfect in your weakness.” I can testify that that is true.

I had multiple radiation treatments in January of 2021. I had scheduled a series of meetings for the month of February thinking that my treatments would be over, and I would be back to normal. What I did not realize was the delayed effect of radiation. I breezed through the treatments, but in February I experienced a lot of digestive issues and a lot of physical weakness.

I was expected to deliver a series of four sermons on four consecutive evenings. We prayed and although I could not get through the day without napping God provided supernatural strength for those evening messages. I praise God that His strength was made perfect in my weakness.

My doctors have plied their trade. I am grateful for the professional medical care that I received. I have done what I could with herbs and supplements and God has been merciful. My last bloodwork came back “undetectable”. May God be praised!

I am sharing my experience to show the correlation between the physical and the spiritual. Physical illness in my experience had a sanctifying effect on my spirit and spiritual renewal conditioned my body for healing. I will be forever grateful for the professional care given by my doctors, but even they realize the limits of their profession. On my last visit to my Medical Oncologist, he said to me, “Now we are going to trust the Lord.” Thank God for God-fearing doctors!

There are several examples in scripture that demonstrate this correlation between physical and spiritual healing. In Mark 2 when they let the paralytic down through the roof into the presence of Jesus, He said to the paralytic, “Thy sins be forgiven thee.” Then He said, “Rise up and walk.” When He was challenged by the Pharisees for forgiving sins, He said to them, “Which is easier to say rise up and walk or thy sins be forgiven”, demonstrating that He had the power to do both. If we believe that Jesus has the power to forgive our sins, do we also believe that He has the power to heal our bodies? I do!

In John 5, Jesus healed a man who lay by the pool of Bethesda. He had this infirmity for thirty-eight years. Jesus came by and healed him. Later when He met him in the temple He said to him, “Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” Note the correlation between the physical and the spiritual.

Physical infirmity has a tremendous potential to open our hearts to spiritual realities if we allow it to. The Psalmist said: Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word –Psalm 119:67. Jesus said: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Take a fresh look at our proof text for this article and notice that Jesus is offering more than physical healing. He promises healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, and liberty to the bruised. These promises are of emotional healing—healing for the hurt that we receive as a result of living in a broken, sin-cursed world.

I am sure that there are many people reading this article who have experienced trauma that I know nothing about. But I want to assure you that you can be healed. Do you believe that? Do you believe that the pain can go away? Do you believe that you can be delivered from fear, anxiety, anger, and bitterness?

We addressed the correlation between spiritual and physical healing. There is also a correlation between spiritual and emotional healing. If you are experiencing a broken heart, Jesus wants to heal your broken heart. If you are a captive—if you are bound to a past or to an addiction that prevents your freedom—Jesus will set you free. If you have been bruised Jesus will heal you.

My wife and I are appalled at the large number of people in our Anabaptist churches that are turning to psych drugs (mind medication) and secular counseling to find solutions for emotional disorders. The Bible addresses most emotional disorders:

Fear

  • There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear –1 John 4:18.
  • What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3.
  • “Fear not” is found 63 times in the Bible

Anxiety

  • Be careful [anxious] for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God –Philippians 4:6.

Anger

  • Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice –Ephesians 4:31.

This is just a sampling of emotional disorders that we encounter in life, and I realize that behind these emotions there is often deep-seated trauma. Your trauma is not an astonishment to Jesus. He may not have experienced your exact trauma, but he has gone to the depth of your pain, and he has come through it in victory.

For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need –Hebrews 4:15-16.

The gospel provides a holistic remedy to man’s sin problem. Our Anabaptist heritage has emphasized the fact that faith in Jesus affects every area of our lives. This faith motivates us to follow Jesus in very practical ways in our daily lives. This results in a life of radical nonconformity to the world around us.

This radical discipleship should also affect our emotional responses to difficult people and circumstances. Or have we become so emotionally fragile that if life does not give us exactly what we want it upsets our emotional equilibrium? Or maybe the gospel that we preach has become a litany of words that appeases the mind but has no effect on our soul.

Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it –Hebrews 4:1-2. Is our faith in God so weak (remember that in the Biblical accounts of healing, it was their faith that enabled the healing) that we have more faith in medication or in a board-certified secular counselor than we have in God and His Word?

This is a discipleship series. Come with me to the mountain where Jesus is teaching. Yes, there is a large crowd, but follow me closely, we will try to get close enough to hear. I hear His voice—He is saying something about “salt of the earth” and “light of the world.” Here is an empty space—just room for two. Let’s sit on the grass and listen:

“Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.”

These are radical teachings. Radical in that they are so opposite from our natural inclinations, and yet, this is the way of peace. Most of our negative emotions such as anger, fear, and anxiety can be remedied by applying these teachings of Jesus to our situations. This may sound overly simplistic, but that is the nature of the gospel and millions of people have found life and freedom through faith in Christ.

Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s –Psalm 103:1-5.

Der Geist des Herrn ist über mir; darum hat er mich gesalbt, den Armen das Evangelium zu predigen; er hat mich gesandt, die zerbrochenen Herzens zu heilen, Gefangenen Befreiung zu verkündigen und den Blinden das Augenlicht wiederzugeben, Gefangene frei zu setzen, das wohlgefällige Jahr des Herrn zu verkündigen – Lukas 4,18-19.

Jesus war in seiner Heimatstadt Nazareth. Es war am Sabbat, und er stand auf, um die Schrift zu lesen, wie er es früher getan hatte. An diesem Sabbat las er aus Jesaja 61. Als er geendet hatte, sagte er: …Heute ist dieses Schriftwort vor euren Ohren erfüllt – Lukas 4,21.

Das markierte den Beginn von Jesu irdischem Dienst. In dieser ersten Predigt beschrieb er die Natur seines Dienstes. Beachten Sie die vielen Hinweise in diesem Abschnitt auf Heilung: Heilung der zerbrochenen Herzen, Befreiung der Gefangenen, Wiederherstellung des Augenlichts für die Blinden und Freiheit für die Gebeugten. Jesus kam, um ein Heilmittel für unsere Zerbrochenheit zu bringen. Er kam, um den Schaden zu reparieren, den die Sünde in die Menschheit gebracht hat.

In diesem Artikel betrachten wir die Möglichkeit der Heilung, die in Jesus zu finden ist. Heilung ist ein Prozess, der innere Wiederherstellung mit äußerer Maßnahmen verbindet. Körperliche Heilung beginnt auf zellulärer Ebene und stellt die körperliche Funktion wieder her. Geistliche Heilung beginnt im Herzen und stellt uns zur Fülle des Lebens wieder her. Jesus sagte: …Ich bin gekommen, damit sie das Leben haben und es in Fülle haben – Johannes 10,10.

Als Jesus die staubigen Wege Judäas ging, traf er viele, die körperliche Heilung benötigten. Es war seine Fähigkeit zu heilen, die viele dazu brachte, ihn aufzusuchen und ihm nachzufolgen. Viele brachten Freunde und Familie zu ihm zur Heilung. In uns allen liegt der Wunsch nach Heilung und Ganzheit. Im Garten Eden wurde der Mensch zur Ganzheit geschaffen. Wenn wir nicht ganz sind, suchen wir jede mögliche Heilung. So sammelten sich Menschenmengen um Jesus in der Hoffnung auf Heilung.

Eines Tages, als Jesus durch Jericho zog, hörte ein Blinder namens Bartimäus, dass er nahte. Hoffnung entflammte in seiner Brust. Er begann, Jesus anzurufen: „Jesus, du Davidsohn, erbarme dich meiner.“ Sie versuchten, ihn zum Schweigen zu bringen, aber er rief lauter: „Jesus, du Davidsohn, erbarme dich meiner.“

Er warf seinen Mantel beiseite und stürzte blind auf die Straße. Jesus fragte ihn: „Was willst du, dass ich dir tun soll?“ Er sagte: „Herr, dass ich wieder sehe.“ Jesu Antwort auf diesen einfachen Glauben war: „Geh hin; dein Glaube hat dich geheilt.“ Sofort empfing er sein Augenlicht und folgte Jesus nach. Das ist nur ein Beispiel für Jesu Heildienst. Die Beispiele sind zahlreich. Er heilte Aussätzige. Er heilte Gelähmte. Er heilte Männer und Frauen von unreinen Geistern.

Heilt Jesus auch heute noch? Ich möchte diese Frage beantworten, indem ich meinen eigenen Heilsweg teile. Mir ist bewusst, dass nicht alle geheilt werden. Auch zu Jesu Zeit wurden nicht alle geheilt. Aber ich möchte meine Heilungsgeschichte teilen, um die Wechselbeziehung von Körperlichem und Geistlichem zu zeigen.

Bei mir wurde im Mai 2020 Krebs diagnostiziert. Als ein Arzt sagte: „Sie haben Millionen von Krebszellen in Ihrem Körper“, wurde ich wie nie zuvor mit meiner Sterblichkeit konfrontiert. Oh, ich wusste, dass ich eines Tages sterben würde, aber das war immer irgendwo in ferner Zukunft. Nun musste ich der Tatsache ins Auge sehen, dass sich in mir eine Krankheit entwickelte, die das Potenzial hatte, meinen Körper zu zerstören.

Ist jemand unter euch krank? Der rufe die Ältesten der Gemeinde zu sich, und sie sollen über ihn beten und ihn mit Öl salben im Namen des Herrn; Und das Gebet des Glaubens wird den Kranken retten, und der Herr wird ihn aufrichten; und wenn er Sünden getan hat, wird ihm vergeben werden. Bekenntt einander die Sünden und betet füreinander, damit ihr geheilt werdet. Das erflehte Gebet eines Gerechten vermag viel – Jakobus 5,14-16.

Ich war immer ein starker Verfechter der Salbung mit Öl. So wie es im Jakobusbuch gelehrt wird, rief ich die Ältesten der Gemeinde herbei und bat sie, mich mit Öl zu salben. In der biblischen Lehre von Gottes Heilung durch Salbung mit Öl sind eine Reihe von Dingen von denen, die Heilung suchen, zu erwarten. Dazu gehören: das Rufen der Ältesten der Gemeinde, das Gebet des Glaubens, füreinander beten, einander die Fehler bekennen, das erflehte Gebet eines Gerechten … und die Liste geht weiter. Eine der Voraussetzungen, um Heilung durch die Salbung mit Öl zu suchen, ist also das Säubern des Herzens von jeder bekannten, ungebeichteten Sünde. Daher durchsuchte ich mein Herz und reinigte es von allem, was Gottes Heilung meines Körpers hindern könnte.

Beachte die enge Verbindung in diesem Abschnitt zwischen dem Körperlichen und dem Geistlichen. Auf meinem Heilsweg stellte ich fest, dass das eine das andere beeinflusst. Körperliche Heilung beginnt mit geistlicher Heilung. Ein paar Tropfen Öl haben keinen therapeutischen Nutzen. Diese Salbung mit Öl ist in erster Linie eine geistliche Übung. Wenn wir diese Ordination so praktizieren, wie sie Jakobus anbietet, reinigen wir unser Herz innerlich und bitten dann Gott um körperliche Heilung.

Das war mein erster Schritt zur Heilung, aber ein langer Weg lag vor mir. Wir konsultierten mehrere Ärzte und entschieden uns schließlich für ein Behandlungsprotokoll, das Strahlentherapie und Hormontherapie einschloss. Diese Behandlung schwächte mich körperlich und ließ mich meine Menschlichkeit spüren. Sie machte mich abhängiger von Gott und anderen und weniger selbstsicher in meinen eigenen Fähigkeiten. Mit Schwäche zu leben brachte mich dazu, meine Stärke von meinem himmlischen Vater zu ziehen, der die Quelle der Kraft ist. Ich war stark auf die Ermutigung und Unterstützung angewiesen, die mir meine Frau und meine Familie gaben.

Es gibt Lehren, die nur durch menschliche Schwäche gelernt werden können. Aus diesem Grund wurde Paulus ein Dorn im Fleisch gegeben. Er bat den Herrn dreimal um Heilung. Gottes Antwort lautete immer gleich: „Meine Gnade genügt dir; denn meine Kraft wird in der Schwachheit vollendet.“ Ich kann bezeugen, dass das wahr ist.

Ich erhielt mehrere Bestrahlungsbehandlungen im Januar 2021. Ich hatte für den Monat Februar eine Reihe von Veranstaltungen geplant, in der Annahme, dass meine Behandlungen vorbei wären und ich wieder normal wäre. Was ich nicht bedacht hatte, war die verzögerte Wirkung der Strahlentherapie. Ich kam gut durch die Behandlungen, aber im Februar hatte ich viele Verdauungsprobleme und große körperliche Schwäche.

Ich sollte eine Reihe von vier Predigten an vier aufeinanderfolgenden Abenden halten. Wir beteten, und obwohl ich den Tag nicht ohne Nickerchen überstehen konnte, gab Gott übernatürliche Kraft für diese Abendbotschaften. Ich preise Gott, dass seine Kraft in meiner Schwachheit vollendet wurde.

Meine Ärzte haben ihren Beruf ausgeübt. Ich bin dankbar für die professionelle medizinische Versorgung, die ich erhalten habe. Ich habe getan, was ich mit Kräutern und Nahrungsergänzungen konnte, und Gott war barmherzig. Meine letzte Blutuntersuchung ergab „nicht nachweisbar“. Gott sei gepriesen!

Ich teile meine Erfahrung, um die Verbindung zwischen dem Körperlichen und dem Geistlichen zu zeigen. Körperliche Krankheit hatte in meiner Erfahrung eine heilende (heiligende) Wirkung auf meinen Geist, und geistliche Erneuerung bereitete meinen Körper für Heilung vor. Ich werde für immer dankbar sein für die professionelle Betreuung durch meine Ärzte, aber auch sie erkennen die Grenzen ihres Fachgebiets. Bei meinem letzten Besuch bei meinem medizinischen Onkologen sagte er zu mir: „Jetzt werden wir dem Herrn vertrauen.“ Gott sei Dank für gottesfürchtige Ärzte!

Es gibt mehrere Beispiele in der Schrift, die diese Verbindung zwischen körperlicher und geistlicher Heilung zeigen. In Markus 2, als sie den Gelähmten durch das Dach zu Jesus hinabließen, sagte er zu dem Gelähmten: „Deine Sünden sind dir vergeben.“ Dann sagte er: „Steh auf und geh umher.“ Als die Pharisäer ihn herausforderten, weil er Sünden vergab, antwortete er ihnen: „Was ist leichter zu sagen: steh auf und geh umher oder deine Sünden sind dir vergeben?“, und zeigte damit, dass er die Macht hatte, beides zu tun. Wenn wir glauben, dass Jesus die Macht hat, unsere Sünden zu vergeben, glauben wir dann auch, dass er die Macht hat, unsere Körper zu heilen? Ich tue das!

In Johannes 5 heilte Jesus einen Mann, der am Teich Bethesda lag. Er hatte diese Schwachheit achtunddreißig Jahre. Jesus kam vorbei und heilte ihn. Später, als er ihn im Tempel traf, sagte er zu ihm: „Siehe, du bist gesund geworden; sündige hinfort nicht mehr, damit dir nicht etwas Schlimmeres widerfahre.“ Beachte die Verbindung zwischen dem Körperlichen und dem Geistlichen.

Körperliche Gebrechen haben ein enormes Potenzial, unsere Herzen für geistliche Wirklichkeiten zu öffnen, wenn wir es zulassen. Der Psalmist sagte: Bevor ich geplagt wurde, ging ich irre; nun aber halte ich dein Wort – Psalm 119,67. Jesus sagte: Der Geist des Herrn ist über mich; darum hat er mich gesalbt, den Armen das Evangelium zu predigen; er hat mich gesandt, die zerbrochenen Herzens zu heilen, Gefangenen Befreiung zu verkündigen und den Blinden das Augenlicht wiederzugeben, Gefangene frei zu setzen, das wohlgefällige Jahr des Herrn zu verkündigen – Lukas 4,18-19.

Betrachten Sie unseren Beweistext für diesen Artikel noch einmal und beachten Sie, dass Jesus mehr als nur körperliche Heilung anbietet. Er verspricht Heilung für die Zerbrochenen, Befreiung für die Gefangenen und Freiheit für die Gebeugten. Diese Verheißungen betreffen seelische Heilung – Heilung für den Schmerz, den wir als Folge des Lebens in einer zerbrochenen, von der Sünde verfluchten Welt erleiden.

Ich bin sicher, dass viele, die diesen Artikel lesen, Traumata erlebt haben, von denen ich nichts weiß. Aber ich möchte Ihnen versichern, dass Sie geheilt werden können. Glauben Sie das? Glauben Sie, dass der Schmerz weggehen kann? Glauben Sie, dass Sie von Furcht, Angst, Zorn und Bitterkeit befreit werden können?

Wir haben die Verbindung zwischen geistlicher und körperlicher Heilung angesprochen. Es besteht auch eine Verbindung zwischen geistlicher und emotionaler Heilung. Wenn dein Herz gebrochen ist, will Jesus dein gebrochenes Herz heilen. Wenn du ein Gefangener bist – wenn du an eine Vergangenheit oder an eine Sucht gebunden bist, die dir die Freiheit raubt – wird dich Jesus frei machen. Wenn du geschlagen bist, wird Jesus dich heilen.

Meine Frau und ich sind entsetzt über die große Zahl von Menschen in unseren mennonitisch-anabaptistischen Gemeinden, die zu Psychopharmaka (Geist-medikation) und weltlicher Beratung greifen, um Lösungen für emotionale Probleme zu finden. Die Bibel spricht die meisten emotionalen Störungen an:

Furcht

  • In der Liebe ist keine Furcht; sondern die vollkommene Liebe treibt die Furcht aus – 1. Johannes 4,18.
  • Wenn ich mich fürchte, so vertraue ich auf dich – Psalm 56,3.
  • „Fürchte dich nicht“ kommt 63 Mal in der Bibel vor

Angst

  • Seid um nichts besorgt; sondern in allen Dingen lasst eure Anliegen durch Gebet und Flehen mit Danksagung vor Gott kundwerden – Philipper 4,6.

Zorn

  • Alle Bitterkeit und Grimm und Zorn und Geschrei und Lästerung sei von euch weggetan samt aller Bosheit – Epheser 4,31.

Dies ist nur eine Auswahl emotionaler Störungen, denen wir im Leben begegnen, und mir ist bewusst, dass hinter diesen Gefühlen oft tief sitzendes Trauma liegt. Dein Trauma ist für Jesus keine Überraschung. Er hat vielleicht nicht genau dein Erlebnis erfahren, aber er ist in die Tiefe deines Schmerzes eingegangen und hat ihn überwunden.

Denn wir haben nicht einen Hohenpriester, der nicht Mitleid haben könnte mit unserer Schwachheit; vielmehr ist er in allem versucht worden wie wir, doch ohne Sünde. So lasst uns nun freimütig hinzutreten zum Thron der Gnade, damit wir Barmherzigkeit empfangen und Gnade finden, die uns rechtzeitig hilft – Hebräer 4,15-16.

Das Evangelium bietet eine ganzheitliche Lösung für das Sündenproblem des Menschen. Unser anabaptistisches Erbe hat betont, dass der Glaube an Jesus jeden Bereich unseres Lebens beeinflusst. Dieser Glaube motiviert uns, Jesus auf sehr praktische Weise in unserem täglichen Leben nachzufolgen. Das führt zu einem Leben radikaler Nichtanpassung an die Welt um uns herum.

Diese radikale Jüngerschaft sollte auch unsere emotionalen Reaktionen auf schwierige Menschen und Umstände beeinflussen. Oder sind wir so emotional zerbrechlich geworden, dass uns das Leben aus dem seelischen Gleichgewicht bringt, wenn es uns nicht genau das gibt, was wir wollen? Oder ist das Evangelium, das wir predigen, zu einer Litanei von Worten geworden, die den Verstand besänftigt, aber keine Wirkung auf unsere Seele hat?

Lasst uns nun dafür fürchten, dass nicht, wenn eine Verheißung übriggeblieben ist, zu der wir gelangen sollen, jemand von euch es so erscheine, als käme er nicht dazu. Denn uns ist das Evangelium wie ihnen verkündigt worden; aber das Predigtwort nutzete ihnen nicht, nicht vermischt mit Glauben bei denen, die es hörten – Hebräer 4,1-2. Ist unser Glaube an Gott so schwach (denke daran, dass in den biblischen Heilungsberichten ihr Glaube die Heilung möglich machte), dass wir mehr Vertrauen in Medikamente oder in einen staatlich anerkannten weltlichen Berater haben als in Gott und sein Wort?

Dies ist eine Jüngerschaftsreihe. Komm mit mir auf den Berg, wo Jesus lehrt. Ja, es ist eine große Menge, aber folge mir genau, wir versuchen, nahe genug zu kommen, um zu hören. Ich höre seine Stimme – er sagt etwas von „Salz der Erde“ und „Licht der Welt“. Hier ist ein freier Platz – gerade genug für zwei. Lasst uns auf dem Gras sitzen und zuhören:

„Ihr habt gehört, dass gesagt ist: Auge um Auge und Zahn um Zahn. Ich aber sage euch: Widersteht dem Bösen nicht; sondern wenn dich jemand auf deine rechte Wange schlägt, dem biete auch die andere dar.

Und wenn jemand dich verklagt und dir dein Hemd nimmt, so lass ihm auch den Mantel. Und wer dich nötigt, eine Meile mitzugehen, dem geh zwei. Gib dem, der dich bittet, und wende dich nicht ab von dem, der von dir borgen will.

Ihr habt gehört, dass gesagt ist: Du sollst deinen Nächsten lieben und deinen Feind hassen. Ich aber sage euch: Liebt eure Feinde, segnet die, die euch fluchen, tut Gutes denen, die euch hassen, und bittet für die, die euch beleidigen und verfolgen; damit ihr Kinder eures Vaters im Himmel werdet; denn er lässt seine Sonne aufgehen über Böse und Gute und lässt regnen über Gerechte und Ungerechte.“

Das sind radikale Lehren. Radikal, weil sie so gegensätzlich zu unseren natürlichen Neigungen sind, und doch ist dies der Weg des Friedens. Die meisten unserer negativen Emotionen wie Zorn, Furcht und Angst können durch die Anwendung dieser Lehren Jesu auf unsere Situationen geheilt werden. Das mag übermäßig vereinfacht klingen, aber das ist die Natur des Evangeliums, und Millionen Menschen haben Leben und Freiheit durch den Glauben an Christus gefunden.

Lobe den HERRN, meine Seele; und alles, was in mir ist, seinen heiligen Namen. Lobe den HERRN, meine Seele, und vergiss nicht alle seine Wohltaten: Der dir alle deine Sünden vergibt, der dir alle deine Gebrechen heilt; Der dein Leben vom Verderben erlöst, der dich krönt mit Gnadenerweisen und Erbarmen; Der dir den Mund sättigt mit Gutem, dass sich dein Jugendgefahr wie des Adlers erneuert – Psalm 103,1-5.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Jesus was in His hometown of Nazareth. It was on the Sabbath, and He stood to read the scripture as He had in the past. This Sabbath He read from Isaiah 61. When He finished, He said, …This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears –Luke 4:21.

This marked the beginning of Jesus’ earthly ministry. In this first sermon He described the nature of His ministry. Notice the many references in this passage to healing: healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, recovering of sight to the blind, and liberty to the bruised. Jesus came to provide a remedy for our brokenness. He came to repair the damage that sin has brought into humanity.

In this article we will look at the possibility for healing that is found in Jesus. Healing is a process that requires inner restoration with outside remediation. Physical healing begins at the cellular level and restores physical function. Spiritual healing begins at the heart level and restores us to fullness of life. Jesus said, …I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly – John 10:10.

As Jesus walked the dusty paths of Judea, He encountered many who needed physical healing. It was His ability to heal that drew many to seek Him out and to follow him. Many brought their friends and family to Him for healing. There is in all of us a desire for healing and wholeness. In the garden of Eden, mankind was created to be whole. When we are not whole, we seek every possible cure. So, crowds gathered around Jesus hoping for healing.

One day as Jesus was journeying through Jericho, a blind man, Bartimaeus, heard that He was approaching. Hope sprang up in his breast. He began to call out to Jesus, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.” They tried to silence him, but he called the louder, “Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.”

He cast his coat aside and blindly rushed into the street. Jesus said to him, “What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?” He said, “Lord, that I might receive my sight.” Jesus’ response to this simple faith was, “Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.” Immediately, he received his sight, and followed Jesus. This is just one example of Jesus’ healing ministry. The examples are many. He healed lepers. He healed paralytics. He healed men and women of unclean spirits.

Does Jesus still heal in our day? I would like to answer that question by sharing my own journey of healing. I realize that not all are healed. Even in Jesus’ day, not all were healed. But I want to share my journey of healing to demonstrate the interconnectedness of the physical and the spiritual.

I was diagnosed with cancer in May of 2020. Hearing a doctor say, “You have millions of cancer cells in your body”, brought me face to face with my mortality like never before. Oh, I knew that someday I would die, but that was always somewhere in the far distant future. Now I needed to face the fact that I had a disease growing within me which had the potential to destroy my body.

Is any sick among you? let him call for the elders of the church; and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord: And the prayer of faith shall save the sick, and the Lord shall raise him up; and if he have committed sins, they shall be forgiven him. Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much –James 5:14-16.

I have always been a strong advocate of anointing with oil. Just like we are taught in the book of James, I called for the elders of the church and asked them to anoint me with oil. In the biblical teaching of God healing through the anointing with oil there are a number of things that are expected of those seeking the healing. There is: call[ing] for the elders of the church, the prayer of faith, pray[ing] one for another, Confess[ing] your faults one to another, the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man… and the list goes on. So, one of the necessities to seek healing through the anointing with oil is the clearing of the heart of any known, unconfessed sin. Hence, I searched my heart and cleansed my heart of anything that would hinder God’s healing of my body.

Notice the close correlation in this passage between the physical and the spiritual. I found in my journey of healing that the one affects the other. Physical healing begins with spiritual healing. A few drops of oil have no therapeutic benefit. This anointing with oil is primarily a spiritual exercise. If we practice this ordinance as James offered it, we cleanse our hearts inwardly and then we ask God for physical healing.

This was my first step to healing, but a long journey lay ahead. We consulted with multiple doctors and eventually we chose a treatment protocol that included radiation and hormone therapy. This treatment weakened me physically and made me feel my humanity. It made me more dependent on God and others and less confident in my own abilities. Living with weakness caused me to draw my strength from my Heavenly Father Who is the source of strength. I relied heavily on the encouragement and support that my wife and family offered.

There are some lessons that can only be learned through human weakness. It was for this reason that Paul was given a thorn in the flesh. He sought the Lord three times for healing. God’s answer came back always the same, “My grace is sufficient for you, for my strength is made perfect in your weakness.” I can testify that that is true.

I had multiple radiation treatments in January of 2021. I had scheduled a series of meetings for the month of February thinking that my treatments would be over, and I would be back to normal. What I did not realize was the delayed effect of radiation. I breezed through the treatments, but in February I experienced a lot of digestive issues and a lot of physical weakness.

I was expected to deliver a series of four sermons on four consecutive evenings. We prayed and although I could not get through the day without napping God provided supernatural strength for those evening messages. I praise God that His strength was made perfect in my weakness.

My doctors have plied their trade. I am grateful for the professional medical care that I received. I have done what I could with herbs and supplements and God has been merciful. My last bloodwork came back “undetectable”. May God be praised!

I am sharing my experience to show the correlation between the physical and the spiritual. Physical illness in my experience had a sanctifying effect on my spirit and spiritual renewal conditioned my body for healing. I will be forever grateful for the professional care given by my doctors, but even they realize the limits of their profession. On my last visit to my Medical Oncologist, he said to me, “Now we are going to trust the Lord.” Thank God for God-fearing doctors!

There are several examples in scripture that demonstrate this correlation between physical and spiritual healing. In Mark 2 when they let the paralytic down through the roof into the presence of Jesus, He said to the paralytic, “Thy sins be forgiven thee.” Then He said, “Rise up and walk.” When He was challenged by the Pharisees for forgiving sins, He said to them, “Which is easier to say rise up and walk or thy sins be forgiven”, demonstrating that He had the power to do both. If we believe that Jesus has the power to forgive our sins, do we also believe that He has the power to heal our bodies? I do!

In John 5, Jesus healed a man who lay by the pool of Bethesda. He had this infirmity for thirty-eight years. Jesus came by and healed him. Later when He met him in the temple He said to him, “Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” Note the correlation between the physical and the spiritual.

Physical infirmity has a tremendous potential to open our hearts to spiritual realities if we allow it to. The Psalmist said: Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word –Psalm 119:67. Jesus said: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, To preach the acceptable year of the Lord –Luke 4:18-19.

Take a fresh look at our proof text for this article and notice that Jesus is offering more than physical healing. He promises healing to the brokenhearted, deliverance to the captives, and liberty to the bruised. These promises are of emotional healing—healing for the hurt that we receive as a result of living in a broken, sin-cursed world.

I am sure that there are many people reading this article who have experienced trauma that I know nothing about. But I want to assure you that you can be healed. Do you believe that? Do you believe that the pain can go away? Do you believe that you can be delivered from fear, anxiety, anger, and bitterness?

We addressed the correlation between spiritual and physical healing. There is also a correlation between spiritual and emotional healing. If you are experiencing a broken heart, Jesus wants to heal your broken heart. If you are a captive—if you are bound to a past or to an addiction that prevents your freedom—Jesus will set you free. If you have been bruised Jesus will heal you.

My wife and I are appalled at the large number of people in our Anabaptist churches that are turning to psych drugs (mind medication) and secular counseling to find solutions for emotional disorders. The Bible addresses most emotional disorders:

Fear

  • There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear –1 John 4:18.
  • What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee –Psalm 56:3.
  • “Fear not” is found 63 times in the Bible

Anxiety

  • Be careful [anxious] for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God –Philippians 4:6.

Anger

  • Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice –Ephesians 4:31.

This is just a sampling of emotional disorders that we encounter in life, and I realize that behind these emotions there is often deep-seated trauma. Your trauma is not an astonishment to Jesus. He may not have experienced your exact trauma, but he has gone to the depth of your pain, and he has come through it in victory.

For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need –Hebrews 4:15-16.

The gospel provides a holistic remedy to man’s sin problem. Our Anabaptist heritage has emphasized the fact that faith in Jesus affects every area of our lives. This faith motivates us to follow Jesus in very practical ways in our daily lives. This results in a life of radical nonconformity to the world around us.

This radical discipleship should also affect our emotional responses to difficult people and circumstances. Or have we become so emotionally fragile that if life does not give us exactly what we want it upsets our emotional equilibrium? Or maybe the gospel that we preach has become a litany of words that appeases the mind but has no effect on our soul.

Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it. For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it –Hebrews 4:1-2. Is our faith in God so weak (remember that in the Biblical accounts of healing, it was their faith that enabled the healing) that we have more faith in medication or in a board-certified secular counselor than we have in God and His Word?

This is a discipleship series. Come with me to the mountain where Jesus is teaching. Yes, there is a large crowd, but follow me closely, we will try to get close enough to hear. I hear His voice—He is saying something about “salt of the earth” and “light of the world.” Here is an empty space—just room for two. Let’s sit on the grass and listen:

“Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.

And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloak also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.

Ye have heard that it hath been said, Thou shalt love thy neighbour, and hate thine enemy. But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you; That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust.”

These are radical teachings. Radical in that they are so opposite from our natural inclinations, and yet, this is the way of peace. Most of our negative emotions such as anger, fear, and anxiety can be remedied by applying these teachings of Jesus to our situations. This may sound overly simplistic, but that is the nature of the gospel and millions of people have found life and freedom through faith in Christ.

Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle’s –Psalm 103:1-5.
