Mwanga wa Bwana uko juu yangu, maana ameninyoosha kuwa nimtangaze maskini habari njema; Amenituma nikuponye waliovuawa moyo, nitangaze uwekaji huru kwa wale waliotawaliwa, na kuwarejeshea kuona vipofu; kuwaweka huru waliopondeka, kutangaza mwaka wa kupendekezwa wa Bwana – Luka 4:18-19.

Yesu alikuwa katika mji wake wa kuzaliwa Nazareti. Ilikuwa siku ya Sabato, naye alisimama kusoma maandiko kama alivyokuwa akifanya hapo awali. Sabato hii alisoma kutoka Isaya 61. Alipoisha, akasema, …Leo maandiko haya yamekamilika machoni mwenu – Luka 4:21.

Hii ilitambulisha mwanzo wa huduma ya Yesu duniani. Katika hotuba yake ya kwanza aliainisha asili ya huduma yake. Angalieni marejeleo mengi katika kifungu hiki kuhusu uponyaji: kuponya waliovuawa moyo, uwekaji huru kwa waliotawaliwa, kurudisha kuona kwa vipofu, na uhuru kwa waliopondeka. Yesu alikuja kuleta tiba kwa uvunjifu wetu. Alikuja kutengeneza uharibifu ambao dhambi imeleta kwa ubinadamu.

Katika makala hii tutaangalia uwezekano wa uponyaji ulio katika Yesu. Uponyaji ni mchakato unaohitaji urejesho wa ndani pamoja na ufumbuzi wa nje. Uponyaji wa kimwili huanza kwa ngazi ya seli na kurejesha kazi za mwili. Uponyaji wa kiroho huanza katika ngazi ya moyo na huturejesha kwa ukamilifu wa maisha. Yesu alisema, …Nimekuja ili wawe na uzima, na wawe nao kwa wingi – Yohana 10:10.

Wakati Yesu alipokuwa akitembea njia za vumbi za Yudea, alikutana na wengi waliokuwa wanahitaji uponyaji wa kimwili. Uwezo wake wa kuponya ndio ulivutia wengi kumwendeleza na kumfuata. Wengi walileta marafiki zao na familia kwake ili aopeanwe uponyaji. Kila mmoja wetu ana tamaa ya uponyaji na ukamilifu. Katika bustani ya Edeni, binadamu aliumbwa kuwa mkamilifu. Tunapokuwa hatukamilifu, tunatafuta kila tiba inayowezekana. Hivyo, umati ulizunguka Yesu wakitafuta uponyaji.

Siku moja Yesu alipokuwa akiwasili Yeriko, mlemavu wa macho, Bartimayo, aliposikia kwamba Yesu anakaribia, tumaini likamshika moyoni. Akaanza kumpigia kelele Yesu, “Yesu, wewe mwana wa Daudi, niee hurumia.” Walijaribu kumatafuta kutiisha sauti yake, lakini alipiga kelele kwa nguvu zaidi, “Yesu, wewe mwana wa Daudi, niee hurumia.”

Alitupa koti lake pembeni na kwa kufuata bila kuona alikimbilia katikati ya mtaa. Yesu akamwambia, “Unataka nifanye nini kwako?” Akasema, “Bwana, nipatie kuona.” Jibu la Yesu kwa imani rahisi hiyo lilikuwa, “Nenda; imani yako imekukufanya uwe mzima.” Mara moja, alipata kuona, akamuunga Yesu. Hii ni mfano mmoja tu wa huduma ya uponyaji ya Yesu. Kuna mifano mingi. Aliwaponya nyamaza. Aliwaponya wenye kuharibika mwili. Aliwaponya wanaume na wanawake waliokuwa na roho wasio safi.

Je, Yesu bado anaponya siku zetu hizi? Ningependa kujibu swali hilo kwa kushiriki safari yangu ya uponyaji. Natambua kwamba si wote wanaponya. Hata siku za Yesu, si wote waliponywa. Lakini nataka kushiriki safari yangu ya uponyaji ili kuonyesha uhusiano wa ndani kati ya kimwili na kiroho.

Niligundulika kuwa na saratani mwezi Mei mwaka 2020. Kusikia daktari akisema, “Una mamilioni ya seli za saratani mwilini mwako”, kulinisukuma uso kwa uso na kifo changu kama sikuwahi hapo awali. Oh, nilijua kwamba siku moja nitaaga dunia, lakini hapo hapo ilikuwa mbali sana. Sasa nililazimika kukabiliana na ukweli kwamba nilikuwa na ugonjwa unaokua ndani yangu ambao ulikuwa na uwezo wa kuharibu mwili wangu.

Kuna miongoni mwa nyinyi aliye mgonjwa? aite wazee wa kanisa; nao wakamwombee, wakimchukua kwa mafuta kwa jina la Bwana: Na sala ya imani itaokoa mgonjwa, naye Bwana atamfufua; na kama ametenda dhambi, atamsamehe. Ombeni dhambi zenu mmoja kwa mwingine, na muombee mwenzenu, ili mpone. Sala yenye nguvu ya mtu mwadilifu inafanya mengi – Yakobo 5:14-16.

Siku zote nimekuwa mkemeaji wa kutengeneza mafuta kwa kumwagwa. Kama tunavyofundishwa katika kitabu cha Yakobo, nilimuita wazee wa kanisa na kuwaomba waanidishe kwa mafuta. Katika mafundisho ya kibiblia ya Mungu kuponya kupitia kunyanywa kwa mafuta kuna mambo kadhaa yanayotarajiwa kwa wale wanaotafuta uponyaji. Kapo: kumuita wazee wa kanisa, sala ya imani, kuombeana, kutamka dhambi zako mmoja kwa mwingine, sala yenye nguvu ya mtu mwadilifu…na orodha inaendelea. Hivyo, mojawapo ya mahitaji ya kutafuta uponyaji kupitia kunyanywa kwa mafuta ni kusafisha moyo wa dhambi yoyote inayojulikana na isiyothibitishwa. Kwa hivyo, nilitafakari moyo wangu na kulisafisha kwa yale yote yangekukwamisha uponyaji wa mwili wangu na Mungu.

Angalieni uwiano wa karibu katika kifungu hiki kati ya kimwili na kiroho. Nilipolitembea katika safari yangu ya uponyaji niligundua kwamba kimoja kinaathiri kingine. Uponyaji wa kimwili huanza kwa uponyaji wa kiroho. Madoa machache ya mafuta hayana faida ya tiba. Kunyanywa kwa mafuta ni zoezi la kiroho kwa msingi. Tukifanya amri hii kama ilivyoletwa na Yakobo, tunasafisha moyo wetu ndani kisha tunaomba Mungu uponyaji wa kimwili.

Huu ulikuwa hatua yangu ya kwanza kwenda kwenye uponyaji, lakini safari ndefu ilikuwa mbele. Tulishauriana na madaktari wengi na hatimaye tukachagua taratibu za matibabu zilizojaa mionzi na matibabu ya homoni. Tiba hii iliniondoa nguvu kimwili na ilinifanya nihisi ubinadamu wangu. Ilinifanya nimtegemeze zaidi Mungu na wengine na nisitumaini uwezo wangu mwenyewe. Kuishi ukiwa dhaifu kulinifanya nivute nguvu zangu kutoka kwa Baba yangu wa Mbingu Asili ya nguvu. Nilitegemea sana faraja na msaada waliyonipa mke wangu na familia.

Kuna mafundisho ambayo yanafundishwa tu kupitia udhaifu wa binadamu. Hii ndiyo sababu Paulo alipopewa ncha ya kazi katika mwili. Aliomba kwa Bwana mara tatu kwa uponyaji. Jibu la Mungu lilirudi kila wakati lile, “Neema yangu ikutoshe, kwa maana nguvu yangu inafanywa kamilifu katika udhaifu wako.” Ninaweza kushuhudia kwamba hilo ni kweli.

Nilipata matibabu ya mionzi mara kadhaa mwezi Januari 2021. Nilikuwa nimepanga mfululizo wa mikutano kwa mwezi wa Februari nikidhani kwamba matibabu yangu yangeisha, na ningerudi kuwa kawaida. Kile nisichokiwa ni athari zilizoahirishwa za mionzi. Nilipita kwa urahisi kupitia matibabu, lakini mwezi Februari nilikumbana na matatizo mengi ya mmeng'enyo na udhaifu mkubwa wa kimwili.

Nilitarajiwa kutoa mfululizo wa mahubiri manne katika jioni nne mfululizo. Tuliomba na ingawa sikuweza kuvumilia siku bila kulala usingizi, Mungu alitupatia nguvu za kihangaika kwa yale mahubiri ya jioni. Ninamshukuru Mungu kwamba nguvu zake zilitendeka kamilifu katika udhaifu wangu.

Madaktari wangu wamefanya kazi yao. Ninashukuru kwa huduma ya kitaalamu ya matibabu niliyoipata. Nimefanya kile nilichoweza kwa mimea na viwango vya lishe na Mungu ametenda rehema. Uchunguzi wangu wa damu wa mwisho ulibaki “hauonekani.” Mungu apendwe!

Ninashiriki uzoefu wangu kuonyesha uhusiano kati ya kimwili na kiroho. Kwa uzoefu wangu ugonjwa wa kimwili ulikuwa na athari ya utakatisho kwa roho yangu na upya wa kiroho uliandaa mwili wangu kwa uponyaji. Nitashukuru milele kwa uangalizi wa kitaalamu uliotolewa na madaktari wangu, lakini hata wao wanatambua mipaka ya taaluma yao. Katika ziara yangu ya mwisho kwa Onkolojia yangu ya Tiba, alisema kwangu, “Sasa tutaweka imani kwa Bwana.” Asifiwe Mungu kwa madaktari wanaomtukuza Mungu!

Kuna mifano kadhaa katika maandiko inayothibitisha uhusiano huu kati ya uponyaji wa kimwili na kiroho. Katika Marko 2 walipopandisha mlemavu juu kupitia paa mbele ya Yesu, Yesu akamwambia mlemavu, “Dharma zako zimesamehewa kwako.” Kisha Akasema, “Inuka, nitenge.” Walipompinga kwa Mafarisayo kwa kusamehe dhambi, Alisema kwao, “Ni rahisi kusema inuka, nitenge au dharma zako zimesamehewa”, akionyesha kwamba alikuwa na uwezo wa kufanya yote mawili. Ikiwa tunaamini kwamba Yesu ana nguvu ya kusamehe dhambi zetu, je, tunaamini pia kwamba Ana nguvu ya kuponya miili yetu? Mimi naamini!

Katika Yohana 5, Yesu aliponya mtu aliyekuwa amelala karibu na bwawa la Bethesda. Alikuwa na ugonjwa huo kwa miaka thelathini na nane. Yesu alikuja naye na kumponya. Baadaye alikutana naye kwenye hekalu akamwambia, “Tazama, umefanywa wa kuishi: usonge dhambi tena, mpunguzi zaidi akikuwe.” Kumbuka uwiano kati ya kimwili na kiroho.

Ugonjwa wa kimwili una uwezo mkubwa wa kufungua mioyo yetu kwa ukweli wa kiroho ikiwa tutaruhusu. Mwanamzabibu alisema: Kabla nilipoteshwa nilitenda kimakosa: sasa nimefuata neno lako – Zaburi 119:67. Yesu alisema: Mwanga wa Bwana uko juu yangu, maana ameninyoosha kuwa nimtangaze maskini habari njema; Amenituma nikuponye waliovuawa moyo, nitangaze uwekaji huru kwa wale waliotawaliwa, na kuwarejeshea kuona vipofu; kuwaweka huru waliopondeka, kutangaza mwaka wa kupendekezwa wa Bwana – Luka 4:18-19.

Chukua mtazamo mpya kwa kifungu chetu cha ushahidi kwa makala hii na uone kwamba Yesu anatoa zaidi ya uponyaji wa kimwili. Aahidi uponyaji kwa waliovuawa moyo, uwekaji huru kwa waliotawaliwa, na uhuru kwa waliopondeka. Ahadi hizi ni za uponyaji wa hisia—uponyaji kwa maumivu tuliyopata kwa kuishi katika dunia iliyovunjika, iliyochanganywa na dhambi.

Nina uhakika kuwa kuna watu wengi wanaosoma makala hii ambao wamepitia madhara ambayo sijui. Lakini nataka kuwahakikishia kuwa mnaweza kuponywa. Je, unaamini hivyo? Je, unaamini kwamba maumivu yanaweza kuondoka? Je, unaamini kwamba unaweza kutolewa kutoka kwa hofu, wasi wasi, hasira, na uchungu?

Tulizungumzia uhusiano kati ya uponyaji wa kiroho na wa kimwili. Pia kuna uhusiano kati ya uponyaji wa kiroho na wa kihisia. Ikiwa una moyo uliovunjika, Yesu anataka kuponya moyo wako uliovunjika. Ikiwa wewe ni mfungwa—ikiwa umefungwa kwa zamani au kwa uraibu unaokuzuia uhuru wako—Yesu atakuweka huru. Ikiwa umekuwa mkomwa Yesu atakuponya.

Mke wangu na mimi tunashangaa idadi kubwa ya watu katika makanisa yetu ya Anabaptisti ambao wanageukia dawa za akili (dawa za akili) na ushauri wa kidunia kutafuta suluhisho kwa matatizo ya kihisia. Biblia inashughulikia matatizo mengi ya kihisia:

Hofu

  • Katika upendo hakuna hofu; bali upendo kamili hutupilia mbali hofu – 1 Yohana 4:18.
  • Wakati nitakapokuwa na hofu, nitakutegemea wewe – Zaburi 56:3.
  • “Usiogope” hupatikana mara 63 katika Biblia

Wasiwasi

  • Msijali wala kwa vitu; bali katika yote kwa sala na maombi pamoja na shukrani mtaelezea matarajio yenu kwa Mungu – Wafilipi 4:6.

Hasira

  • Kuondoe kabisa uchungu, na hasira, na chuki, na kelele, na kuzungumza ubaya, mbali nanyi wote, pamoja na uhasama wote – Waefeso 4:31.

Hii ni sampuli tu ya matatizo ya kihisia tunayokutana nayo maishani, na natambua kwamba nyuma ya hisia hizi mara nyingi kuna madhara makubwa yaliyopitiliza. Madhara yako sio ya mshangao kwa Yesu. Huenda hakuwahi kupitia madhara yako hasa, lakini amepitia kina cha maumivu yako, na ametoka humo kwa ushindi.

Mimi si mwanapadri mkuu ambaye asiweze kuguswa na hisia za magonjwa yetu; bali alijaribiwa katika mambo yote kama sisi, isipokuwa bila dhambi. Tuwe basi kwa ujasiri tukamrukiwa kiti cha neema, ili tupate rehema na kupata neema ya kusaidiwa wakati wa uhitaji – Wahudi 4:15-16.

Injili inatoa tiba kamili ya shida ya dhambi ya mwanadamu. Urithi wetu wa Anabaptisti umeweka mkazo kwamba imani kwa Yesu inaathiri kila eneo la maisha yetu. Imani hii inatuchochea kumfuata Yesu kwa njia za vitendo katika maisha yetu ya kila siku. Hii inasababisha maisha ya kutokubaliana kwa kina na ulimwengu unaotuzunguka.

Ufuasi wa kikimbilio huu pia unapaswa kuathiri majibu yetu ya kihisia kwa watu na mazingira magumu. Au je, tumekuwa dhaifu kihisia kiasi kwamba ikiwa maisha hayatupatii hasa kile tunataka basi inavuruga usawa wetu wa kihisia? Au labda injili tunayoihubiri imekuwa mfululizo wa maneno yanayotuliza akili lakini hayana athari kwa nafsi yetu.

Tuwe basi tukihofu, jamani, pengine ahadi iliyotolewa kwetu ya kuingia katika mapumziko yake, mtu yeyote kati yenu asije akawa mkomo yake. Kwetu pia ilihubiriwa injili, kama ilivyohubiriwa kwao; lakini neno lililohubiriwa halikuwasaidia, kwa kutokujumuishwa kwa imani kwa wale waliolisikia – Wahudi 4:1-2. Je, imani yetu kwa Mungu ni dhaifu kiasi gani (kumbuka kwamba katika maelezo ya Biblia kuhusu uponyaji, ilikuwa imani yao iliyoifanya uponyaji uweze) kwamba tunaamini zaidi kwenye dawa au mshauri wa kivitendo wa kidunia kuliko tunavyoamini Mungu na Neno lake?

Hii ni mfululizo wa ufuasi. Njoo nami kwenye mlima ambako Yesu anafundisha. Ndiyo, kuna umati mkubwa, lakini nifuateni kwa karibu, tutajaribu kutosheka kusikia. Nasikia sauti yake—Anasema kitu kuhusu “chumvi ya dunia” na “mwanga wa dunia.” Hapa kuna nafasi tupu—tu nafasi kwa wawili. Tuketi kwa nyasi na tusikilize:

“Mmejisikia kuwa ilisemwa, Jicho kwa jicho, meno kwa meno: Bali mimi nawaambia, Msipigane na uovu; bali yeye ambaye atakupiga upande wa kulia wa uso wako, mgeukie pia mwingine.

Na ikiwa mtu mwingine atakutaka kortini, na kuchukua koti lako, mpe pia kapeti yako. Na yule ambaye atakusaliti kwenda umbali wa maili moja, nenda naye maili mbili. Mpe msiyetaka, na usimkimbie mwombaji.

Mmejisikia kuwa ilisemwa, Utampenda jirani yako, na umchukie adui yako. Lakini mimi nawaambia, Mpende maadui zenu, muwabariki wakao wanaokutukana, wafanyie mema wale wanaokwenda kukuchukia, na waombee wale wanaotukana nanyi, na kuwatawanya; Ili mje kuwa watoto wa Baba yenu aliye mbinguni: maana yeye hufanya jua lake lipuke juu ya mabaya na wema, na kutuma mvua kwa wenye haki na wasio haki.”

Haya ni mafundisho ya kina. Ya kina kwa kuwa yanapingana kabisa na mwelekeo wetu wa asili, na bado, huu ndiyo njia ya amani. Hisia zetu nyingi hasi kama hasira, hofu, na wasi wasi zinaweza kutibiwa kwa kutekeleza mafundisho haya ya Yesu kwa hali zetu. Hii inaweza kuonekana rahisi kupita kiasi, lakini hiyo ni asili ya injili na mamilioni ya watu wamepata uzima na uhuru kupitia imani katika Kristo.

Msifu Bwana, roho yangu: na yote yaliyomo ndani yangu yimwabuduye jina lake takatifu. Msifu Bwana, roho yangu, wala usisahau faida zake zote: Yeye anayesamehe dhambi zako zote; yeye anaponya magonjwa yako yote; Yeye anayokuokoa maisha yako kutoka mauti; yeye anakushika kwa wema na rehema; Yeye anayekufidianisha kinywa chako kwa vitu vyema; hata ujana wako urudishwe kama mwewe – Zaburi 103:1-5.

The history of our world has been defined by its conflicts. From the earliest disputes of Cain and Abel to the military operations of the twenty-first century, humanity has never ceased to attack one another. Peacetime is simply a waiting period for the next battle; treaties and ceasefires are only delays in the violence.

The wars of the spiritual realm have been equally as long and as brutal as the physical wars. These battles have reached us from the earliest dawn of time, where they originated in the hearts of Adam and Eve. The struggle against temptation and rebellion is present in each of us, whether it is acknowledged or not. Few emerge victorious into a true peace, and even that peace is a watchful peace that can be shattered in a moment of wavering.

The following account is but a brief spark in this trying fire of strife.

The year was 1942, and all across the world there raged a war the likes of which had never been seen before. Destruction and carnage had become commonplace, none more so than in the Pacific theater. There, speckled amongst the vast blue expanse of the Pacific Ocean, its tropical islands hosted battles of unparalleled ferocity and savagery. Suicide charges, artillery annihilation, and arial bombardments made life for the common soldier a living nightmare. At any moment a banzai charge (a typically nocturnal all-out attack of massed infantry yelling at the top of their voices as they charged) might split the night air into a rush of charging enemies whipped into a killing frenzy. A wayward shell, some weighing as much as a small car, could fall from the sky with deadly results. Death was ever present, claiming lives seemingly at random.

Four thousand miles to the east, another battle was raging. This one was as deadly as the first, encompassing hundreds of young men in an all-out struggle for their spiritual survival. Instead of the physical fighting on the Oriental islands of the Far East, this battle would be fought in the hearts and minds of those involved in this battle. Instead of machine guns and grenades, they would be armed with the sharpest of two-edged swords (The Holy Scriptures), guided by a power (The Holy Spirit) greater than any naval fleet.

These young men were called to a term of service in the physical warfare that was raging. Two years earlier, the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 had been passed before the United States entered the war. This Act required all men between the ages of eighteen and forty-five to register for the draft. Those selected were expected to serve a one-year term. Once war was declared, this term would be extended until the end of the fighting.

To these young men, this draft and the current war prompted their memories of stories of a similar war and a similar draft, scarcely a generation prior, that had called away their fathers to the training camps of the United States military. There, the older generation had been subjected to all manner of malicious maltreatment. At that time, it was expected that all able-bodied young men would not only be willing, but also eager, to serve their country in battle against the enemy. This prevailing sentiment had brought about a general anger and animosity towards the conscientious objectors of the First World War. Pressure was applied to make them join in the drills and decorum of the armed forces, and penalties of various kinds could be and were enforced against those that refused. So severe were the punishments that many suffered physically, and several were killed by the treatment they received.

In like manner to their fathers, these young men were being called to serve their earthly country by bearing arms. Draftees were to report to their local recruiting office, where they would be organized and shipped to one of several training camps around the country. There they were to be molded into soldiers, prepared to kill their fellow man, and then sent overseas for that purpose. Yet their faith decreed otherwise.

Fortunately, they were not the only ones who remembered the First World War. In the two and a half decades since that war, both Mennonites and various concerned individuals had been at work, ensuring that if the need arose, there would be an option that could satisfy the government’s requirements of service while not going against the principles and convictions of conscientious objectors. Thus were born various organizations and programs that afforded an exemption to military duty. Conscientious objectors were placed in various service roles through these programs. They served in hospitals, built roads and irrigation canals, and provided labor for conservation efforts. In this way they could fulfill the law without breaking the Law (see Mark 12:17).

Despite the bureaucratic acceptance of the conscientious objectors’ (COs) convictions, and their subsequent alternate service, public feeling often still ran hot against, not only the nonresistant Mennonites and Amish, but against any conscientious objectors. Individuals who refused to fight could expect that not only would they personally be brought under pressure, but that their families and friends would also be scrutinized. Some of their families were shunned or looked down on, with the local community boycotting their businesses. In some cases, local law enforcement would turn a blind eye to the mistreatment of non-resistant people within their jurisdiction. In extreme instances, patriotic fervor would boil over, resulting in mob violence, property damage, and in a few rare instances, direct attacks against the perceived slackers.

Although most of Europe and its allies had been embroiled in this war since Hitler’s invasion of Poland in September of 1939, the United States did not join in the initial dispute. While the German army stormed through Europe, the early years of the war in the Pacific were dominated by Japan, who had already invaded China as early as 1937. The United States remained neutral during this time, motivated by a general feeling of isolationism. This would all change on the morning of December 7, 1941, as the Japanese Navy launched a surprise attack on the United States, attacking ships moored in Pearl Harbor, the home of the United States Pacific fleet. Retaliation was swift, and war was declared on Japan and its allies. Japan redoubled their offensive, sweeping over the island nations scattered across the Pacific. The Japanese commitment to the war was personal and intense. Honor, even in death, was esteemed higher than life. The emperor was worshiped as infallible, and Japanese soldiers hurled themselves into battle in his name, even in the face of overwhelming odds. Spurred by its fanaticism and an efficient, well-supplied attack force, Japan set its sights on the Philippines. There its army was met by a force vastly inferior to their own.

Meanwhile, at their various stations throughout the country, the COs were facing their own attack. They had been afforded the relief of not needing to fight a physical fight. With this exception came unforeseen opportunities for serving the suffering individuals under their care. Throughout their various ministries, they would encounter all manner of people. Each encounter was another opportunity to show a Christian’s peace and love in the midst of the on-going war, especially in the mental institutions and hospitals that employed some of the COs. The state of the mental hospitals at the time was deplorable. Patients were treated roughly, or simply neglected. Troublesome ones would be bound in strait jackets for weeks or forced to live in their own filth. Food and sanitation did not begin to meet the needs represented. Several of the young men brought attention to the situation of the mentally handicapped, through writing to newspapers or detailing their observations about the abuse to their contacts at home. These actions led to growing public awareness and concern about the treatment of the disabled, which would be the catalyst for change in the care of those unable to care for themselves.

Unfortunately, the opportunity to serve came at a cost. The COs were young and separated from their church and family. Ungodly influences abounded around them. Because they were separated from their churches and families, these influences weighed more heavily on the young men’s minds than they would have at home. The battle was still being waged, and now more than ever they had to lean on God as their strength, support, and defense.

In the Pacific, Japan moved in for an overpowering assault of the Philippines. The island nation had long been preparing its defenses, and now it would be tested by the impetus of the Japanese invaders. This defending army was a product of the training and leadership of General George A. MacArthur. MacArthur was somewhat of a prodigy of the United States military, emerging from his service in World War I as the youngest divisional commander in the Army. Since then, his time between the Wars had been spent largely in the Philippines, whose beaches and jungles he was now defending. In the months leading up to the invasion, he requested reinforcements, updated equipment, and sufficient materials to withstand an attack. Because the focus of the United States at the time was squarely focused on winning the war in Europe first, his requests were denied, and he was therefore out-manned and out-gunned. Nonetheless, MacArthur dug in and prepared to defend against the inevitable landings and subsequent inward crawl of the invaders. His troops suffered massive casualties in their slow retreat. Although defeat soon became apparent, the General refused to leave the island. Not until the time when the island was all but taken, was he finally persuaded to slip through enemy lines, evacuating to Batchelor Field, Australia. Here it was that he made a solemn promise to those he had left behind: “I shall return.”

The COs, now spread across numerous projects and fields of service, faced an equally diverse set of challenges. Instead of the steady guidance of their home congregations, they were now under the leadership of government appointed directors. Their camp schedules kept them at work, up to six days a week. Sundays were generally reserved for worship services. The influence of a world at war all around them had set in. Harry Litwiller, a Mennonite youth in Canada, was one of those who fell to the influences of the world. He was put into the army, where he quickly filed for CO status. While his request was being processed, he picked up gambling and drinking from other recruits. Word of his new habits soon made their way to his military superiors, and his request was denied. Churches prayed, wrote letters, and otherwise made efforts to support the young men in their trials. They could not know it, but their time of testing would soon be drawing to a close.

Finally, the year was 1945. The last months of the war had seen the conscription of young boys and old men into the German Army as Hitler made a last desperate stand, caught between the allied armies of the Eastern and Western fronts. Unable to continue, the Germans sued for peace. Now that the war was over in Europe, the tide of war shifted to the Pacific. America rallied, propelled by its greater industrial capacity and natural resources, causing the Japanese advance to grind to a halt—thus, the American counter-offensive began. Slowly, island-hopping across the ocean, General MacArthur drew ever closer to Japan.

MacArthur had not forgotten his promise to the Filipino people. In his four years of absence, battles had been fought over the smallest of atolls—coral islands just large enough for an airstrip and a garrison. Even as the Japanese were uprooted from these strongholds, they maintained a solid footing in the Philippines. The island nation had suffered through the years of the enemy occupation. It was home to prison camps— housing prisoners of war and those accused of aiding the allies.

Time was now running out for the Japanese. Spread thin—with troops, equipment, and resources dwindling—they fought a desperate defensive campaign. On October 24, 1944, an Allied force landed on the eastern coast of the island of Leyte. The battle for the Philippines would last for two months, but at its end MacArthur emerged victorious. Many months earlier he had overseen the island’s surrender, now he commanded its repossession. His promise was fulfilled.

The war dragged on. In Europe, it was over, but the Pacific was yet to be won. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who had led the nation through the war, sickened and died. His vice president, Harry S. Truman, was sworn into office. His first decision was one unlike anything he could have ever imagined. Should he expend hundreds of thousands of lives to take Japan by land, or make them a gruesome example of a newly developed atomic bomb being dropped from the relative safety of the air? Truman deliberated and made his choice.

The war ended in the blink of an eye. The devastation of a pair of atomic bombs shocked Japan into surrender. They sued for peace, and peace was given. Except for the formalities, the war was over. Over, but the temporary peace was bought with an astronomical price of human life. Millions would never return to their grieving families.

For the COs, it was a return to a new normal. They were returning to their families, their churches, and their homes. But the war had changed them. Months and years had been spent away from spiritual oversight. Many would settle into their communities, raising their families and living out their Christian faith. Yet there had been casualties, with some, like Harry Litwiller, having given up their faith. The battle had been fierce, and not all its contestants had been wearing the full biblical armor available to them.

Both MacArthur and the victorious COs persevered to the end. Each believed in their cause, MacArthur in the devastation and destruction of war, and the COs in the redemption and peace of a fully surrendered life. They parallel each other here only in the fact that they both fought. The crucial difference is in what they fought for, and how they fought for it.

Världens historia har präglats av dess konflikter. Från Kain och Abels tidigaste tvister till det tjugoförsta århundradets militära operationer, har mänskligheten aldrig upphört att anfalla varandra. Fredstid är helt enkelt en väntetid inför nästa strid; fördrag och eldupphör är endast uppskjutningar av våldet.

Kriget i den andliga världen har varit lika långt och brutalt som de fysiska krigen. Dessa strider når oss från tidens allra första gryning, där de härstammar i Adam och Evas hjärtan. Kampen mot frestelse och uppror finns i var och en av oss, vare sig den erkänns eller inte. Få går segrande fram till sann frid, och även den friden är en vaksam frid som kan krossas i ett ögonblick av vacklande.

Följande berättelse är blott en kort gnista i denna prövande eld av strid.

Året var 1942, och över hela världen rasade ett krig som aldrig förr hade skådats. Förstörelse och blodspillan hade blivit vardag, inget mer än i Stilla havets krigsöken. Där, strödda bland Stilla havets vidsträckta blå yta, hyste de tropiska öarna strider av oöverträffad vildhet och grymhet. Självmordsdåd, artilleriutplåning och luftbombardemang gjorde livet till en mardröm för den vanlige soldaten. När som helst kunde en banzai-attack (en vanligtvis nattlig alltigenom attack med massinfanteri som ropar för full hals när de stormar fram) dela nattluften i en ström av anfallande fiender upphetsade till en dödande frenesi. Ett vilselett granatskal, några vägande lika mycket som en liten bil, kunde falla från skyn med dödlig verkan. Döden var ständigt närvarande och krävde liv till synes slumpmässigt.

Fyratusen mil österut rasade en annan kamp. Denna var lika dödlig som den första och omfattade hundratals unga män i en alltigenom kamp för deras andliga överlevnad. Istället för det fysiska slaget på de orientaliska öarna i Fjärran östern, skulle denna kamp utkämpas i hjärtan och sinnen hos dem som var inblandade. Istället för maskingevär och granater skulle de vara beväpnade med det skarpaste av tveeggat svärd (Heliga Skrifterna), ledda av en makt (Helige Ande) större än någon flottstyrka.

Dessa unga män hade kallats till en tjänstperiod i det fysiska krig som rasade. Två år tidigare hade Selective Training and Service Act från 1940 antagits innan USA gick med i kriget. Denna lag krävde att alla män mellan arton och fyrtiofem år registrerade sig för värnplikt. De som valdes ut förväntades tjänstgöra under ett år. När krig utbröt skulle denna tjänstgöring bli förlängd till krigets slut.

För dessa unga män väckte värnplikten och det nuvarande kriget minnen av berättelser om ett liknande krig och en liknande värnplikt, knappt en generation tidigare, som kallat bort deras fäder till träningslägren i den amerikanska militären. Där hade den äldre generationen utsatts för alla former av illvilligt missförhållande. Vid den tiden förväntades det att alla fysiskt dugliga unga män inte bara skulle vara villiga, utan också ivriga att tjäna sitt land i striden mot fienden. Denna rådande känsla hade gett upphov till allmän ilska och fientlighet mot samvetsvägrare från första världskriget. Påtryckningar utövades för att få dem att delta i militärens övningar och uppförande, och olika slags straff kunde och blev utdömda mot dem som vägrade. Straffen var så hårda att många led fysiskt, och flera dog av den behandling de utsattes för.

Likaledes som sina fäder kallades dessa unga män att tjäna sitt jordiska land genom att bära vapen. Värnpliktiga skulle anmäla sig vid sitt lokala rekryteringskontor, där de skulle organiseras och skickas till ett av flera träningsläger runt om i landet. Där skulle de formas till soldater, beredas att döda sina medmänniskor och sedan skickas utomlands i det syftet. Deras tro föreskrev dock något annat.

Lyckligtvis var de inte de enda som mindes första världskriget. Under de två och ett halvt decennierna sedan det kriget hade både mennoniter och olika angelägna individer arbetat för att säkerställa att om behov uppstod skulle det finnas ett alternativ som kunde uppfylla statens krav på tjänstgöring utan att strida mot samvetsvägrarnas principer och övertygelser. Så föddes olika organisationer och program som gav undantag från militärtjänst. Samvetsvägrare placerades i olika serviceuppgifter genom dessa program. De tjänstgjorde på sjukhus, byggde vägar och bevattningskanaler och bidrog med arbetskraft till naturvårdsinsatser. På detta sätt kunde de uppfylla lagen utan att bryta lagen (se Mark 12:17).

Trots den byråkratiska acceptansen av samvetsvägrarnas övertygelser, och deras efterföljande alternativa tjänst, var allmänhetens känslor ofta fortfarande hetsiga mot inte bara de icke-våldsamma mennoniterna och amish, utan mot alla samvetsvägrare. Individer som vägrade att strida kunde räkna med att inte bara de själva utsattes för påtryckningar utan även deras familjer och vänner granskades. Några av deras familjer blev utstötta eller sågade ner i anseende, med lokalsamhället som bojkottade deras företag. I vissa fall vände lokal rättsväsende bort blicken för misshandeln av icke-våldsamma inom deras jurisdiktion. I extrema fall kokade patriotisk iver över och resulterade i upploppsvåld, egendomsskador och i några sällsynta fall direkta attacker mot de uppfattade slackrarna.

Fastän större delen av Europa och dess allierade varit indragna i detta krig sedan Hitlers invasion av Polen i september 1939, deltog inte USA i den inledande konflikten. Medan den tyska armén stormade genom Europa dominerade Japan de tidiga krigsåren i Stilla havet, efter att redan 1937 ha invaderat Kina. USA förblev under denna tid neutralt, drivet av en allmän isolationism. Allt detta förändrades den morgonen den 7 december 1941, när den japanska flottan inledde en överraskningsattack mot USA och anföll fartyg förtöjda i Pearl Harbor, hem för den amerikanska Stilla havsflottan. Hämnden var snabb, och krig förklarades mot Japan och dess allierade. Japan ökade sin offensiv och svepte över ö-nationerna spridda över Stilla havet. Det japanska engagemanget i kriget var personligt och intensivt. Ära, även i döden, värderades högre än liv. Kejsaren dyrkades som ofelbar, och japanska soldater kastade sig in i striden i hans namn, även inför överväldigande odds. Uppeldade av sin fanatism och en effektiv, välförsedd attackstyrka satte Japan sikte på Filippinerna. Där mötte deras armé en kraft som var långt underlägsen deras egen.

Samtidigt stod samvetsvägrarna vid sina olika stationer runt om i landet inför sin egen attack. De hade beviljats lättnad från att behöva delta i fysiskt stridande. Med detta undantag kom oförutsedda möjligheter att tjäna de lidande individer som fanns under deras vård. Genom sina olika tjänster mötte de alla slags människor. Varje möte var en ny möjlighet att visa en kristens frid och kärlek mitt i det pågående kriget, särskilt inom mentalsjukhusen och sjukhusen som anställde några av samvetsvägrarna. Tillståndet vid mentalsjukhusen vid den tiden var beklagligt. Patienter behandlades hårt eller helt enkelt försummades. Besvärliga patienter bands i tvångströjor i veckor eller tvingades leva i sin egen smuts. Mat och sanitet motsvarade inte behoven. Flera av de unga männen uppmärksammade situationen för de psykiskt handikappade genom att skriva till tidningar eller redogöra för sina iakttagelser om missbruk till kontakter hemma. Dessa handlingar ledde till ökad allmän uppmärksamhet och oro över behandlingen av funktionshindrade, vilket blev katalysatorn för förändring i vården av dem som inte kunde ta hand om sig själva.

Tyvärr kom möjligheten att tjäna också med en kostnad. Samvetsvägrarna var unga och skilda från sin kyrka och familj. Oredliga influenser frodades runt dem. Eftersom de var separerade från sina församlingar och familjer vägde dessa influenser tyngre på de unga männens sinnen än de skulle ha gjort i hemlandet. Striden pågick fortfarande, och nu mer än någonsin måste de luta sig mot Gud som sin styrka, stöd och försvar.

I Stilla havet gick Japan till en överväldigande attack mot Filippinerna. Ö-nationen hade länge förberett sitt försvar och skulle nu sättas på prov av de japanska angriparnas framfart. Den försvarande armén var ett resultat av general George A. MacArthurs utbildning och ledarskap. MacArthur var något av ett underbarn i den amerikanska militären och hade framstått efter sin insats i första världskriget som den yngsta divisionskommendören i armén. Sedan dess hade hans tid mellan krigen till stor del tillbringats på Filippinerna, vars stränder och djungler han nu försvarade. Under månaderna före invasionen hade han begärt förstärkningar, uppdaterad utrustning och tillräckliga material för att stå emot ett angrepp. Eftersom USA då var inriktat på att vinna kriget i Europa först, nekades hans begäranden, och han var därför underbemannad och underutrustad. Ändå grävde MacArthur in sig och förberedde sig för att försvara mot de oundvikliga landstigningarna och den efterföljande inbrytningen av angriparna. Hans trupper led enorma förluster i sin långsamma reträtt. Trots att nederlag snart blev uppenbart vägrade generalen lämna ön. Inte förrän ön nästan var tagen blev han slutligen övertalad att smita genom fiendens linjer och evakuera till Batchelor Field, Australien. Där avlade han ett högtidligt löfte till dem han lämnat kvar: "I shall return."

Samvetsvägrarna, nu utspridda över olika projekt och verksamhetsfält, ställdes inför en lika mångfasetterad uppsättning utmaningar. Istället för sina hemförsamlingars stadiga vägledning stod de nu under ledning av statligt utsedda direktörer. Deras lägerscheman höll dem i arbete upp till sex dagar i veckan. Söndagar reserverades i allmänhet för gudstjänster. Påverkan från en värld i krig omkring dem hade tagit fäste. Harry Litwiller, en mennonitisk ung i Kanada, var en av dem som föll för världens influenser. Han placerades i armén där han snabbt ansökte om status som samvetsvägrare. Medan hans begäran behandlades tog han upp spel och dryckenskap från andra rekryter. Ord om hans nya vanor nådde snart hans militära överordnade, och hans begäran nekades. Kyrkor bad, skrev brev och gjorde andra ansträngningar för att stötta de unga männen i deras prövningar. De kunde inte veta det, men deras prövningstid skulle snart vara på väg att ta slut.

Till sist var året 1945. Krigets sista månader hade sett värnplikt av unga pojkar och gamla män in i den tyska armén när Hitler gjorde sitt sista desperata stånd, fångad mellan de allierade arméerna på öst- och västfronten. Oförmögna att fortsätta stämde tyskarna i för fred. Nu när kriget var över i Europa skiftade krigets ebb till Stilla havet. Amerika samlade sig, drivet av sin större industriella kapacitet och naturresurser, vilket fick den japanska framryckningen att stanna av—så började den amerikanska motoffensiven. Sakta, genom ö-för-ö-förflyttning över havet, drog general MacArthur allt närmare Japan.

MacArthur hade inte glömt sitt löfte till det filippinska folket. Under sina fyra år borta hade strider förts om de minsta atoller—korallöar precis tillräckligt stora för en landningsbana och en garnison. Även när japanerna rycktes upp från dessa fästen behöll de ett fast grepp i Filippinerna. Ö-nationen hade lidit under åren av fiendens ockupation. Den var hemvist för fångläger—huserande krigsfångar och de som anklagades för att ha hjälpt allierade.

Tiden var nu knapp för japanerna. Utspridda med trupper, utrustning och resurser som minskade, förde de en desperat försvarskampanj. Den 24 oktober 1944 gick en allierad styrka i land på ön Leytes östra kust. Striden om Filippinerna skulle pågå i två månader, men i dess slut framträdde MacArthur som segrare. Många månader tidigare hade han översett öns kapitulation, nu kommenderade han dess återtagande. Hans löfte hade uppfyllts.

Kriget drog ut på tiden. I Europa var det över, men Stilla havet återstod att vinna. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, som lett nationen genom kriget, blev sjuk och dog. Hans vice president, Harry S. Truman, svors in i ämbetet. Hans första beslut var något han aldrig kunnat föreställa sig. Skulle han offra hundratusentals liv för att inta Japan till lands, eller göra dem till ett gruvligt exempel genom en nyutvecklad atombomb släppt från relativ luftsäkerhet? Truman överlade och fattade sitt val.

Kriget slutade i ett ögonblick. Förödelsen från ett par atombomber chockade Japan till kapitulation. De bad om fred, och fred gavs. Förutom formaliteterna var kriget över. Över, men den tillfälliga freden hade köpts till ett astronomiskt pris i mänskliga liv. Miljoner skulle aldrig återvända till sina sörjande familjer.

För samvetsvägrarna var det en återgång till en ny normalitet. De återvände till sina familjer, sina kyrkor och sina hem. Men kriget hade förändrat dem. Månader och år hade tillbringats borta från andlig tillsyn. Många skulle slå sig till ro i sina samhällen, uppfostra sina familjer och leva ut sin kristna tro. Ändå hade det funnits förluster, med några, som Harry Litwiller, som övergivit sin tro. Striden hade varit hård, och inte alla dess deltagare hade burit hela den bibliska rustning som stått till buds.

Både MacArthur och de segerrika samvetsvägrarna höll ut till slutet. Var och en trodde på sin sak, MacArthur i krigets förstörelse och förintelse, och samvetsvägrarna i försoningens och fridens fullständigt överlåtna liv. De liknar varandra här endast i det faktum att de båda kämpade. Den avgörande skillnaden ligger i vad de kämpade för och hur de kämpade för det.

I want to introduce this article on Spiritual Gifts by observing an interesting verse: Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men –Ephesians 4:8. Throughout history, when a king went to battle against a city and conquered it, he and his army returned home, to be greeted by their people with great fanfare. They would march through the city with all the spoils of war, after which the king would hand out gifts from the stuff that was taken in battle, giving it to his people.

Likewise, when Jesus was crucified, through His death and resurrection, He conquered the enemy. He took the power from death, hell, the grave and from Satan himself for those who repent and believe in Him. When He returned home (ascended up on high) He gave gifts to His people— the Church. Here in Ephesians, we have a condensed list of spiritual gifts: And he [God] gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers –Ephesians 4:11.

We observe more detailed descriptions of these gifts given to the Church in 1 Corinthians chapter 12 both at the beginning of the chapter and the end of the chapter and in Romans chapter 12 verses 6 to 8. In 1 Corinthians we see the following gifts given—the word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, tongues, discerning of tongues, helps, and governments. Then, in Romans, we have more gifts added to our list—ministry, exhortation, giving, ruling, and showing mercy.

If I did not miss any, there is a total of 19 gifts given to the church. What a wealth of gifts have been given to the church when Jesus ascended up on high! It would be good for us to do a thorough study on each one of these gifts so that we would be able to recognize them in our congregations. One thing that could be observed is that our Pentecostal friends have taken a select few of these gifts such as miracles, healing, and speaking in tongues, and have held them above the rest, making them a validation of whether a person is born again, baptized in the Holy Spirit, or if they are more spiritual than those lacking these gifts. Or we could consider how the evangelicals tend to do the same with the gift of evangelism, which has made inroads into many conservative Anabaptist churches. Finally, we might examine how some of us plain churches take only the gifts that have to do with Church government, leaving it only to those who are ordained to have gifts, while most all the rest of the gifts are left unrecognized.

This all leads me to ask the question, “Should we be lifting one or two gifts out above the rest and emphasizing them, or should all of the gifts be recognized equally?” The only time that I see one lifted above the rest is in Paul’s letter to the Corinthians in the last verse of Chapter 12, and the first verse in chapter 14, where he exhorts them to covet after the best gift which, with careful reading, we will notice is referring to prophesy. As we continue with our careful reading, we discover that prophecy should hold precedence over speaking in tongues since apparently the Corinthian understanding of speaking in tongues was being abused and misused and the Church might not have been edified by their behavior.

Spiritual Gifts Should Not Excuse Ungodly Behavior

A word of caution might be in order here. There is an emphasis by some, on “knowing what my spiritual gift is.” I think this can be good, but it should not be done to the fault of excusing myself for bad behavior because “I have this gift and not the other.” For example, the prophet might excuse himself for being harsh because his gift is that of a prophet; since he may not have the gift of mercy, people may be unnecessarily hurt. We will all probably have a primary gift or gifts. As much as we may try to be well-equipped with as many of the gifts as we can, some will still be more dominant than others.

I have asked numerous people which gift was primary in the life of our Lord Jesus and the short answer is that He was full of the Holy Ghost and without measure and had them all. True enough, but even so, since we all want to be like Jesus, maybe we should stop excusing ourselves to one limited gift and pursue to be as fully equipped as possible. I know, and you know, that in this flesh we will not master them all and yet we should be receptive to them all. Having said that, we must realize, we are meant to be interdependent; that is why Jesus handed out these gifts severally to each man and we will all have our primary gift or gifts. But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will –1 Corinthians 12:11. Nevertheless, let’s be careful that we do not excuse wrong behavior, or, on the other hand, negligence of doing good, because “Well, that is just not my gift”.

Spiritual Gifts Are Not The Christian’s Identity

A couple of cautions may also be in place when seeking to understand spiritual gifts. Our identity should not be the gift that we have but rather that our identity is in Christ. We are a child of the King; we are not primarily a prophet, a teacher, or an evangelist. However, in being a child of the King, we have been given a gift by Him, to do His work, with His power. Recognizing first and foremost who we are in Christ will keep us in a beautiful place of humility, but if our primary identity is “this gift that I have,” I suppose it would be hard not to fall into pride and thus we open ourselves up to many pitfalls and dangers.

Spiritual Gifts Are God-Given, Not To Be Sought After By Man

Could there be a caution given in how we seek this gift? What does it mean when the Scripture says that God gives gifts according to His choosing? For instance, God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? –Hebrews 2:4. Or, But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will –1 Corinthians 12:11.

Do you notice in both verses the WILL of God being very involved in the giving of gifts in the Church? Maybe our “seeking spiritual gifts” should be done alone in our closet, asking God to make me humble and endue me with whatever gift He wants me to have to make me a useful tool in the church body that I am a part of—“Not my will, but thine be done”. Maybe He has given me a gift that I am not recognizing or using, and what I actually need is to stir up that gift and not neglect it, but rather use it in the place I fill in the church. Could it be possible that, if I were to seek enough after another spiritual gift, I just might get myself a counterfeit?

Also, it would be good to mention very directly again that when there is a focused seeking after spiritual gifts usually there is some resulting negative problem. Sometimes a select few are lifted out and taught to be more spiritually important, such as speaking in tongues, miracles, and healing. Some will promote that there is little to no value in the teaching of spiritual gifts and that the only ones which are for our day are the ones pertaining to the ordained church leaders such as government, pastors, and teachers. While some people use their understanding of spiritual gifts to become individualistic and they see little value in being a part of a body. This is wrong, since a careful reading of these Scriptures show us that ALL the gifts are essential so that God will have the ability to make use of all the gifts by a collaboration of all the people. Could it be possible that where certain gifts are elevated above the rest, whether it is speaking in tongues, healings, and miracles; or if it is evangelism; or if it is those more suited for the ordained among us, that there could be an unrecognized element of pride in our midst? We are so prone to disillusionment that it would be good to check our hearts thoroughly when seeking after spiritual gifts.

Spiritual Gifts Are Not Included In The Biblical List of Qualifications For Church Leaders

Paul told Timothy, Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery –1 Timothy 4:14. Maybe rather than seeking out a gift, we need to stop neglecting the gift that has been given to us. Rather than seeking something new and exciting, we should stir up the gift we do have. It has happened that men in leadership have been removed from their post, because they do not have the gift for that which they were ordained. I would be very slow and very prayerful before removing an ordained brother from his office for that reason. Would it not be better to pray that God would increase that gift that had been given him by the laying on of hands? To quickly conclude that he does not have the gift may just be the easy way out.

We would never do that in a marriage. How often has it happened that a wife was more gifted in leadership than her husband? Disannulling the marriage is not an option, nor is it an option to add a third person to the marriage union to bring balance to the perceived lack of a proper balance of gifting. We have often seen that when prayer and the Holy Ghost was involved in a situation like this, God gave the husband what he lacked (1 Corinthians 12:24-25), and the wife learned to yield her gifting in a way that allowed her husband to be the godly head of the home.

God can also give the necessary gift to those in such a marriage and in such a ministry team if they find themselves lacking. For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked: That there should be no schism [division] in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another –1 Corinthians 12:24-25. Is there ever a time to remove one from an office because of the lack of gifting? Maybe so, but let’s be very cautious, slow, careful, and prayerful.

In the case of church difficulty that seems to be due to the lack of gifting among the ordained, we need to consider the following verses. Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom. But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth. This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace. –James 3:13-18. Very rare is the case of church trouble involving church leadership when there is not a major lack by one or more of the ordained to be fully living out of God’s will and wisdom as defined herein.

The biblical answer to solving church problems that involves church leaders is three-fold. (1a) The leaders in question must humble their hearts in repentance before God and His Word, before the rest of the ordained, and where necessary before the local church. (1b) If the situation has deteriorated too much, then the wisdom of outside overseers should be sought. (2) The leaders who may be lacking in a specific gift should seek God through fervent prayer, both personally and of the local church, and should seek God’s provision for enabling ability through …the laying on of the hands of the presbytery –1 Timothy 4:14. (3) Then AFTER stability is restored the local brotherhood is at a good place to seek God’s will together about ordaining another brother to assist.

God’s Goal for Spiritual Gifts

I would see two main reasons for the gifts of the Spirit to be given to the Church.

The first reason is for the benefit of the church. In Ephesians we read: and he gave… [various spiritual gifts to believers] [to some this gift and to others a different gift] … For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: –Ephesians 4:11-12. First Corinthians chapter 12 has a long dialogue on how the gifts are to be utilized so as to benefit the body of Christ (the local church) and in verse 25 in particular, that there should be no schisms in the body, but that the members should have the same care one for another.

There are those who are going about preaching the need to have spiritual gifts, encouraging specific gifts such as evangelism, healing, miracles, and tongues, and it can be seen in many cases that this focused teaching actually causes divisions rather than unity. The Bible says that the gifts were given to bring the Church together and if it is not doing that, we should consider whether it is the real thing or if it is a counterfeit. I realize divisions happen for many reasons, but if the gifts in the body are not bringing together but dividing, we had better seek God for answers on why, because the gifts were meant to bring unity, oneness, and edification.

The second reason is for the benefit of the unbeliever. Some of the gifts were given as a sign for the unbeliever. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe –1 Corinthians 14:22. We see that throughout the New Testament tongues, miracles and healings followed the gospel in places where it was being presented to those who had never heard it before. This was a way that God used to solidify and validate in the hearts and minds of the unbeliever that this gospel must be of God because of the supernatural manifestations. We see that tongues also followed the spreading of the gospel so that all could hear it in their own language as on the day of Pentecost.

I would consider these to be the two main reasons and are the primary purposes of the gifts. We would do well to evaluate our gifts in light of these two main reasons to be sure we have the real thing and are using them according to the purposes for which they were given.

It is interesting that of the 19 gifts we are considering, most of these will be best utilized in the local Church. Remember, God uses the church to reach the world. Some of the gifts given to the church are for reaching the world, for instance, the evangelist has a more unique calling to reach the world. Gifts like healings, miracles, and speaking in tongues are some of the gifts that are more prevalent on the frontier of the gospel. This is not to say that these gifts are never seen in the local church. My prayer is that if someone came into our services who cannot understand a word of English, and there is no one who can interpret the preaching of the Word into their language, then may God give us the gifts of tongues so that they might hear the gospel and be edified.

We have seen where there was sickness, and the elders of the church were called and there was anointing and prayer. At times God chose to miraculously heal. However, just because we (believers) have this wonderful gift of healing it does not necessarily mean that God wants all of us to be healed of every illness. The apostle Paul prayed three times to be healed from his recurring illness (2 Corinthians 12:7-12), yet God told him no. If he was not healed when he had healed many others, why would I think it needs to be different for me? So, it is with all the gifts that are given to the church; they are allowed by God to be exercised according to His will, not ours. It is absolutely essential for me and you to be a part of a local body so we will have the gifts of the Spirit working together through all the members, for the work of the church, in bringing unity, oneness, and edification, and for the ongoing work of the Church in calling men from a world of sin and calling them into His kingdom.

The Gift of Tongues

It is important to consider for a moment the spiritual gift of tongues and specifically the place it fills in the Kingdom of God. The Apostle Paul tells us they are given for a sign. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe –1 Corinthians 14:22.

It is not a sign to the believer that he really has the Holy Spirit, but it is a sign to the unbeliever that the gospel message is real. The classic example was on the day of Pentecost. We do not determine Peter’s credibility because he spoke in another language. We all would agree without any doubt, that Peter was born again, and that the many different languages were not for his approval but rather so that the ones hearing would know that this speaking in many different languages was supernatural. It would have taken a stubborn soul to scoff at the message being preached that day.

Recently, I was made aware of studies that have been done by recording the gibberish that comprises most of what is called tongues today. Interestingly, they found that English speakers used English syllables in repetition, and that Spanish speaking people used Spanish syllables, thus, they deducted that most of what is called tongues today is a counterfeit where the person, in their own language, repeats syllables of their native tongue in repetition. I believe that in many cases it is done innocently because of the vast amount of deception that follows the speaking in tongues.

What I understand as the real thing is the example of a lady in Canada, who only knew French and did not understand any English. This woman happened to come to a revival meeting where the revivalist was preaching in English with no French interpreter. She responded in repentance to the message and those who counseled with her asked her how she understood the message, which was in English. She responded that what she had heard was shared in the most beautiful French she had ever heard. Clearly a miracle took place so that she would hear the message of salvation and be able to respond to it. I am sure it was heartwarming to know how it was supernatural that she was able to hear it. I suspect there is a good possibility that at times, the one speaking in tongues may not even be aware of it. Surely, if God could confound the languages of those working on the tower of Babel, He can also cause the words of an English-speaking preacher to be converted into French words before entering the ears of a French-speaking hearer.

The reason we find in scripture for the gift of speaking in tongues, is twofold, and is for the unbeliever who comes among us. The first reason is so that he would hear the gospel message in his own language. The second reason is that when he hears it miraculously in his own language and the one speaking does not know his language, it is a sign for the unbeliever to cause him to acknowledge that the message he is hearing is of God, and by God.

In conclusion, we find that two of the main purposes of God giving gifts to the church, giving them severally as He wills, is for the unity and edification of the body of Christ, and for the unbeliever to hear and be persuaded of the gospel message. Let us seriously consider whether the spiritual gifts we have and those gifts that are evident in our churches are fulfilling the purpose for which they were given.

Jeg vil innlede denne artikkelen om åndelige gaver ved å legge merke til et interessant vers: Derfor sier han: Da han fór opp til høydene, førte han fangene med seg og gav gaver åt menneskene – Efeserne 4:8. Gjennom historien, når en konge dro i krig mot en by og erobret den, vendte han og hæren hans hjem og ble mottatt av folket med stor begeistring. De ville marsjere gjennom byen med alt krigsbyttet, hvoretter kongen delte ut gaver fra det som var tatt i kamp, og ga det til sitt folk.

På samme måte, da Jesus ble korsfestet, seiret han over fienden gjennom sin død og oppstandelse. Han tok makten fra døden, dødsriket, graven og fra Satan selv for dem som omvender seg og tror på ham. Da han vendte hjem (for opp til himmelen) gav han gaver til sitt folk—kirken. Her i Efeserne har vi en konsis liste over åndelige gaver: Og han [Gud] ga noen til å være apostler; noen til å være profeter; noen til å være evangelister; noen til å være hyrder og lærere – Efeserne 4:11.

Vi finner mer detaljerte beskrivelser av disse gavene gitt til kirken i 1. Korinterbrev kapittel 12 både i begynnelsen og slutten av kapitlet, og i Romerne kapittel 12 vers 6 til 8. I 1. Korinter ser vi følgende gaver gitt—visdommens ord, kunnskapens ord, tro, helbredelse, undergjerninger, tungetale, å skjelne ånder, hjelpearbeid og styreoder. Så, i Romerne, får vi flere gaver lagt til listen—tjeneste, formaning, gavmildhet, ledelse og barmhjertighet.

Hvis jeg ikke har oversett noen, er det totalt 19 gaver gitt til kirken. For en rikdom av gaver som er gitt til kirken når Jesus for opp til himmelen! Det ville være godt for oss å gjøre en grundig studie av hver av disse gavene slik at vi kunne kjenne dem igjen i våre menigheter. En ting som kan observeres er at våre pinsevennene har tatt et utvalg av disse gavene som mirakler, helbredelse og tungetale, og holdt dem fram over de andre, og gjort dem til en bekreftelse på om en person er født på ny, døpt i Den Hellige Ånd, eller om de er mer åndelige enn dem som mangler disse gavene. Eller vi kan legge merke til hvordan evangeliske ofte gjør det samme med gavene til evangelisme, noe som har fått innpass i mange konservative anabaptistiske kirker. Til slutt kan vi undersøke hvordan noen av oss i de enkelhetssamfunnene bare tar med gavene som har å gjøre med kirkelig styre, og overlater det til de ordinerte å ha gaver, mens nesten alle de øvrige gavene forblir uerkjente.

Alt dette får meg til å stille spørsmålet: «Bør vi løfte én eller to gaver fram over de andre og fremheve dem, eller bør alle gavene anerkjennes likt?» Den eneste gangen jeg ser at én blir løftet over de andre er i Paulus’ brev til korinterne i det siste verset i kapittel 12 og det første verset i kapittel 14, hvor han formaner dem til å begjære den beste gaven som, ved nøye lesning, viser seg å referere til profeti. Når vi fortsetter vår nøye lesning, oppdager vi at profeti bør ha forrang framfor tungetale siden korinthernes forståelse av tungetale tydeligvis ble misbrukt, og menigheten kanskje ikke ble bygget opp av deres oppførsel.

Åndelige gaver skal ikke unnskylde ugudelig oppførsel

En advarsel kan være på sin plass her. Noen legger vekt på «å vite hva min åndelige gave er.» Jeg tror dette kan være godt, men det bør ikke brukes som et påskudd for å unnskylde dårlig oppførsel med at «jeg har denne gaven og ikke den andre.» For eksempel kan profeten unnskylde seg for å være hard fordi hans gave er profeti; siden han kanskje ikke har barmhjertighetens gave, kan folk bli unødvendig såret. Vi vil alle sannsynligvis ha en primærgave eller primærgaver. Så mye som vi kanskje prøver å være velrustet med så mange gaver som mulig, vil noen fortsatt være mer dominerende enn andre.

Jeg har spurt mange mennesker hvilken gave som var primær i vår Herre Jesu liv, og kort sagt var han fylt av Den Hellige Ånd ute av mål og hadde dem alle. Riktig nok, men likevel, siden vi alle ønsker å ligne Jesus, bør vi kanskje slutte å unnskylde oss med en begrenset gave og i stedet strebe etter å være så fullt utrustet som mulig. Jeg vet, og du vet, at i dette kjødet vil vi ikke mestre dem alle, men vi bør være mottakelige for dem alle. Når det er sagt, må vi innse at vi er ment å være gjensidig avhengige; derfor delte Jesus disse gavene ut til hver enkelt, og vi vil alle ha vår primærgave eller våre primærgaver. Men alt dette blir virket av én og samme Ånd, som deler ut til hvert menneske særskilt etter sitt råd – 1. Korinter 12:11. Ikke desto mindre, la oss være forsiktige så vi ikke unnskylder feil oppførsel, eller på den annen side forsømmelse av å gjøre godt, med at «vel, det er ikke min gave».

Åndelige gaver er ikke kristenens identitet

Noen få flere forsiktighetsregler kan også være på sin plass når vi søker å forstå åndelige gaver. Vår identitet bør ikke være gaven vi har, men heller at vår identitet er i Kristus. Vi er et barn av Kongen; vi er ikke først og fremst en profet, en lærer eller en evangelist. Men som et barn av Kongen har vi fått en gave av ham for å gjøre hans arbeid med hans kraft. Å gjenkjenne først og fremst hvem vi er i Kristus vil holde oss i et vakkert sted av ydmykhet, men hvis vår primære identitet er «denne gaven jeg har», ville det være vanskelig å unngå å falle inn i stolthet, og dermed utsetter vi oss for mange fallgruver og farer.

Åndelige gaver er Guds gaver, ikke noe mennesket skal søke etter

Kan det gis en advarsel i hvordan vi søker denne gaven? Hva betyr det når Skriften sier at Gud gir gaver etter sitt eget råd? For eksempel, Som også vitnet dem med tegn og under og med forskjellige undergjerninger og nådegaver av Den Hellige Ånd etter sin vilje – Hebreerne 2:4. Eller, Men alt dette virker én og samme Ånd, som deler ut til hvert menneske særskilt som han vil – 1. Korinter 12:11.

Legg merke til i begge versene at Guds VILJE er sterkt involvert i å gi gaver i kirken. Kanskje vår «søken etter åndelige gaver» bør skje alene i vårt skap, og be Gud gjøre meg ydmyk og utruste meg med hvilken som helst gave han vil gi meg for å gjøre meg til et nyttig redskap i menighetskroppen jeg er en del av—«Ikke min vilje, men din skje.» Kanskje han har gitt meg en gave som jeg ikke kjenner igjen eller bruker, og det jeg egentlig trenger er å vekke den gaven til live og ikke forsømme den, men i stedet bruke den der jeg fyller en plass i kirken. Kunne det være mulig at hvis jeg søkte ivrig nok etter en annen åndelig gave, kunne jeg få meg en forfalskning?

Det er også godt å nevne veldig direkte igjen at når det er et fokusert søk etter åndelige gaver, følger det vanligvis noen negative problemer. Noen få blir løftet fram og lært opp til å være mer åndelig viktige, slik som tungetale, mirakler og helbredelse. Noen vil fremme at det er liten eller ingen verdi i å lære om åndelige gaver, og at de eneste gavene for vår tid er de som gjelder de ordinerte menighetslederne som styre, hyrder og lærere. Mens noen bruker sin forståelse av åndelige gaver til å bli individualistiske og ser liten verdi i å være en del av en kropp. Dette er galt, siden en nøye lesning av disse skriftene viser oss at ALLE gavene er nødvendige slik at Gud kan bruke alle gavene gjennom et samarbeid av alle menneskene. Kunne det være mulig at der visse gaver blir hevet over de andre—enten det er tungetale, helbredelser og mirakler; eller om det er evangelisme; eller om det er de som passer best for de ordinerte blant oss—at det kunne være et uerkjent element av stolthet blant oss? Vi er så tilbøyelige til misforståelser at det ville være godt å undersøke våre hjerter grundig når vi søker etter åndelige gaver.

Åndelige gaver er ikke med i den bibelske listen over kvalifikasjoner for kirkeledere

Paulus sa til Timoteus: Ikke neglisjer nådegaven som er i deg, som du fikk ved profetisk formaning da eldste la hendene på deg – 1. Timoteus 4:14. Kanskje i stedet for å søke etter en gave, trenger vi å slutte å neglisjere den gaven som er blitt gitt oss. I stedet for å søke noe nytt og spennende, bør vi oppmuntre til å vekke den gaven vi har. Det har hendt at menn i lederskap er blitt fjernet fra sitt embete, fordi de ikke har den gave som krevdes for det de var ordinerte til. Jeg ville være veldig langsom og meget bønnfylt før jeg fjernet en ordinerte bror fra hans embete av den grunn. Ville det ikke være bedre å be om at Gud ville øke den gaven som ble gitt ham ved håndspåleggelse? Å raskt konkludere at han ikke har gaven kan bare være den enkle utveien.

Vi ville aldri gjøre det i et ekteskap. Hvor ofte har det skjedd at en kone var mer utrustet i lederskap enn sin mann? Å annullere ekteskapet er ikke et alternativ, og det er heller ikke et alternativ å legge til en tredje person i ekteskapet for å bringe balanse i den antatte mangelen på riktig fordeling av gaver. Vi har ofte sett at når bønn og Den Hellige Ånd var innblandet i en slik situasjon, ga Gud mannen det han manglet (1. Korinter 12:24-25), og kvinnen lærte å underordne sin gavning på en måte som tillot mannen å være det gudfryktige hodet i hjemmet.

Gud kan også gi den nødvendige gaven til dem i et slikt ekteskap og i et slikt tjenesteteam hvis de finner at de mangler. For våre vakre deler trenger ikke det: men Gud har satt kroppen sammen og gitt stor ære til den del som var angrende; at det ikke skulle være skism [splittelse] i kroppen; men at lemmene skulle ha samme omsorg for hverandre – 1. Korinter 12:24-25. Er det noen gang riktig å fjerne en fra et embete på grunn av mangel på gave? Kanskje, men la oss være meget forsiktige, langsomme, omhyggelige og bønnfulle.

I tilfelle av kirkesvikt som synes å skyldes mangel på gaver blant de ordinerte, må vi vurdere følgende vers: Hvem er vis og har kunnskap blant dere? La ham vise ut av et sunt levevis sine gjerninger med ydmykhetens visdom. Men hvis dere har bitter misunnelse og strid i deres hjerter, så skryt ikke og tal ikke usant mot sannheten. Denne visdommen kommer ikke ovenfra, men er jordisk, sanselig, djevelsk. For hvor misunnelse og strid er, der er uorden og all slags ondskap. Men den visdom som er fra oven, er først ren, så freden skaper, mild, og lett å overtale, full av barmhjertighet og gode frukter, uten partiskhet og uten hykleri. Og rettferdighetens frukt blir sådd i fred av dem som gjør fred. – Jakob 3:13-18. Veldig sjelden er saken med kirkestrid som involverer kirkens ledelse når det ikke er en betydelig mangel hos en eller flere av de ordinerte i å leve full ut etter Guds vilje og visdom som definert her.

Det bibelske svaret for å løse kirkens problemer som involverer kirkeledere er tredelt. (1a) De berørte lederne må ydmyke sine hjerter i omvendelse for Gud og hans Ord, for de øvrige ordinerte, og der det er nødvendig for den lokale menigheten. (1b) Hvis situasjonen har forverret seg for mye, bør visdommen til utenforstående overtilsynsmenn søkes. (2) Lederne som kan mangle en bestemt gave, bør søke Gud gjennom ivrig bønn, både personlig og i den lokale menigheten, og bør søke Guds tilrettelegging for evne gjennom …håndspåleggelsen fra eldsterådet – 1. Timoteus 4:14. (3) Så ETTER at stabilitet er gjenopprettet er det et godt tidspunkt for den lokale brorskap å sammen søke Guds vilje om å ordinere en annen bror til å bistå.

Guds mål for de åndelige gavene

Jeg ser to hovedårsaker til at Åndens gaver er gitt til kirken.

Den første grunnen er til menighetens nytte. I Efeserne leser vi: og han gav… [forskjellige åndelige gaver til troende] [til noen denne gaven og til andre en annen gave] … til å gjøre de hellige fullkomnetjenestens gjerning, til bygning av Kristi kropp: – Efeserne 4:11-12. 1. Korinter kapittel 12 har en lang dialog om hvordan gavene skal brukes for å gagne Kristi kropp (den lokale menigheten) og i vers 25 spesielt at det ikke skal være splittelser i kroppen, men at lemmene skal ha samme omsorg for hverandre.

Det finnes de som går omkring og forkynner behovet for å ha åndelige gaver, og som oppmuntrer spesifikke gaver som evangelisme, helbredelse, mirakler og tungetale, og det kan sees i mange tilfeller at denne fokuserte undervisningen faktisk forårsaker splittelser framfor enhet. Bibelen sier at gavene ble gitt for å samle kirken, og hvis det ikke gjør det, bør vi vurdere om det er ekte eller en forfalskning. Jeg innser at splittelser skjer av mange grunner, men hvis gavene i kroppen ikke samler men deler, bør vi søke Gud om svar på hvorfor, fordi gavene var ment å gi enhet, enhet og oppbyggelse.

Den andre grunnen er til de ikke-troendes nytte. Noen av gavene ble gitt som tegn for den ikke-troende. Derfor er tungetale et tegn, ikke for dem som tror, men for dem som ikke tror; men profeti er ikke for dem som ikke tror, men for dem som tror – 1. Korinter 14:22. Vi ser gjennom Det nye testamente at tungetale, mirakler og helbredelser fulgte evangeliet der det ble framført for dem som aldri hadde hørt det før. Dette var en måte Gud brukte for å stadfeste og bekrefte i hjertene og sinnene til den ikke-troende at dette evangeliet måtte være fra Gud på grunn av de overnaturlige manifestasjonene. Vi ser at tungetale også fulgte spredningen av evangeliet slik at alle kunne høre det på sitt eget språk, som på pinsedagen.

Jeg vil betrakte disse som de to hovedgrunnene og de primære formålene med gavene. Vi ville gjøre klokt i å vurdere våre gaver i lys av disse to hovedgrunnene for å sikre at vi har det ekte og bruker dem i henhold til formålene de ble gitt for.

Det er interessant at av de 19 gavene vi vurderer, vil de fleste bli best brukt i den lokale kirke. Husk, Gud bruker kirken til å nå verden. Noen av gavene gitt til kirken er for å nå verden; for eksempel har evangelisten et mer særegent kall til å nå verden. Gaver som helbredelser, mirakler og tungetale er noen av gavene som er mer utbredt på forkant av evangeliets utbredelse. Dette betyr ikke at disse gavene aldri ses i den lokale menigheten. Min bønn er at om noen kom til våre samlinger som ikke kunne forstå et eneste ord engelsk, og det ikke var noen som kunne tolke forkynnelsen av Ordet til deres språk, da måtte Gud gi oss tungetalen slik at de kunne høre evangeliet og bli bygd opp.

Vi har sett at når sykdom var til stede, ble menighetens eldste kalt og det var salving og bønn. Til tider valgte Gud å helbrede mirakuløst. Men bare fordi vi (troende) har denne vidunderlige gaven til helbredelse, betyr det ikke nødvendigvis at Gud ønsker at vi alle skal bli helbredet for enhver sykdom. Apostelen Paulus ba tre ganger om å bli helbredet fra sin tilbakevendende lidelse (2. Korinter 12:7-12), likevel sa Gud nei. Hvis han ikke ble helbredet når han hadde helbredet mange andre, hvorfor skulle jeg tro det måtte være annerledes for meg? Så det er med alle gavene som er gitt til kirken; de får utfolde seg etter Guds vilje, ikke vår. Det er helt avgjørende for meg og deg å være en del av en lokal kropp slik at Åndens gaver kan virke sammen gjennom alle lemmene, for menighetens arbeid, i å bringe enhet, samsvar og oppbyggelse, og for kirkens fortsatte arbeid i å kalle mennesker fra en syndens verden og inn i hans rike.

Tungtalegaven

Det er viktig å betrakte et øyeblikk den åndelige gaven tungetale og spesielt hvilken plass den fyller i Guds rike. Apostelen Paulus sier oss at de er gitt som et tegn. Derfor er tungetale et tegn, ikke for dem som tror, men for dem som ikke tror; men profeti tjener ikke for dem som ikke tror, men for dem som tror – 1. Korinter 14:22.

Det er ikke et tegn for den troende at han virkelig har Den Hellige Ånd, men det er et tegn for den ikke-troende at evangeliebudskapet er ekte. Det klassiske eksemplet er på pinsedagen. Vi avgjør ikke Peters troverdighet fordi han talte på et annet språk. Vi ville alle være enige uten tvil om at Peter var født på ny, og at de mange forskjellige språkene ikke var for hans godkjennelse, men snarere for at de som hørte skulle vite at denne talen i mange språk var overnaturlig. Det ville krevd en sta sjel å spotte budskapet som ble forkynt den dagen.

Nylig ble jeg gjort oppmerksom på studier som er blitt gjort ved å ta opp det pludrende stoffet som det meste av det som kalles tungetale i dag består av. Interessant nok fant de at engelsktalende brukte engelske stavelser i repetisjon, og at spansktalende brukte spanske stavelser, og dermed konkluderte de med at det meste av det som kalles tungetale i dag er en forfalskning hvor personen, på sitt eget språk, gjentar stavelser av sitt morsmål i repetisjon. Jeg tror at i mange tilfeller gjøres dette uskyldig på grunn av den store mengde bedrag som følger tungetalen.

Det jeg forstår som det ekte, er eksempelet på en dame i Canada som bare kunne fransk og ikke forsto engelsk. Denne kvinnen kom tilfeldigvis til et vekkelsesmøte hvor vekkelsespredikanten forkynte på engelsk uten fransk tolk. Hun svarte i omvendelse på budskapet, og de som veiledet henne spurte hvordan hun hadde forstått budskapet som var på engelsk. Hun svarte at det hun hadde hørt ble delt i det vakreste franske hun noen gang hadde hørt. Klart skjedde det et mirakel slik at hun kunne høre frelsesbudskapet og svare på det. Jeg er sikker på at det var hjertelig å vite at det var overnaturlig at hun kunne høre det. Jeg mistenker at det er en god mulighet for at den som taler i tungene noen ganger ikke engang er klar over det. Sannelig, om Gud kunne forvirre språkene til dem som bygde Babels tårn, kan han også la ordene fra en engelsktalende predikant bli omsatt til franske ord før de entrer ørene til en fransktalende tilhører.

Grunnen vi finner i Skriften for gaven tungetale er todelt, og gjelder for den ikke-troende som kommer blant oss. Den første grunnen er at han skal høre evangeliebudskapet på sitt eget språk. Den andre grunnen er at når han hører det mirakuløst på sitt eget språk og den som taler ikke kjenner hans språk, er det et tegn for den ikke-troende som får ham til å erkjenne at budskapet han hører er fra Gud, og ved Gud.

Avslutningsvis finner vi at to av hovedformålene med at Gud gir gaver til kirken, ved å gi dem særskilt etter sin vilje, er for enhet og oppbyggelse av Kristi kropp, og for at den ikke-troende skal høre og bli overbevist om evangeliets budskap. La oss alvorlig vurdere om de åndelige gavene vi har og de gavene som er tydelige i våre kirker oppfyller formålet de ble gitt for.
