The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.

Das Jahr war etwa 60 n. Chr. Der Apostel Paulus war in Jerusalem von einem Mob wütender Juden ergriffen und beinahe im Tempel getötet worden.

Einige Tage später war er wegen einer Gefahr durch eine Gruppe jüdischer Verschwörer dem römischen Statthalter Felix übergeben worden. Felix hatte seinen Fall gehört, und obwohl es keine Beweise gab, um Paulus zu verurteilen, hatte Felix ihn die nächsten zwei Jahre im Gefängnis behalten, bis der neue Statthalter Festus sein Amt antrat.

König Herodes Agrippa II. kam zu Besuch zu Festus, und die beiden hörten Paulus sprechen. Während der Anhörung …legte er dar von Gerechtigkeit, von Enthaltsamkeit und vom Gericht, das kommen soll [bis schließlich] Felix erbebte und antwortete: Geh hin; zu passender Zeit will ich dich herbeirufen – Apostelgeschichte 24,25. Gegen Ende von Paulus’ Rede …sprach Festus mit lauter Stimme: Paulus, du bist verrückt; viele Gelehrsamkeit macht dich toll – Apostelgeschichte 26,24.

Festus meinte nicht wissenschaftliches Wissen, sondern die Tatsache, dass Paulus gelehrt war. Schlimmer noch: Paulus machte den Statthalter durch seine Rede über die sündhafte Lebensführung unbehaglich, und seine Argumentation machte deutlich, dass die einzige Lösung für Festus und Agrippa darin bestand, den Schriften der Hebräer zu folgen.

Paulus war gut gebildet. Er macht es in seinen Briefen und Predigten deutlich, indem er nicht nur aus der jüdischen Bibel zitiert, sondern auch aus einer Reihe griechischer und kretischer Philosophen und Dichter.

In moderneren Zeiten scheint Wissenschaft kein Freund des Glaubens zu sein. Viele Wissenschaftler behaupten, die Idee eines intelligenten Schöpfers des Universums sei lächerlich. Außerdem würden viele von ihnen sagen, dass diejenigen, die so etwas glauben, kaum noch über dem Niveau von Wilden stünden.

Das führt viele Christen gewiss dazu, der Wissenschaft ganz fernzubleiben. Sie sehen etwas, das ihrem grundlegenden christlichen Glauben so feindlich gegenübersteht, als nicht nützlich an.

Ich kann diesen Standpunkt verstehen, aber ich denke, wir sollten das Lernen nicht aufgeben, nur weil einige derjenigen, die sich für so kenntnisreich halten, in Wirklichkeit recht töricht sind.

Schöpfung

Wenn ich über das Thema Wissenschaft nachdenke, beginne ich oft beim Thema Schöpfung. Das ist der Anfang von allem und der erste Ort, an dem „Wissenschaft“ und die Bibel in Konflikt geraten.

Die Wissenschaft ist einfach nicht in der Lage zu akzeptieren, dass es einen Schöpfergott geben könnte, der alles, was wir sehen, in Bewegung gesetzt hat.

Es gibt viele Bücher, die sich mit dem Thema intelligentes Design und Gottes Fingerabdrücke in der Schöpfung beschäftigen. Es erfordert weit mehr Glauben zu glauben, das Universum sei durch Zufall entstanden, als an einen Schöpfer zu glauben.

Die Bibel macht deutlich, dass Gott nicht nur zur Zeit der Schöpfung gegenwärtig war, sondern dass Er sie auch begonnen hat (Johannes 1,1–3). Paulus sagt: Denn das Unsichtbare von ihm, sein ewiges Wesen und seine Gottheit, wird seit der Schöpfung der Welt an den Werken durch Nachdenken wahrgenommen – so dass sie ohne Entschuldigung sind – Römer 1,20.

Die Menschen sollten erkennen können, dass bei unserer Welt und dem Universum seit der Schöpfung ein Schöpfergott mitwirkt. Sie sollten auch einige andere Dinge über Ihn verstehen können. Vielleicht am wichtigsten für unsere Diskussion hier: Wir können durch Betrachtung der Schöpfung erkennen, dass Gott ein ordentlicher Gott ist und die Welt so geschaffen hat, dass sie mit einer bestimmten Struktur und geltenden Gesetzen funktioniert.

Das ist einer der großen Unterschiede zwischen dem Schöpfungsbericht in Genesis und den mythischen Schöpfungsgeschichten anderer Kulturen der Zeit. Die Bibel macht deutlich, dass Gott die Welt absichtlich schuf, dass Er sie in geordneter Weise schuf und dass Er dafür sorgte, dass jeder Teil mit allen anderen Teilen zusammenpasste. Es gibt keine Magie oder mystisches Denken im Genese-Bericht.

Die Gesetze des Universums gelten weiter

Es gibt viele Menschen, die glauben, sie könnten die Funktionsweise des Universums ändern, dass sie unmoralisch handeln und nicht die Folgen der Sünde tragen müssten, und dass sie töricht handeln können, ohne die Konsequenzen ihres Verhaltens zu erleiden.

Der Prophet Jeremia sagt uns, dass es Gesetze gibt, die in Kraft sind und nicht aufhören werden zu wirken. So spricht der HERR, der die Sonne gibt zum Licht am Tage und die Satzungen des Mondes und der Sterne zum Licht bei Nacht, der das Meer scheidet, wenn seine Wogen toben: Der HERR Zebaoth heißt sein Name. Wenn diese Satzungen vor mir weichen, spricht der HERR, so wird auch der Same Israel für immer und ewig aufhören, ein Volk vor mir zu sein – Jeremia 31,35–36.

Es gibt ein ganzes Set von Gesetzen, die regeln, wie die Erde sich um ihre Achse dreht und die Sonne umkreist. Alles, von der Lichtgeschwindigkeit bis zu der Art, wie die Schwerkraft Dinge zu großen Massen hinzieht, wurde zur Zeit der Schöpfung eingesetzt—…alle Dinge bleiben so, wie sie von Anbeginn der Schöpfung gewesen sind – 2. Petrus 3,4.

Da diese Gesetze fortbestehen und nicht schwanken, können wir sie wenigstens teilweise verstehen. Das ist es, was Wissenschaft ist—das Studium der natürlichen Welt, die wir sehen, und der Versuch zu begreifen, wie sie funktioniert. Gott hat unsere Welt so geschaffen, dass, wenn man ein Experiment immer auf dieselbe Weise durchführt, man jedes Mal die gleichen Ergebnisse erhält.

Die Wissenschaft wird niemals alles verstehen

Der Prophet Jesaja sagt: Denn meine Gedanken sind nicht eure Gedanken, und eure Wege sind nicht meine Wege, spricht der HERR. Denn wie der Himmel höher ist als die Erde, so sind auch meine Wege höher als eure Wege und meine Gedanken höher als eure Gedanken – Jesaja 55,8–9.

Sogar die klügsten Quantenphysiker geben zu, dass sie nicht alles verstehen. Tatsächlich ist die Zahl der Fragen, die sie haben, größer als der gesamte Wissensschatz, der sich angesammelt hat.

Die meisten von uns werden weit weniger Verständnis vom Universum haben als das. Wir werden nicht alle Details verstehen, wie das Atom funktioniert. Wir werden nicht die nötige Analysis beherrschen, um einen Satelliten in die Umlaufbahn zu bringen. Das ist in Ordnung. Wichtig ist, dass wir lernen, was wir können, um zu begreifen, was für einen erstaunlichen und ordentlichen Gott wir dienen.

Vorausannahmen sind ein Problem

Das größte Problem, das wir in der Wissenschaft sehen, ist nicht die Wissenschaft selbst, sondern die Vorurteile derjenigen, die die Wissenschaft betreiben. Der Narr sagt in seinem Herzen: Es ist kein Gott – Psalm 14,1. Nach dieser Definition sind viele Wissenschaftler Narren.

Ich sage das nicht leichtfertig. Atheisten betrachten das Universum und da sie glauben, dass es keinen Gott geben kann, müssen sie erklären, wie es ohne das Vorhandensein eines wirklichen Schöpfers existiert. Das ist das Herz der Torheit.

Wenn sie an Lücken in ihrem Wissen gelangen, schweigen sie, während der Christ sie in wenigen einfachen Worten erklären kann. Wie ich zuvor sagte: Wenn wir die Komplexität des Universums betrachten, von den kleinsten Dingen bis zu den größten Galaxien, können wir die Hand Gottes am Werk sehen.

Wenn ich deinen Himmel sehe, das Werk deiner Finger, den Mond und die Sterne, die du bereitet hast: Was ist der Mensch, dass du seiner gedenkst, und des Menschen Sohn, dass du dich seiner annimmst? – Psalm 8,3–4. Wenn wir über die Welt um uns nachdenken und lesen, was Wissenschaftler schreiben, ist es entscheidend, dass wir mit dem Wissen herangehen, dass Gott hinter all dem steht. Denn in ihm leben, weben und sind wir – Apostelgeschichte 17,28 und nichts, was die Wissenschaft erkennen kann, wird das ändern.

Die Wissenschaft sollte wie ein Detektiv sein, der Gottes Fingerabdrücke im Universum aufdeckt, nicht jemand, der darauf aus ist, Seine sehr reale Gegenwart zu diskreditieren.

Viele Wissenschaftler glauben an Gott

Ein Blick in die Vergangenheit zeigt, dass viele Wissenschaftler Männer waren, die an den Gott der Bibel glaubten. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nikolaus Kopernikus und viele andere glaubten an die Bibel und äußerten diesen Glauben offen gegenüber anderen.

Auch in moderneren Tagen gibt es viele Männer und Frauen der Wissenschaft, die an den Gott der Bibel glauben. Nur weil jemand in der Wissenschaft arbeitet, bedeutet das nicht, dass er kein Leben des Glaubens haben kann.

Viele Menschen haben wissenschaftliche Entdeckungen für Botschaften vereinnahmt, die dem christlichen Glauben und der Lehre widersprechen.

Wir müssen uns daran erinnern, dass es bei einem Satz von Fakten normalerweise verschiedene Erklärungen gibt, die ihr Vorhandensein erklären können. Schöpfung und Evolution betrachten dieselben Naturfakten, doch aus unterschiedlicher Perspektive oder Voreingenommenheit gelangen sie zu völlig verschiedenen Schlussfolgerungen. Vielleicht ist es ein wenig wie in einer Sherlock-Holmes-Geschichte, in der Dr. Watson routinemäßig die Fakten nimmt und eine ungenaue Erklärung dafür gibt, während der Detektiv dieselben Informationen nimmt und die richtige Erklärung liefert.

Wissenschaft und Medizin

Es steht nicht im Widerspruch zur Schrift, zu erforschen, wie Dinge in unserem Universum funktionieren, solange wir dies innerhalb eines biblischen Rahmens und mit dem Verständnis tun, dass es einen Schöpfergott gibt, der alles ordnet.

Die moderne Medizin ist eine Anwendung vieler verschiedener Gebiete, einschließlich Anatomie, Mikroanatomie, Genetik und Biochemie. Ziel ist es in diesem Fall, den menschlichen Körper bestmöglich zu beobachten und dann die Dinge zu beheben, die mit ihm schiefgehen. Ärzte können Wissenschaftler sein, aber die meisten von ihnen wenden einfach Wissen an, das ihnen durch ihre Ausbildung weitergegeben wurde.

Beobachtung ist der Anfang. Betrachten wir Diabetes als Beispiel. Aretaeus von Kappadokien im zweiten Jahrhundert n. Chr. war der erste, der eine vollständige Beschreibung des Diabetes gab und der Krankheit tatsächlich den Namen diabetes gab. Das Problem war, dass er zwar in der Lage war, Menschen mit dieser Krankheit zu diagnostizieren, aber keine Behandlung hatte, die seinen Patienten half. Die Beobachtung brachte ihn nur so weit.

Im Laufe der Zeit wurde weitergearbeitet, und es zeigte sich, dass das Problem in der Bauchspeicheldrüse lag und etwas Spezifisches mit den Inselzellen nicht stimmte. Selbst bis in die frühen 1900er Jahre gab es keine Heilung für Diabetes mellitus, und die einzige Lösung, die Ärzte anboten, war eine extrem kohlenhydratarme Diät mit strengen Kalorienbegrenzungen—man versuchte, Patienten bei 500 oder 600 Kalorien pro Tag zu halten. Wie man sich denken kann, war das keine ideale Behandlung.

Erst in den 1920er Jahren entdeckten einige Forscher in Kanada eine Methode, Insulin aus Hunden zu extrahieren, und verabreichten es einem 14-Jährigen, der an Diabetes zu sterben drohte. Das Extrakt rettete sein Leben und leitete eine neue Ära für Menschen mit Diabetes ein.

So funktioniert das: Wir beginnen mit der Beobachtung einer Krankheit und verschiedener Medikamente, die sich als wirksam erweisen, dann können wir im Laufe der Zeit und durch sorgfältige Tests beurteilen, welche Behandlungen am effektivsten sind.

Studien, in denen die Hälfte der Teilnehmer mit einer Krankheit ein Medikament oder eine Behandlung erhält und die andere Hälfte ein Placebo (eine Pille ohne medizinische Wirksamkeit), sind nach wie vor die effektivste Methode, um festzustellen, ob etwas wirklich wirkt.

Warum Behandlungen untersucht werden müssen

Es besteht die Tendenz zu glauben, dass die Dinge, die man gelehrt bekommen hat, wirksam sind. Wir wissen, dass George Washington an einer Lungenentzündung starb. Seine Ärzte verringerten wahrscheinlich seine Chancen auf Genesung, indem sie ihn viermal bluteten, insgesamt fast 40 Prozent seines Blutvolumens. Wahrscheinlich hätten sie ihn ein fünftes Mal geblutet, aber man hielt ihn nicht stark genug, um das Verfahren zu überleben.

Ärzte bluteten Patienten, weil sie glaubten, es gäbe toxische Ansammlungen im Blut, die man herauslassen müsse. Die meisten Menschen, die nach dem Aderlass starben, wären wahrscheinlich ohnehin gestorben, aber kranke Menschen zu bluten hilft ihnen sicher nicht bei der Genesung.

Vielleicht wollten die Ärzte einfach etwas tun. Patienten erwarteten Aderlass und so erfüllten die Ärzte diese Erwartungen, obwohl es den Patienten schadete.

Erfahrung ist das, was einen dieselben Fehler mit viel mehr Selbstvertrauen wiederholen lässt.

Was eine gute Studie ausmacht

Gute Studien haben viele Patienten, eine Kontrollgruppe (die entweder eine inaktive Pille, ein Placebo, oder die aktuell beste Behandlung für diese Krankheit erhält), und die Testgruppe erhält die neue Behandlung. Es ist auch wichtig, dass Kontroll- und Testgruppe möglichst eng übereinstimmen. Schließlich ist die Größe der Gruppen in der Studie entscheidend für die Schlussfolgerungen der Studie. Wenn nur zehn oder zwanzig Patienten in der Studie sind, ist das nicht groß genug, um wirklich herauszufinden, ob etwas wirkt oder nicht.

Bei vielen Krankheiten gibt es einen sogenannten Placeboeffekt. Dieser Placeboeffekt tritt ein, wenn Menschen sich von einer Krankheit erholen, obwohl sie nichts erhalten, das die Krankheit tatsächlich wirksam behandeln sollte. Interessanterweise bekommen in Studien viele Menschen Nebenwirkungen von den wirkstofffreien Pillen. Wenn 20 Prozent der Personen, die das Placebo erhalten, besser werden und 45 Prozent der Personen, die die Behandlung erhalten, besser werden, würde das darauf hindeuten, dass die Behandlung wirksam ist. Wenn der Unterschied minimal ist—sagen wir 20 Prozent der Placebogruppe und 23 Prozent der Behandlungsgruppe verbessern sich—dann ist die Behandlung nicht wirksam.

Probleme

Das größte Problem bei vielen Behandlungen ist, dass sie einfach nicht untersucht werden. Vitaminpräparate und Kräuterkombinationen mögen wirken, aber viele von ihnen wurden nie in einer Studie mit Kontrollgruppe geprüft. Die meisten Informationen sind anekdotisch. Die Tatsache, dass jemandes Großmutter oder Onkel von etwas profitiert hat, ist möglicherweise ein Hinweis auf Wirksamkeit, sagt aber nichts darüber aus, wie wirksam diese Behandlung ist oder welche Dosierung ideal ist.

Ein weiteres Problem ist, wenn Studien einfach nicht genügend Teilnehmer haben, um wirklich genaue Informationen zu liefern. Viele Studien umfassen nur zehn oder zwanzig Patienten. Das reicht einfach nicht aus, um zu identifizieren, wie gut eine Behandlung wirkt oder welche Nebenwirkungen zu erwarten sind. Damit ein Medikament von der FDA zugelassen wird, wird es typischerweise an zwischen 1.000 und 3.000 Patienten mit der betreffenden Krankheit getestet.

Ein letztes Problem bei Studien ist, wenn sie zeigen, dass ein Medikament wirksam ist, der Effekt aber klinisch nicht signifikant ist. Als Beispiel wurde vor Kurzem ein neues injizierbares Medikament gegen Demenz (Aducanumab) von der FDA zugelassen. Es ist sehr teuer, und der Nutzen schien gering zu sein. Patienten, die es erhielten, beantworteten im Durchschnitt nach 18 Monaten 1,5 mehr Fragen richtig in einem 85‑Fragen-Test zum mentalen Status im Vergleich zur Kontrollgruppe.

Man kann berechtigterweise hinterfragen, ob der durch dieses Medikament gezeigte Nutzen die Kosten von 50.000 Dollar pro Jahr wert ist. Vielmehr: Wie viel bedeutsame Verbesserung der Alltagsaktivitäten einer Person würde sich durch die Anwendung eines solchen Medikaments ergeben? Es erscheint unwahrscheinlich, dass es sehr viel Unterschied machen würde.

Es ist bedauerlich, aber Pharmafirmen werden immer versuchen, ihr Medikament als das beste darzustellen, selbst wenn die Studien keinen signifikanten Nutzen gegenüber bestehenden, billigeren Optionen zeigen.

Schlussfolgerung

Christen stehen einer Welt gegenüber, die sie und ihren Glauben nicht liebt. Viele würden versuchen, Wissenschaft zu benutzen, um sie dazu zu bringen, ihren Glauben aufzugeben. Ich hoffe, das führt uns nicht dazu, die wissenschaftliche Methode aufzugeben oder den Versuch aufzugeben, die Gesetze hinter dem Universum zu verstehen, das Gott geschaffen hat.

Die wissenschaftliche Methode ist gültig, auch wenn viele derjenigen, die sie anwenden, Atheisten oder Agnostiker sind. Wenn eine Behandlung wirkt, sollte sie beobachtbar, testbar und reproduzierbar sein.

Schon bei ihrer Anwendung haben wir ein grundlegendes Verständnis des Universums, das Atheisten nicht haben. Zu wissen, dass es einen Schöpfergott gibt, der uns liebt, macht einen großen Unterschied, wenn wir die Ergebnisse all der verschiedenen Beobachtungen interpretieren, die auf dem Gebiet der Medizin und anderswo gemacht werden.

Diejenigen, die Gott nicht kennen, sind dazu bestimmt, immer zu lernen und niemals zur Erkenntnis der Wahrheit zu kommen – 2. Timotheus 3,7. Andererseits können wir, wenn wir mit einem biblischen Verständnis beginnen, die Wissenschaft als Werkzeug benutzen, um die Schöpfung zu verstehen, die Er um uns gelegt hat.

I grew up in the same church setting in which my parents were born and raised. However, by the time I was 10, my parents began to be concerned with the direction the young folks were going and wanted something different for their children. So, my parents got in touch with a church from another state, which helped them make connections with a small church that was located close to where we lived.

I was more of a quiet, strong-willed child and was quickly turning into a rebellious teenager. My parents did all they knew to do with me at the time. One of which was making the move to this new church since it had more of a godly youth environment. I had a hard time with this change. At our old church, I had friends that were on the same page as me and supported me in my rebellious ways, but at the new church I was more of the “bad guy” and didn’t fit in with the other young people.

Over the course of time that church dissolved, and my parents decided to move to another state, closer to a more stable church. So it was, that, when I was 14, we spent our first night in a different state, in a different house, on a different road, and with different neighbors. We went shopping in a different town and went to a different church, with people that I barely knew. I didn’t like change. I found it challenging to meet new people and make new friends. I struggled majorly with all these changes, so, I never bothered trying to plug in and be an active part in our new life. Instead, I slowly built walls around my life and heart, all the while growing colder and more rebellious.

As I grew older and harder, my parents tried to work with me, but I would have nothing to do with it. I eventually got a job and was introduced to country music and other worldly things. Since I enjoy work, I poured myself into it and worked long hours. That way I wouldn’t need to be around the family or church people, and I wouldn’t need to go to church activities. Thus, I became more removed and isolated from those around me.

The church people didn’t know how to relate to me; most of them just left me to myself. Deep down I was desperately longing for love and acceptance from my family and church. This caused me to spiral downward. I continued to stuff my feelings and build a wall around myself, all the while hardening my heart further. As time went on, I withdrew more and more from my family and the church. I felt more and more like a social misfit that no one knew what to do with. I decided I was going to run away and live my own life.

Somehow my parents got wind of this idea and tried to do all that they knew to do to help me, but I resented it. Looking back, I know without a doubt that they were doing it out of love and care, but there was a great lack in our relationship. Thus, I continued to grow harder and colder.

The summer I was 17, a visiting minister (‘Mike’) and his family came to our church for meetings. I knew them from years before and somehow through our interaction during the meetings my heart started to soften and open. I’m not quite sure why, but for some reason, I decided that I wanted to go spend the winter with them. So, my parents got in contact with them, and it was decided that I could stay with them for a few months.

My plan was to spend a few months away from everything and then I would return home when I was almost 18. Once I was 18, I was planning to leave home and do my own thing. I was certain no one could stop me because I would be of legal age. However, God obviously had different plans...

Somehow ‘Mike’ convinced me to go to along to a week of meetings in another state. While we were there, I don’t remember that the conviction was any stronger than any other time. However, one evening after the service he asked me if I wanted to become a Christian and have my sins forgiven. I don’t remember what I told him, but we talked for a while. He took me through the Bible, helping me to see what God says about it all; then we prayed. When we got up from praying, I can’t say that something major happened, but it was definitely the night that I found salvation! That night, something changed in my heart. I knew that I now wanted to do things God’s way. I knew that my end goal in life was to run the race well and to finish victoriously. That is what has helped me through the years.

On July 31, 2011, I was baptized upon the confession of my faith. The next number of years were definitely not easy. I would even say that at times it seemed to have been harder than in the years before my conversion. Out of respect to others, I don’t feel I can share everything that has happened over the years, but I will try to share several main points. You can imagine that with the walls I had built around myself and the comfort I had found in this, that the years following my conversion were full of ups and downs as I tried to relearn how to relate to other believers and to people in general.

Even though I had reached out to God for forgiveness of my sins and had committed my life to following Him, I had many old habits of relating to others in wrong ways that still needed to be sanctified. Things at home continued to improve but there was still room for progress, which added to the stress. As the years went by, my stress level continued to rise. I didn’t know what to do with it, so I resorted to taking high doses of NoDoz® with an energy drink before I went to bed, trying to get my nerves to relax enough so I could sleep (don’t try this at home, it is dangerous). The next day I would get up and face it all again. One year for most of the year I struggled with thoughts of not wanting to continue on with life. During this time, I had a very close friend who gave me much encouragement. I believe that the regular contact I had with this close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness all working together kept me from doing something that I would have later regretted.

I had another close friend who had also gone through a lot but seemed to be finding God’s answers to life’s struggles. We would go out for supper, spending time together talking about life’s struggles. I remember times that I would leave his car and tears would be streaming down his face because he wasn’t sure if I was going to make it. Then he went to the mission field for two years to teach English.

I’m not sure what all was going on in his life but one day we got word that he was missing. Eventually we heard from him; he was okay and was living back in the states again. My heart was torn… One of the few friends that I had, had now turned his back on what he had once believed and on that which he had once tried to convince me of. Yet here I was, still struggling… Why not just give up fighting…? Why not just go live the easy life…? As time went on, I continued to long for love and acceptance. At times the struggle, the aching, and the longing seemed almost unbearable. But I knew deep down that giving up was not what I wanted. It would not get the end result that I wanted. Once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on.

Another young man started taking an interest in my life and we eventually became close friends. He and his wife were a great encouragement to me. Then due to some disagreements with the church, they became dissatisfied and left the church. They threw aside a lot of what they had once stood for. So here I was once again with a close friend that had turned his back on what he had once stood for. What’s the use? Why does life need to be so hard? Maybe I should also give up… But I didn’t want to totally throw God out. Maybe I could find a church that was less strict. Once again, I came to my senses and realized that’s not really what I wanted. That direction wouldn’t take me where I wanted to go. So once more through the encouragement and regular contact with my close friend, the prayers of others, and God’s faithfulness, I continued to press on. At the time it was tough, but looking back, I see I have learned a lot by all I have gone through.

In the fall of 2015, I went to Washington state due to a work opportunity. At the time I went, there were things going on at my home church that I was struggling with. Because of all the stress that I was facing, I was feeling quite discouraged about Church life, Christianity, and life in general. I wasn’t wanting to throw my Christianity away, but I was wondering, “Is this really what it’s all about?” “Why can’t people just get along?” Is this really what God had in mind for His people? If we are “little Christs” like we claim to be, shouldn’t we be able to get along? Shouldn’t we be the ones that are joyful and full of life?

I went to Washington with these kinds of thoughts on my mind. While there, I attended a church that was both Biblical and spiritually minded. It’s hard to explain all that went on in my mind, heart, and life during those six months. But I left there and went back home with a renewed strength and vision.

We should be the light of the world! We should have something to offer others! We should be able to get along with one another! Yes, we do go through hard times individually and collectively as a church, but if we fight the good fight of faith, if we finish our course, if we keep the faith, there is laid up for each of us a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only but unto all them also that love his appearing. I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing –2 Timothy 4:7-8.

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

June 15, 2018, at 4:40 pm. the scream of the emergency services’ pager split the peaceful afternoon as it crackled to life. “One-car rollover on ‘Gingko Avenue’, possible entrapment,” was the repeated dispatch. As we walked onto the scene, there sat a young girl who appeared to be in her mid-twenties and was visibly banged up. With blood and tears streaming down her face, she repeated these phrases, “I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die… I may never see my baby again.” As seconds turned to minutes, the paramedics tried to calm her anxious nerves. We searched the mangled car and surrounding area for the supposed missing baby. All the while she sat there with lines of worry and fear. She had tears and blood streaming down her face, as she repeated, “I may never see my baby again… I don’t want to die… I’m not ready to die.”

As first responders, all we found was a car seat that wasn’t fastened in, with no evidence of a baby anywhere. As the ambulance crew strapped her to the stretcher and loaded her in the ambulance, she was still repeating, “Where’s my baby…? I’m not ready to die… I don’t want to die… I may never see my baby again.”

As I left the scene that evening, with that image and those phrases running through my mind, I was struck with two sober thoughts. If that was me, miraculously surviving an accident and sitting there beside my vehicle, barely coherent, with blood streaming down my face, what would I be saying? What would the paramedics and rescue team remember me by? Would I be ready to die? Would I be clear before God?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

As Christians, when is the last time we helped someone prepare their soul for death? As believers who have been redeemed from the misery and chaos of a life of sin (see 1 Corinthians 6:9-11), we should …be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh [us] you a reason of the hope that is in [us] you with meekness and fear: –1 Peter 3:15.

In the fall of 2018, God opened the door for me to move to a church in a different state where I have found stability. It was here that God brought a godly young lady into my life, and we were married on November 30, 2019. Being married and having brothers who surrounded me with discipleship, compassion, and prayerful support helped me to grow in the Lord in many ways.

Being here has awakened within me a renewed vision to be the light of the world. Today, I am thankful that God did not let me go. As I kept fighting the spiritual fight, God kept giving me the strength and wisdom to do the next right thing. With each victory, my strength has grown stronger. Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you… –James 4:8. I thank God for giving me victory and for helping me find my ultimate source of love, security, and purpose—my Lord and Saviour, Jesus Christ.

Ik ben opgegroeid in dezelfde kerkomgeving waarin mijn ouders geboren en opgevoed waren. Tegen de tijd dat ik echter 10 was, begonnen mijn ouders zich zorgen te maken over de richting waarin de jongeren gingen en wilden ze iets anders voor hun kinderen. Zo namen mijn ouders contact op met een kerk uit een andere staat, die hen hielp verbinding te maken met een kleine kerk dicht bij waar wij woonden.

Ik was meer een stil, eigenzinnig kind en veranderde snel in een rebelse tiener. Mijn ouders deden alles wat ze op dat moment konden bedenken. Eén daarvan was de verhuizing naar deze nieuwe kerk, omdat die een godvruchtigere jeugdomgeving had. Ik had het moeilijk met die verandering. In onze oude kerk had ik vrienden die op dezelfde golflengte zaten als ik en mij steunden in mijn opstandige manieren, maar in de nieuwe kerk was ik meer de “slechterik” en paste ik niet bij de andere jongeren.

Naarmate de tijd verstreek, viel die kerk uiteen en besloten mijn ouders naar een andere staat te verhuizen, dichter bij een stabielere kerk. Zo was het dat we, toen ik 14 was, onze eerste nacht doorbrachten in een andere staat, in een ander huis, aan een andere weg en met andere buren. We gingen winkelen in een andere stad en gingen naar een andere kerk, met mensen die ik nauwelijks kende. Ik hield niet van verandering. Ik vond het moeilijk om nieuwe mensen te ontmoeten en nieuwe vrienden te maken. Ik worstelde er enorm mee, dus deed ik geen moeite om me te verbinden en een actief deel van ons nieuwe leven te worden. In plaats daarvan bouwde ik langzaam muren om mijn leven en hart, terwijl ik steeds kouder en rebelerender werd.

Toen ik ouder en harder werd, probeerden mijn ouders met mij te werken, maar ik wilde er niets van weten. Uiteindelijk kreeg ik een baan en maakte ik kennis met countrymuziek en andere wereldse zaken. Omdat ik van werk hield, stortte ik me erop en werkte lange uren. Zo hoefde ik niet bij het gezin of de kerkmensen te zijn, en hoefde ik niet naar kerkactiviteiten te gaan. Daardoor raakte ik meer verwijderd en geïsoleerd van de mensen om me heen.

De kerkmensen wisten niet hoe ze met mij moesten omgaan; de meesten lieten me gewoon met rust. Diep vanbinnen verlangde ik wanhopig naar liefde en aanvaarding van mijn familie en kerk. Dit deed me verder afglijden. Ik bleef mijn gevoelens wegstoppen en bouwde een muur om mezelf, terwijl mijn hart steeds harder werd. Naarmate de tijd verstreek, trok ik me steeds meer terug van mijn familie en de kerk. Ik voelde me steeds meer een sociale buitenstaander waar niemand raad mee wist. Ik besloot dat ik zou weglopen en mijn eigen leven zou gaan leiden.

Op de een of andere manier kregen mijn ouders lucht van dat idee en deden ze alles wat ze konden om me te helpen, maar ik hield er wrok jegens. Terugkijkend weet ik zonder twijfel dat ze het deden uit liefde en zorg, maar er was een groot tekort in onze relatie. Zo bleef ik harder en kouwelijker worden.

De zomer dat ik 17 was, kwam een bezoekende prediker (‘Mike’) met zijn gezin voor bijeenkomsten naar onze kerk. Ik kende hen van jaren eerder en op de een of andere manier begon mijn hart tijdens onze omgang in die bijeenkomsten zacht te worden en zich te openen. Ik weet niet precies waarom, maar om de één of andere reden besloot ik dat ik de winter bij hen wilde doorbrengen. Dus namen mijn ouders contact met hen op en werd besloten dat ik een paar maanden bij hen kon verblijven.

Mijn plan was een paar maanden van alles weg te zijn en dan terug naar huis te gaan als ik bijna 18 was. Zodra ik 18 was, was ik van plan het huis te verlaten en mijn eigen gang te gaan. Ik was ervan overtuigd dat niemand me kon tegenhouden omdat ik dan meerderjarig zou zijn. God had echter duidelijk andere plannen...

Op de een of andere manier overtuigde ‘Mike’ me om mee te gaan naar een week van bijeenkomsten in een andere staat. Terwijl we daar waren, herinner ik me niet dat de overtuiging sterker was dan andere keren. Toch vroeg hij me na een dienst op een avond of ik christen wilde worden en mijn zonden wilde laten vergeven. Ik weet niet precies wat ik hem antwoordde, maar we praatten een tijdje. Hij leidde me door de Bijbel en hielp me te zien wat God hierover zegt; daarna baden we. Toen we opstonden van het gebed kan ik niet zeggen dat er iets ongelofelijks gebeurde, maar het was zeker de nacht waarop ik redding vond! Die nacht veranderde er iets in mijn hart. Ik wist dat ik voortaan dingen op Gods manier wilde doen. Ik wist dat mijn uiteindelijke doel in het leven was om de race goed te lopen en zegevierend te eindigen. Dat is wat me door de jaren heeft geholpen.

Op 31 juli 2011 werd ik gedoopt op belijdenis van mijn geloof. De daaropvolgende jaren waren beslist niet gemakkelijk. Ik zou zelfs zeggen dat het soms zwaarder leek te zijn dan de jaren vóór mijn bekering. Uit respect voor anderen voel ik dat ik niet alles kan delen wat er door de jaren is gebeurd, maar ik zal proberen enkele hoofdpunten te noemen. Je kunt je voorstellen dat met de muren die ik om mezelf had gebouwd en het gemak dat ik daarin had gevonden, de jaren na mijn bekering vol ups en downs waren terwijl ik opnieuw moest leren omgaan met andere gelovigen en mensen in het algemeen.

Hoewel ik tot God was gekeerd om vergeving voor mijn zonden en mijn leven aan Hem had toegewijd, had ik vele oude gewoonten in de omgang met anderen die nog geheiligd moesten worden. Thuis verbeterden de zaken wel, maar er was nog ruimte voor vooruitgang, wat extra stress gaf. Naarmate de jaren verstreken, bleef mijn stressniveau toenemen. Ik wist niet wat ik ermee aan moest, dus nam ik hoge doses NoDoz® met een energiedrank voordat ik naar bed ging, in de poging mijn zenuwen genoeg te laten ontspannen om te kunnen slapen (doe dit niet thuis, het is gevaarlijk). De volgende dag stond ik weer op en ging ik opnieuw de strijd aan. Eén jaar heb ik het grootste deel van het jaar geworsteld met gedachten dat ik niet meer verder wilde leven. In die tijd had ik een zeer close vriend die mij veel aanmoediging gaf. Ik geloof dat het regelmatige contact met die vriend, de gebeden van anderen en Gods trouw samenwerkend mij ervan weerhielden iets te doen waar ik later spijt van zou hebben.

Ik had nog een goede vriend die ook veel had doorgemaakt maar die de antwoorden van God op levensproblemen leek te vinden. We gingen uit eten en brachten tijd met elkaar door om over levensproblemen te praten. Ik herinner me momenten dat ik zijn auto verliet en tranen over zijn gezicht stroomden omdat hij niet zeker wist of ik het zou redden. Daarna ging hij voor twee jaar naar het zendingsveld om Engels te onderwijzen.

Ik weet niet precies wat er allemaal in zijn leven speelde, maar op een dag kregen we bericht dat hij vermist was. Uiteindelijk hoorden we van hem; hij had het overleefd en woonde weer in de Verenigde Staten. Mijn hart was verscheurd… Eén van de weinige vrienden die ik had, had nu zijn rug gekeerd naar wat hij eens geloofd had en naar waar hij ooit had geprobeerd mij van te overtuigen. En hier was ik nog steeds aan het worstelen… Waarom niet gewoon opgeven…? Waarom niet het gemakkelijke leven gaan leiden…? Naarmate de tijd verstreek, bleef ik verlangen naar liefde en acceptatie. Soms leken de strijd, het pijnlijke gemis en het verlangen bijna ondraaglijk. Maar diep vanbinnen wist ik dat opgeven niet was wat ik wilde. Het zou me niet het uiteindelijke resultaat geven dat ik zocht. Nogmaals, door de aanmoediging en het regelmatige contact met mijn goede vriend, de gebeden van anderen en Gods trouw, bleef ik doorgaan.

Een andere jongeman begon interesse in mijn leven te tonen en we werden uiteindelijk goede vrienden. Hij en zijn vrouw waren voor mij een grote bemoediging. Toen, door enkele meningsverschillen met de kerk, raakten zij ontevreden en verlieten de kerk. Ze wierpen veel van wat ze ooit hadden gehad overboord. Zo stond ik weer met een goede vriend die zijn rug keerde naar waar hij ooit voor had gestaan. Waar heeft het voor nodig? Waarom moet het leven zo zwaar zijn? Misschien moest ik ook maar opgeven… Maar ik wilde God niet helemaal weggooien. Misschien kon ik een kerk vinden die minder strikt was. Opnieuw kwam ik tot bezinning en realiseerde ik me dat dat niet echt was wat ik wilde. Die richting zou me niet brengen waar ik naartoe wilde. Dus wederom, door de aanmoediging en het regelmatige contact met mijn goede vriend, de gebeden van anderen en Gods trouw, bleef ik doorgaan. Destijds was het zwaar, maar als ik terugkijk zie ik dat ik veel geleerd heb van alles wat ik heb doorgemaakt.

In de herfst van 2015 ging ik naar de staat Washington vanwege een werkgelegenheid. Toen ik ging, speelden er dingen in mijn thuisgemeente waar ik moeite mee had. Vanwege alle stress waarmee ik te maken had, voelde ik me behoorlijk ontmoedigd over het kerkelijk leven, het christendom en het leven in het algemeen. Ik wilde mijn christendom niet weggooien, maar ik vroeg me af: “Is dit werkelijk waar het om draait?” “Waarom kunnen mensen niet gewoon met elkaar omgaan?” Is dit echt wat God voor Zijn mensen in gedachten had? Als we “kleine Christus” zijn zoals we beweren te zijn, zouden we dan niet met elkaar overweg moeten kunnen? Zouden wij niet degenen moeten zijn die vreugdevol en vol leven zijn?

Ik ging naar Washington met zulke gedachten in mijn hoofd. Terwijl ik daar was, bezocht ik een kerk die zowel Bijbels als geestelijk gericht was. Het is moeilijk uit te leggen wat er allemaal in mijn geest, hart en leven gebeurde gedurende die zes maanden. Maar ik vertrok daar en ging terug naar huis met hernieuwde kracht en visie.

We zouden het licht van de wereld moeten zijn! We zouden iets te bieden moeten hebben voor anderen! We zouden in staat moeten zijn met elkaar om te gaan! Ja, we gaan individueel en gezamenlijk als kerk door harde tijden, maar als we de goede strijd van het geloof strijden, als we onze loopbaan voltooien, als we het geloof bewaren, ligt er voor ieder van ons een kroon van gerechtigheid klaar, welke de Here, de rechtvaardige Rechter, mij op die dag zal geven; en niet alleen mij, maar ook allen die zijn verschijning liefhebben. Ik heb een goede strijd gestreden, ik heb mijn loopbaan voleindigd, ik heb het geloof bewaard: Voortaan ligt er voor mij een kroon van gerechtigheid klaar, welke de Here, de rechtvaardige Rechter, mij op die dag zal geven; en niet alleen mij, maar ook allen die zijn verschijning liefhebben – 2 Timoteüs 4:7-8.

15 juni 2018, 16:40. Het gehuil van de pager van de hulpdiensten verbrak de vredige namiddag toen hij tot leven kwam. “Eén auto over de kop op ‘Gingko Avenue’, mogelijke beknelling,” was de herhaalde melding. Toen we op de plaats van het ongeval aankwamen, zat daar een jonge vrouw die ongeveer in haar midden twintig leek en zichtbaar gewond was. Met bloed en tranen die over haar gezicht stroomden, herhaalde ze de zinnen: “Ik wil niet dood… Ik ben er niet klaar voor om te sterven… Misschien zie ik mijn baby nooit meer.” Terwijl seconden minuten werden, probeerden de paramedici haar zenuwen te kalmeren. We doorzochten de verfrommelde auto en de omgeving op zoek naar de vermeende vermiste baby. Ondertussen zat zij daar met rijen van zorgen en angst. Ze had tranen en bloed op haar gezicht en herhaalde: “Misschien zie ik mijn baby nooit meer… Ik wil niet dood… Ik ben er niet klaar voor om te sterven.”

Als hulpverleners vonden we slechts een autostoeltje dat niet vastgemaakt was, zonder bewijs van een baby ergens. Terwijl de ambulancebemanning haar vastmaakte op de brancard en in de ambulance laadde, bleef ze herhalen: “Waar is mijn baby…? Ik ben er niet klaar voor om te sterven… Ik wil niet dood… Misschien zie ik mijn baby nooit meer.”

Toen ik die avond de plaats verliet, met dat beeld en die zinnen in mijn hoofd, werd ik door twee ernstige gedachten getroffen. Als ik het was, miraculeus een ongeluk overlevend en daar zittend naast mijn voertuig, nauwelijks coherent, met bloed over mijn gezicht—wat zou ik dan zeggen? Waaraan zouden de paramedici en het reddingsteam mij herinneren? Zou ik er klaar voor zijn om te sterven? Zou ik helder zijn voor God?

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Als christenen, wanneer hebben we voor het laatst iemand geholpen zijn ziel voor de dood voor te bereiden? Als gelovigen die verlost zijn uit de ellende en de chaos van een leven van zonde (zie 1 Korinthiërs 6:9-11), zouden we… altijd bereid moeten zijn een antwoord te geven aan eenieder die ons naar de hoop die in ons is vraagt, met zachtmoedigheid en ontzag – 1 Petrus 3:15.

In de herfst van 2018 opende God de deur voor mij om naar een kerk in een andere staat te verhuizen waar ik stabiliteit vond. Het was daar dat God een godvruchtige jongedame in mijn leven bracht, en we zijn getrouwd op 30 november 2019. Getrouwd zijn en broeders om mij heen hebben die mij omringden met discipelschap, medeleven en biddende steun hielpen mij op vele manieren in de Heer te groeien.

Het verblijf daar heeft in mij een hernieuwde visie wakker geroepen om het licht van de wereld te zijn. Vandaag ben ik dankbaar dat God mij niet heeft losgelaten. Terwijl ik bleef vechten in de geestelijke strijd, gaf God mij telkens weer de kracht en wijsheid om de volgende juiste stap te doen. Met elke overwinning groeide mijn kracht. Nadert tot God, en Hij zal tot u naderen… – Jacobus 4:8. Ik dank God dat Hij mij overwinning heeft gegeven en mij heeft geholpen mijn uiteindelijke bron van liefde, zekerheid en doel te vinden—mijn Heer en Verlosser, Jezus Christus.

The year was around 60 AD. The Apostle Paul had been apprehended and almost killed in the Temple at Jerusalem by a mob of angry Jews.

A few days later, he had been whisked off to the Roman Procurator Felix because of danger from a group of Jewish plotters. Felix had heard his case and though there was no evidence to convict Paul, Felix had kept him in prison for the next two years until the new Procurator, Festus, took his place.

King Herod Agrippa II came to visit Festus and the two of them listened to Paul speak. During the hearing Paul …reasoned of righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come, [until finally] Felix trembled, and answered, Go thy way for this time; when I have a convenient season, I will call for thee –Acts 24:25. Then towards the end of Paul’s oration …Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad –Acts 26:24.

Festus was not speaking of scientific knowledge, but of the fact that Paul was well-studied. Worse yet, Paul was making the governor uncomfortable with his sinful life and his reasoning made clear that the only solution for both Festus and Agrippa was to follow the Scriptures of the Hebrews.

Paul was well educated. He made clear in his letters and sermons, quoting not only from the Jewish Bible, but also from a variety of Greek and Cretan philosophers and poets.

In more modern times, it seems as though science is not a friend to faith. Many scientists claim that the idea of an intelligent designer of the Universe is ludicrous. Further, many of them would say that those who believe such things are the next thing to savages.

It certainly turns many Christians away from science entirely. They do not see something so antagonistic to the fundamental Christian faith as being useful.

I can understand this point of view, but I think that we should not give up learning simply because some of those who claim to be so knowledgeable are, in actuality, quite foolish.

Creation

When I think about the subject of science, I often begin with the subject of creation. This is the beginning of everything and is the first place where “science” and the Bible first come into conflict.

Science is simply unable to accept that there could have been a Creator God who set in motion everything that we see.

There are many books delving into the subject of intelligent design and seeing God’s fingerprints throughout creation. It takes a lot more faith to believe that the universe happened by chance, than to believe in a Creator.

The Bible makes it clear that God was not only present at the time of Creation, but it was also He who began it (John 1:1-3). Paul says For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse –Romans 1:20.

People should be able to discern that there is a Creator God involved in our world and the universe from the time of Creation. They should be able to understand a few other things about Him as well. Perhaps most important for our discussion here, we can tell by looking at creation that God is an orderly God and that He created the world to function with a specific structure and laws that govern it.

This is one of the big differences between the Creation account found in Genesis and the myths of creation found in other cultures of the time. The Bible makes it clear that God intentionally created the world, that He did so in an orderly fashion, and that He made certain that every part of it meshed with all the other parts. There is no magic or mystical thinking in the Genesis account.

The Laws of the Universe Still Stand

There are many people who believe that they can alter the way that the universe functions, that they can behave in immoral ways and not suffer the rewards of sin, and that they can do foolish things and not suffer the consequences of their behavior.

The Prophet Jeremiah tells us that there are laws which are in place that will not cease to function. Thus saith the LORD, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The LORD of hosts is his name: If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the LORD, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever –Jeremiah 31:35-36.

There is a whole set of laws that governs the way that the earth rotates on its axis and orbits the sun. Everything from the speed of light to the way that gravity pulls things towards large bodies of mass was instituted at the time of Creation—…all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation –2 Peter 3:4.

Since those laws continue and do not fluctuate, we are able to understand them—at least in part. This is what science is—the study of the natural world that we see and an attempt to comprehend the ways in which it works. God created our world in such a way that if you do an experiment the same way every time, you will get the same results every time.

Science Will Never Understand Everything

The Prophet Isaiah says, For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts –Isaiah 55:8-9.

Even the smartest quantum physicists will admit that they don’t understand everything. In fact, the number of questions that they have is greater than the whole storehouse of knowledge that has been accumulated.

Most of us will have far less understanding of the universe than that. We won’t understand all the details of how the atom functions. We won’t be able to do the calculus necessary to put a satellite into orbit. That’s all right. The important thing is that we learn what we can in order to understand what an amazing and orderly God we serve.

Presuppositions are a Problem

The biggest problem that we see in science is not the science itself, rather it is the biases of the people performing the science. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God… –Psalm 14:1. By this definition, many scientists are fools.

I don’t say this lightly. Atheists observe the universe and since they believe that there cannot be a God, they must then explain how it exists without the presence of an actual Creator. This is the heart of foolishness.

When they come to gaps in their knowledge, they are silent and yet the Christian can explain them in a few simple words. As I said before, when we look at the complexity of the universe, from the tiniest things to the largest galaxies, we can see the hands of God at work.

When I consider thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast ordained; What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? –Psalm 8:3-4. When we think about the world around us, when we read what scientists write, it is crucial that we come to it with a knowledge that God is behind all of this. For in him we live, and move, and have our being… – Acts 17:28, and nothing that science can discern will change that.

Science should be like a detective, uncovering God’s fingerprints on the universe, not someone bound and determined to discredit His very real presence.

Many Scientists Believe in God

Looking into the past, many scientists were men who believed in the God of the Bible. Isaac Newton, Francis Bacon, Nicholas Copernicus and many others believed in the Bible and were forthright in their expression of this faith to others.

In more modern days, there are many men and women of science who believe in the God of the Bible. Just because one is working in science doesn’t mean that they are unable to have a life of faith.

Many people have co-opted scientific discoveries to push messages that are against Christian belief and teaching.

We need to remember that when there is a set of facts, there are usually different explanations that can account for their presence. Creation and evolution examine the same facts of nature, yet from a different perspective or bias, thus they end up with vastly different conclusions. Perhaps it is a little like a Sherlock Holmes story, where Dr. Watson routinely takes the facts and gives an inaccurate explanation of them, while the detective takes the same information and gives the right explanation.

Science and Medicine

It is not against Scripture to research how things work in our universe, as long as we do so within a Biblical framework and understanding that there is a Creator God who is ordering it all.

Modern medicine is an application of many various fields, including anatomy, microanatomy, genetics, and biochemistry. The point, in this case, is to observe the human body the best that we can and then to fix the things that go wrong with it. Doctors can be scientists, but most of them are simply applying knowledge which has been passed down to them through their training.

Observation is where things start. Let’s consider diabetes as an example. Aretaeus of Cappadocia in the second century AD was the first person to give a complete description of diabetes and actually gave the disease the name diabetes. The problem was that while he was able to diagnose people with this illness, he had no treatment to help his patients. Observation had only taken him so far.

Over time, other work was done that demonstrated that the problem was an issue in the pancreas and that something was specifically wrong with the islet cells. Even into the early 1900s, there was no cure for Diabetes Mellitus and the only solution that doctors had to offer was an extremely low glycemic diet with severe calorie limits—attempting to keep patients at 500 or 600 calories a day. As can be imagined, this wasn’t an ideal treatment.

It wasn’t until the 1920s that a couple of researchers in Canada discovered a way to extract insulin from dogs and administered it to a 14-year-old who was dying of diabetes. The extract saved his life and began a new era for people with diabetes.

This is the way that things work. We begin by observing a disease and various medications that seem to be effective for it, then over time and through meticulous testing we can assess what treatments are most effective for that illness.

Studies in which half of the participants with a disease are given a medication or treatment and half are given a placebo (a pill without medical efficacy) are still the most effective way of telling whether something really works.

Why Treatments Need to be Studied

There is a real tendency to believe that the things that you have been taught are effective. We know that George Washington died of pneumonia. His doctors probably damaged his chances of recovery by bleeding him four times for a total of close to 40 percent of his blood volume. They probably would have bled him a fifth time, but he wasn’t thought to be strong enough to survive the procedure.

Doctors bled patients because they believed that there were toxic build ups in the blood stream that had to be let out. Most of the people who died after bloodletting would probably have died anyway, but bleeding people who are really sick certainly doesn’t help them recover.

Maybe the doctors simply wanted to be doing something. Patients expected bloodletting and so they met those expectations, even though it harmed the patients.

Experience is what lets you make the same mistakes with a lot more confidence.

What Makes a Good Study

Good studies—have plenty of patients in them, have a control group (that either receives an inactive pill called a placebo, or the current best treatment for that disease), and have the test group getting the new treatment. It is also important for the control group and the test group to be matched as closely as possible. Finally, the size of the groups in the study is vital to the conclusions of the study. If there are only ten or twenty patients in the study, it is not a large enough group to really sort out if something works or doesn’t.

For many diseases there is something called a placebo effect. This placebo effect is when people get better from an illness even though they are not receiving something that should be effective at treating the malady. Interestingly, in studies, many people get side effects from the inert pills. If 20 percent of the people getting the placebo get better and 45 percent of the people getting the treatment get better, that would indicate that the treatment is effective. If the difference is minimal—say 20 percent of the placebo group and 23 percent of the treatment group improve—then the treatment isn’t effective.

Problems

The biggest problem with many treatments is that they simply aren’t studied. Vitamin supplements and herbal compounds may work, but many of them have never actually been studied in a trial comparing them with a control group. Most of the information is anecdotal. The fact that someone’s grandmother or uncle benefited from something is possibly an indication that it is effective, but it doesn’t tell us how effective this treatment is or what dosage level is ideal.

Another issue is when studies simply don’t have enough participants to really give accurate information. Many studies only include ten or twenty patients. That is simply not enough to identify how well a treatment works or what side effects can be expected. For a drug to be approved by the FDA, it will typically have been studied on between 1,000 to 3,000 patients with the disease.

A final issue with studies is when they show that a medication is effective, but the effect isn’t clinically significant. As an example, a new injectable medication for dementia (aducanumab) was recently approved by the FDA. It is very expensive, and the benefit seemed to be small. Patients who were on it got an average of 1.5 more test questions right on an 85-question mental status questionnaire after 18 months compared to the control group.

One can rightly question if the benefits shown by this medication are worth the 50,000 dollar-per-year cost. More than that, how much of a meaningful improvement in someone’s everyday activities would come from using such a medicine? It seems unlikely that it would make very much of a difference.

It is unfortunate, but drug companies will always try to make it seem like their medicine is the best, even if the studies do not show significant benefit over existing, cheaper options.

Conclusion

Christians are faced with a world which does not love them or their beliefs. Many would try to use science as a way to bludgeon them into giving up their faith. I hope that does not lead us to give up on the scientific method or to give up attempting to understand the laws behind the universe that God created.

The scientific method is valid, even if many of the people who use it are atheists or agnostics. If a treatment works, it should be observable, testable, and repeatable.

Even as we approach it, we have a basic understanding of the universe that atheists don’t have. Knowing that there is a Creator God who loves us makes a major difference as we interpret the results of all the different observations that are being made in the fields of medicine and other places.

Those who do not know God are bound to be ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth –2 Timothy 3:7. On the other hand, if we begin with a Biblical understanding, we can use science as a tool to help us to understand the creation that He has placed around us.
