The history of our world has been defined by its conflicts. From the earliest disputes of Cain and Abel to the military operations of the twenty-first century, humanity has never ceased to attack one another. Peacetime is simply a waiting period for the next battle; treaties and ceasefires are only delays in the violence.

The wars of the spiritual realm have been equally as long and as brutal as the physical wars. These battles have reached us from the earliest dawn of time, where they originated in the hearts of Adam and Eve. The struggle against temptation and rebellion is present in each of us, whether it is acknowledged or not. Few emerge victorious into a true peace, and even that peace is a watchful peace that can be shattered in a moment of wavering.

The following account is but a brief spark in this trying fire of strife.

The year was 1942, and all across the world there raged a war the likes of which had never been seen before. Destruction and carnage had become commonplace, none more so than in the Pacific theater. There, speckled amongst the vast blue expanse of the Pacific Ocean, its tropical islands hosted battles of unparalleled ferocity and savagery. Suicide charges, artillery annihilation, and arial bombardments made life for the common soldier a living nightmare. At any moment a banzai charge (a typically nocturnal all-out attack of massed infantry yelling at the top of their voices as they charged) might split the night air into a rush of charging enemies whipped into a killing frenzy. A wayward shell, some weighing as much as a small car, could fall from the sky with deadly results. Death was ever present, claiming lives seemingly at random.

Four thousand miles to the east, another battle was raging. This one was as deadly as the first, encompassing hundreds of young men in an all-out struggle for their spiritual survival. Instead of the physical fighting on the Oriental islands of the Far East, this battle would be fought in the hearts and minds of those involved in this battle. Instead of machine guns and grenades, they would be armed with the sharpest of two-edged swords (The Holy Scriptures), guided by a power (The Holy Spirit) greater than any naval fleet.

These young men were called to a term of service in the physical warfare that was raging. Two years earlier, the Selective Training and Service Act of 1940 had been passed before the United States entered the war. This Act required all men between the ages of eighteen and forty-five to register for the draft. Those selected were expected to serve a one-year term. Once war was declared, this term would be extended until the end of the fighting.

To these young men, this draft and the current war prompted their memories of stories of a similar war and a similar draft, scarcely a generation prior, that had called away their fathers to the training camps of the United States military. There, the older generation had been subjected to all manner of malicious maltreatment. At that time, it was expected that all able-bodied young men would not only be willing, but also eager, to serve their country in battle against the enemy. This prevailing sentiment had brought about a general anger and animosity towards the conscientious objectors of the First World War. Pressure was applied to make them join in the drills and decorum of the armed forces, and penalties of various kinds could be and were enforced against those that refused. So severe were the punishments that many suffered physically, and several were killed by the treatment they received.

In like manner to their fathers, these young men were being called to serve their earthly country by bearing arms. Draftees were to report to their local recruiting office, where they would be organized and shipped to one of several training camps around the country. There they were to be molded into soldiers, prepared to kill their fellow man, and then sent overseas for that purpose. Yet their faith decreed otherwise.

Fortunately, they were not the only ones who remembered the First World War. In the two and a half decades since that war, both Mennonites and various concerned individuals had been at work, ensuring that if the need arose, there would be an option that could satisfy the government’s requirements of service while not going against the principles and convictions of conscientious objectors. Thus were born various organizations and programs that afforded an exemption to military duty. Conscientious objectors were placed in various service roles through these programs. They served in hospitals, built roads and irrigation canals, and provided labor for conservation efforts. In this way they could fulfill the law without breaking the Law (see Mark 12:17).

Despite the bureaucratic acceptance of the conscientious objectors’ (COs) convictions, and their subsequent alternate service, public feeling often still ran hot against, not only the nonresistant Mennonites and Amish, but against any conscientious objectors. Individuals who refused to fight could expect that not only would they personally be brought under pressure, but that their families and friends would also be scrutinized. Some of their families were shunned or looked down on, with the local community boycotting their businesses. In some cases, local law enforcement would turn a blind eye to the mistreatment of non-resistant people within their jurisdiction. In extreme instances, patriotic fervor would boil over, resulting in mob violence, property damage, and in a few rare instances, direct attacks against the perceived slackers.

Although most of Europe and its allies had been embroiled in this war since Hitler’s invasion of Poland in September of 1939, the United States did not join in the initial dispute. While the German army stormed through Europe, the early years of the war in the Pacific were dominated by Japan, who had already invaded China as early as 1937. The United States remained neutral during this time, motivated by a general feeling of isolationism. This would all change on the morning of December 7, 1941, as the Japanese Navy launched a surprise attack on the United States, attacking ships moored in Pearl Harbor, the home of the United States Pacific fleet. Retaliation was swift, and war was declared on Japan and its allies. Japan redoubled their offensive, sweeping over the island nations scattered across the Pacific. The Japanese commitment to the war was personal and intense. Honor, even in death, was esteemed higher than life. The emperor was worshiped as infallible, and Japanese soldiers hurled themselves into battle in his name, even in the face of overwhelming odds. Spurred by its fanaticism and an efficient, well-supplied attack force, Japan set its sights on the Philippines. There its army was met by a force vastly inferior to their own.

Meanwhile, at their various stations throughout the country, the COs were facing their own attack. They had been afforded the relief of not needing to fight a physical fight. With this exception came unforeseen opportunities for serving the suffering individuals under their care. Throughout their various ministries, they would encounter all manner of people. Each encounter was another opportunity to show a Christian’s peace and love in the midst of the on-going war, especially in the mental institutions and hospitals that employed some of the COs. The state of the mental hospitals at the time was deplorable. Patients were treated roughly, or simply neglected. Troublesome ones would be bound in strait jackets for weeks or forced to live in their own filth. Food and sanitation did not begin to meet the needs represented. Several of the young men brought attention to the situation of the mentally handicapped, through writing to newspapers or detailing their observations about the abuse to their contacts at home. These actions led to growing public awareness and concern about the treatment of the disabled, which would be the catalyst for change in the care of those unable to care for themselves.

Unfortunately, the opportunity to serve came at a cost. The COs were young and separated from their church and family. Ungodly influences abounded around them. Because they were separated from their churches and families, these influences weighed more heavily on the young men’s minds than they would have at home. The battle was still being waged, and now more than ever they had to lean on God as their strength, support, and defense.

In the Pacific, Japan moved in for an overpowering assault of the Philippines. The island nation had long been preparing its defenses, and now it would be tested by the impetus of the Japanese invaders. This defending army was a product of the training and leadership of General George A. MacArthur. MacArthur was somewhat of a prodigy of the United States military, emerging from his service in World War I as the youngest divisional commander in the Army. Since then, his time between the Wars had been spent largely in the Philippines, whose beaches and jungles he was now defending. In the months leading up to the invasion, he requested reinforcements, updated equipment, and sufficient materials to withstand an attack. Because the focus of the United States at the time was squarely focused on winning the war in Europe first, his requests were denied, and he was therefore out-manned and out-gunned. Nonetheless, MacArthur dug in and prepared to defend against the inevitable landings and subsequent inward crawl of the invaders. His troops suffered massive casualties in their slow retreat. Although defeat soon became apparent, the General refused to leave the island. Not until the time when the island was all but taken, was he finally persuaded to slip through enemy lines, evacuating to Batchelor Field, Australia. Here it was that he made a solemn promise to those he had left behind: “I shall return.”

The COs, now spread across numerous projects and fields of service, faced an equally diverse set of challenges. Instead of the steady guidance of their home congregations, they were now under the leadership of government appointed directors. Their camp schedules kept them at work, up to six days a week. Sundays were generally reserved for worship services. The influence of a world at war all around them had set in. Harry Litwiller, a Mennonite youth in Canada, was one of those who fell to the influences of the world. He was put into the army, where he quickly filed for CO status. While his request was being processed, he picked up gambling and drinking from other recruits. Word of his new habits soon made their way to his military superiors, and his request was denied. Churches prayed, wrote letters, and otherwise made efforts to support the young men in their trials. They could not know it, but their time of testing would soon be drawing to a close.

Finally, the year was 1945. The last months of the war had seen the conscription of young boys and old men into the German Army as Hitler made a last desperate stand, caught between the allied armies of the Eastern and Western fronts. Unable to continue, the Germans sued for peace. Now that the war was over in Europe, the tide of war shifted to the Pacific. America rallied, propelled by its greater industrial capacity and natural resources, causing the Japanese advance to grind to a halt—thus, the American counter-offensive began. Slowly, island-hopping across the ocean, General MacArthur drew ever closer to Japan.

MacArthur had not forgotten his promise to the Filipino people. In his four years of absence, battles had been fought over the smallest of atolls—coral islands just large enough for an airstrip and a garrison. Even as the Japanese were uprooted from these strongholds, they maintained a solid footing in the Philippines. The island nation had suffered through the years of the enemy occupation. It was home to prison camps— housing prisoners of war and those accused of aiding the allies.

Time was now running out for the Japanese. Spread thin—with troops, equipment, and resources dwindling—they fought a desperate defensive campaign. On October 24, 1944, an Allied force landed on the eastern coast of the island of Leyte. The battle for the Philippines would last for two months, but at its end MacArthur emerged victorious. Many months earlier he had overseen the island’s surrender, now he commanded its repossession. His promise was fulfilled.

The war dragged on. In Europe, it was over, but the Pacific was yet to be won. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, who had led the nation through the war, sickened and died. His vice president, Harry S. Truman, was sworn into office. His first decision was one unlike anything he could have ever imagined. Should he expend hundreds of thousands of lives to take Japan by land, or make them a gruesome example of a newly developed atomic bomb being dropped from the relative safety of the air? Truman deliberated and made his choice.

The war ended in the blink of an eye. The devastation of a pair of atomic bombs shocked Japan into surrender. They sued for peace, and peace was given. Except for the formalities, the war was over. Over, but the temporary peace was bought with an astronomical price of human life. Millions would never return to their grieving families.

For the COs, it was a return to a new normal. They were returning to their families, their churches, and their homes. But the war had changed them. Months and years had been spent away from spiritual oversight. Many would settle into their communities, raising their families and living out their Christian faith. Yet there had been casualties, with some, like Harry Litwiller, having given up their faith. The battle had been fierce, and not all its contestants had been wearing the full biblical armor available to them.

Both MacArthur and the victorious COs persevered to the end. Each believed in their cause, MacArthur in the devastation and destruction of war, and the COs in the redemption and peace of a fully surrendered life. They parallel each other here only in the fact that they both fought. The crucial difference is in what they fought for, and how they fought for it.

De geschiedenis van onze wereld is bepaald door haar conflicten. Van de vroegste twisten tussen Kaïn en Abel tot de militaire operaties van de eenentwintigste eeuw, de mensheid heeft nooit opgehouden elkaar aan te vallen. Vredestijd is eenvoudigweg een wachttijd voor de volgende slag; verdragen en staakt‑het‑vuren zijn slechts uitstel van geweld.

De oorlogsvoering in het geestelijke rijk is even lang en wreed geweest als de fysieke oorlogen. Deze gevechten hebben ons bereikt vanaf de vroegste dageraad van de tijd, waar ze hun oorsprong vonden in de harten van Adam en Eva. De strijd tegen verzoeking en opstand is in ieder van ons aanwezig, of het nu wordt erkend of niet. Weinigen treden zegevierend in ware vrede, en zelfs die vrede is een waakzame vrede die in een ogenblik van aarzeling verbrijzeld kan worden.

Het volgende verslag is slechts een korte vonk in dit beproevende vuur van strijd.

Het jaar was 1942, en over de hele wereld woedde een oorlog zoals men nog nooit had gezien. Vernietiging en slachting waren alledaags geworden, nergens meer dan in het Pacifische toneel. Daar, verspreid over de uitgestrekte blauwe vlakte van de Stille Oceaan, huisden tropische eilanden gevechten van ongeëvenaarde felheid en wreedheid. Zelfmoordaanvallen, artillerie‑vernietiging en luchtaanvallen maakten het leven van de gewone soldaat tot een levende nachtmerrie. Elk ogenblik kon een banzai‑charge (een gewoonlijk nachtelijke alles‑of‑niets‑aanval van massale infanterie die met luide kreten vooruit stormt) de nachtelijke lucht splijten in een storm van aanvallers in moorddadige razernij. Een voorbijvliegende granaat, sommigen zo zwaar als een kleine auto, kon uit de lucht vallen met dodelijke gevolgen. De dood was altijd aanwezig, en nam schijnbaar willekeurige levens.

Vierduizend mijl naar het oosten woedde een andere strijd. Deze was even dodelijk als de eerste, en omvatte honderden jonge mannen in een allesomvattende strijd om hun geestelijke overleving. In plaats van de fysieke gevechten op de oostelijke eilanden van het Verre Oosten, zou deze strijd in de harten en geesten van de betrokkenen worden gevochten. In plaats van mitrailleurs en granaten zouden zij gewapend zijn met het scherpste tweesnijdende zwaard (De Heilige Schrift), geleid door een macht (De Heilige Geest) groter dan welke vloot ook.

Deze jonge mannen waren opgeroepen voor een termijn van dienst in de fysieke oorlog die woedde. Twee jaar eerder was de Selective Training and Service Act van 1940 aangenomen voordat de Verenigde Staten de oorlog ingingen. Deze wet verplichtte alle mannen tussen achttien en vijfenveertig zich in te schrijven voor de dienstplicht. Degenen die geselecteerd werden, werden verwacht een termijn van één jaar te dienen. Zodra de oorlog verklaard werd, zou deze termijn worden verlengd tot het einde van de gevechten.

Voor deze jonge mannen riep deze dienstplicht en de huidige oorlog herinneringen op aan verhalen van een soortgelijke oorlog en een gelijkaardige dienstplicht, nauwelijks een generatie eerder, die hun vaders had weggeroepen naar de trainingskampen van het Amerikaanse leger. Daar was de oudere generatie aan allerlei kwaadaardige mishandeling onderworpen geweest. Destijds werd verwacht dat alle gezonde jonge mannen niet alleen bereid, maar ook gretig zouden zijn hun land te dienen in de strijd tegen de vijand. Deze heersende sentimenten hadden geleid tot algemene woede en vijandigheid tegenover de gewetensbezwaarden van de Eerste Wereldoorlog. Er werd druk uitgeoefend om hen te laten meedoen aan de oefeningen en het protocol van de strijdkrachten, en straffen van verschillende aard konden en werden opgelegd aan degenen die weigerden. Zo zwaar waren de straffen dat velen fysiek leden en enkelen door de behandeling die zij ontvingen omkwamen.

Net als hun vaders werden ook deze jonge mannen opgeroepen hun aardse vaderland te dienen door wapens te dragen. Oproepelingen moesten zich melden bij hun plaatselijke rekruteringsbureau, waar zij georganiseerd en verzonden zouden worden naar een van de verschillende trainingskampen door het land. Daar zouden zij gevormd worden tot soldaten, voorbereid om hun medemens te doden, en vervolgens naar het buitenland gestuurd voor dat doel. Hun geloof bepaalde echter iets anders.

Gelukkig waren zij niet de enigen die zich de Eerste Wereldoorlog herinnerden. In de tweeënhalf decennia sinds die oorlog hadden zowel mennonieten als diverse betrokken personen zich ingezet om ervoor te zorgen dat er, mocht de nood zich voordoen, een optie beschikbaar zou zijn die aan de eisen van de overheid voor dienstplicht zou voldoen zonder in te gaan tegen de principes en overtuigingen van gewetensbezwaarden. Zo werden verschillende organisaties en programma’s geboren die vrijstelling van militaire dienst boden. Gewetensbezwaarden werden via deze programma’s in verschillende dienstrollen geplaatst. Zij dienden in ziekenhuizen, bouwden wegen en irrigatiekanalen en verrichtten arbeid voor natuurbehoud. Op deze manier konden zij de wet vervullen zonder de Wet te breken (zie Marcus 12:17).

Ondanks de bureaucratische acceptatie van de overtuigingen van de gewetensbezwaarden (GB’s) en hun daaropvolgende alternatieve dienst, liep het publieke sentiment vaak nog heet tegen, niet alleen de niet‑gewelddadige mennonieten en amish, maar tegen alle gewetensbezwaarden. Personen die weigerden te vechten, konden verwachten dat niet alleen zij persoonlijk onder druk zouden worden gezet, maar dat ook hun families en vrienden zouden worden ondervraagd. Sommige van hun families werden gemeden of neergekeken, waarbij de lokale gemeenschap hun bedrijven boycotte. In sommige gevallen keurde de lokale wetshandhaving de mishandeling van niet‑gewelddadige mensen binnen hun rechtsgebied stilzwijgend goed. In extreme gevallen kookte het patriottische enthousiasme over, met als gevolg rellen, eigendomsschade en in enkele zeldzame gevallen directe aanvallen tegen de vermeende lafaards.

Hoewel het grootste deel van Europa en haar bondgenoten sinds Hitlers inval in Polen in september 1939 in deze oorlog waren verwikkeld, deed de Verenigde Staten niet mee aan het initiële geschil. Terwijl het Duitse leger door Europa stormde, werd de oorlog in de vroege jaren in de Stille Oceaan gedomineerd door Japan, dat China al zo vroeg als 1937 had binnengevallen. De Verenigde Staten bleven in deze periode neutraal, gedreven door een algemeen gevoel van isolationisme. Dit veranderde op de ochtend van 7 december 1941, toen de Japanse marine een verrassingsaanval op de Verenigde Staten lanceerde en schepen in Pearl Harbor, de thuisbasis van de Amerikaanse Pacificvloot, aanviel. De vergelding was snel, en de oorlog werd verklaard aan Japan en haar bondgenoten. Japan verdubbelde hun offensief en trok over de eilanden verspreid over de Stille Oceaan. De inzet van Japan in de oorlog was persoonlijk en intens. Eer, zelfs in de dood, werd hoger gewaardeerd dan het leven. De keizer werd als onfeilbaar vereerd, en Japanse soldaten wierpen zich in de strijd in zijn naam, zelfs bij overweldigende kansen. Aangewakkerd door fanaticisme en een efficiënte, goed bevoorrade aanvalsmacht, richtte Japan zijn blik op de Filipijnen. Daar werd hun leger geconfronteerd met een strijdkracht die verre inferiorer was.

Intussen stonden de GB’s, verspreid over verschillende projecten en dienstvelden, voor hun eigen aanval. Zij hadden de verlichting gekregen dat zij geen fysieke strijd hoefden te voeren. Met deze uitzondering kwamen onvoorziene mogelijkheden om de lijdende personen onder hun zorg te dienen. Gedurende hun diverse bediening kwamen zij allerlei mensen tegen. Elke ontmoeting was een nieuwe gelegenheid om de vrede en liefde van een christen te tonen temidden van de voortdurende oorlog, vooral in de psychiatrische instellingen en ziekenhuizen waar sommige GB’s werkzaam waren. De staat van de psychiatrische ziekenhuizen was destijds erbarmelijk. Patiënten werden ruw behandeld of gewoon verwaarloosd. Moeilijke patiënten werden wekenlang in dwangjassen gebonden of gedwongen in hun eigen vuil te leven. Voeding en hygiëne voldeden bij lange na niet aan de behoeften. Enkele van de jonge mannen vestigden via brieven aan kranten of door hun observaties over het misbruik te melden aan contacten thuis de aandacht op de situatie van geestelijk gehandicapten. Deze handelingen leidden tot groeiende publieke bewustwording en zorg over de behandeling van gehandicapten, wat de katalysator zou zijn voor verandering in de zorg voor hen die niet voor zichzelf konden zorgen.

Helaas kwam de kans om te dienen met een prijs. De GB’s waren jong en gescheiden van hun kerk en familie. Ongoddelijke invloeden overvloedden rondom hen. Omdat zij verwijderd waren van hun kerken en families, drukten deze invloeden zwaarder op de gedachten van de jonge mannen dan zij thuis zouden hebben gedaan. De strijd woedde voort, en nu meer dan ooit moesten zij op God leunen als hun kracht, steun en verdediging.

In de Stille Oceaan voerde Japan een overweldigende aanval op de Filipijnen. Het eilandrijk had lang aan zijn verdediging gewerkt en nu zou deze door de aandrang van de Japanse indringers op de proef worden gesteld. Dit verdedigende leger was het product van de training en leiding van generaal George A. MacArthur. MacArthur was enigszins een wonderkind van het Amerikaanse leger, opgekomen uit zijn dienst in de Eerste Wereldoorlog als de jongste divisiecommandant in het leger. Sindsdien had hij zijn tijd tussen de oorlogen grotendeels in de Filipijnen doorgebracht, wiens stranden en jungles hij nu verdedigde. In de maanden voorafgaand aan de invasie had hij versterkingen, vernieuwde uitrusting en voldoende materiaal aangevraagd om een aanval te weerstaan. Omdat de focus van de Verenigde Staten destijds volledig gericht was op het winnen van de oorlog in Europa eerst, werden zijn verzoeken afgewezen, en hij was dus in de minderheid qua manschap en bewapening. Desalniettemin groef MacArthur zich in en bereidde zich voor om de onvermijdelijke landingen en de daaropvolgende vorderingen van de indringers af te slaan. Zijn troepen leden enorme verliezen tijdens hun trage terugtocht. Hoewel nederlaag spoedig duidelijk werd, weigerde de generaal het eiland te verlaten. Pas toen het eiland vrijwel in vijandelijke handen was, werd hij uiteindelijk overtuigd door de linies van de vijand te glippen en te evacueren naar Batchelor Field, Australië. Daar deed hij een plechtig beloof aan degenen die hij had achtergelaten: “Ik zal terugkeren.”

De GB’s, nu verspreid over talrijke projecten en dienstvelden, kregen een even divers stel uitdagingen te verduren. In plaats van de vaste leiding van hun thuisgemeenten stonden zij nu onder leiding van door de overheid aangestelde directeuren. Hun kamproosters hielden hen aan het werk, tot wel zes dagen per week. Zondagen waren doorgaans gereserveerd voor samenkomsten. De invloed van een wereld in oorlog om hen heen had zijn invloed laten gelden. Harry Litwiller, een mennonitische jongeman in Canada, was een van degenen die bezweken voor de invloeden van de wereld. Hij werd in het leger geplaatst, waar hij snel CO‑status aanvroeg. Terwijl zijn verzoek werd verwerkt, raakte hij besmet met gokken en drinken door andere rekruten. Het nieuws van zijn nieuwe gewoonten bereikte al snel zijn militaire superieuren, en zijn verzoek werd afgewezen. Kerken baden, schreven brieven en deden anderszins pogingen om de jonge mannen in hun beproevingen te steunen. Zij konden het niet weten, maar hun tijd van beproeving trok spoedig naar een einde.

Eindelijk brak het jaar 1945 aan. De laatste maanden van de oorlog hadden geleid tot de dienstplicht van jonge jongens en oude mannen in het Duitse leger toen Hitler een laatste wanhopige stand maakte, ingesloten tussen de geallieerde legers van het oostelijke en westelijke front. Niet in staat door te gaan, vroegen de Duitsers om vrede. Nu de oorlog in Europa voorbij was, verschoof de oorlogstroom naar de Stille Oceaan. Amerika mobiliseerde, aangedreven door zijn grotere industriële capaciteit en natuurlijke hulpbronnen, waardoor de Japanse opmars tot stilstand kwam—zo begon het Amerikaanse tegenoffensief. Langzaam, eiland voor eiland over de oceaan, naderde generaal MacArthur steeds dichter bij Japan.

MacArthur was zijn belofte aan het Filipijnse volk niet vergeten. In zijn afwezigheid van vier jaar waren er gevechten geleverd om de kleinste atollen—koraaleilanden net groot genoeg voor een landingsbaan en een garnizoen. Zelfs toen de Japanners uit deze bolwerken werden verdreven, behielden zij een stevige voet in de Filipijnen. Het eilandrijk had geleden onder jaren van bezetting door de vijand. Het herbergde gevangenkampen—kampen voor krijgsgevangenen en degenen die ervan werden beschuldigd de geallieerden te hebben geholpen.

De tijd liep nu uit voor de Japanners. Verspreid en met slinkende troepen, uitrusting en middelen voerden zij een wanhoopsoffensief ter verdediging. Op 24 oktober 1944 landde een geallieerde macht aan de oostkust van het eiland Leyte. De strijd om de Filipijnen zou twee maanden duren, maar aan het eind kwam MacArthur als overwinnaar tevoorschijn. Maanden eerder had hij al het ontwapeningsproces van het eiland gehandhaafd en nu beval hij de herovering. Zijn belofte werd vervuld.

De oorlog sleepte zich voort. In Europa was zij voorbij, maar de Stille Oceaan moest nog worden gewonnen. President Franklin D. Roosevelt, die de natie door de oorlog had geleid, werd ziek en stierf. Zijn vicepresident, Harry S. Truman, werd ingezworen. Zijn eerste beslissing was er een die hij zich nooit had kunnen voorstellen. Moest hij honderduizenden levens opofferen om Japan over land in te nemen, of hen een gruwelijk voorbeeld maken door een pas ontwikkeld atoombom vanuit relatieve veiligheid uit de lucht te laten vallen? Truman beredeneerde en maakte zijn keuze.

De oorlog eindigde in een oogwenk. De verwoesting door een paar atoombommen schokte Japan tot overgave. Zij vroegen om vrede, en vrede werd gegeven. Behalve de formaliteiten was de oorlog voorbij. Voorbij, maar de tijdelijke vrede was gekocht met een astronomische prijs van mensenlevens. Miljoenen keerden nooit terug naar hun bedroefde families.

Voor de GB’s betekende het een terugkeer naar een nieuwe norm. Zij keerden terug naar hun families, hun kerken en hun huizen. Maar de oorlog had hen veranderd. Maanden en jaren waren weggeëist van geestelijke supervisie. Velen zouden zich vestigen in hun gemeenschappen, gezinnen stichten en hun christelijk geloof uitdragen. Toch waren er slachtoffers gevallen, sommigen, zoals Harry Litwiller, hadden hun geloof opgegeven. De strijd was hevig geweest, en niet al haar strijders hadden de volledige Bijbelse wapenrusting gedragen die hen ter beschikking stond.

Zowel MacArthur als de overwinnaars onder de GB’s hielden vol tot het einde. Ieder geloofde in zijn zaak: MacArthur in de vernietiging en het geweld van oorlog, en de GB’s in de verlossing en vrede van een volledig overgegeven leven. Zij lopen hier alleen parallel in het feit dat zij beiden vochten. Het cruciale verschil ligt in waar zij voor vochten, en hoe zij daarvoor vochten.

I want to introduce this article on Spiritual Gifts by observing an interesting verse: Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men –Ephesians 4:8. Throughout history, when a king went to battle against a city and conquered it, he and his army returned home, to be greeted by their people with great fanfare. They would march through the city with all the spoils of war, after which the king would hand out gifts from the stuff that was taken in battle, giving it to his people.

Likewise, when Jesus was crucified, through His death and resurrection, He conquered the enemy. He took the power from death, hell, the grave and from Satan himself for those who repent and believe in Him. When He returned home (ascended up on high) He gave gifts to His people— the Church. Here in Ephesians, we have a condensed list of spiritual gifts: And he [God] gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers –Ephesians 4:11.

We observe more detailed descriptions of these gifts given to the Church in 1 Corinthians chapter 12 both at the beginning of the chapter and the end of the chapter and in Romans chapter 12 verses 6 to 8. In 1 Corinthians we see the following gifts given—the word of wisdom, the word of knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, tongues, discerning of tongues, helps, and governments. Then, in Romans, we have more gifts added to our list—ministry, exhortation, giving, ruling, and showing mercy.

If I did not miss any, there is a total of 19 gifts given to the church. What a wealth of gifts have been given to the church when Jesus ascended up on high! It would be good for us to do a thorough study on each one of these gifts so that we would be able to recognize them in our congregations. One thing that could be observed is that our Pentecostal friends have taken a select few of these gifts such as miracles, healing, and speaking in tongues, and have held them above the rest, making them a validation of whether a person is born again, baptized in the Holy Spirit, or if they are more spiritual than those lacking these gifts. Or we could consider how the evangelicals tend to do the same with the gift of evangelism, which has made inroads into many conservative Anabaptist churches. Finally, we might examine how some of us plain churches take only the gifts that have to do with Church government, leaving it only to those who are ordained to have gifts, while most all the rest of the gifts are left unrecognized.

This all leads me to ask the question, “Should we be lifting one or two gifts out above the rest and emphasizing them, or should all of the gifts be recognized equally?” The only time that I see one lifted above the rest is in Paul’s letter to the Corinthians in the last verse of Chapter 12, and the first verse in chapter 14, where he exhorts them to covet after the best gift which, with careful reading, we will notice is referring to prophesy. As we continue with our careful reading, we discover that prophecy should hold precedence over speaking in tongues since apparently the Corinthian understanding of speaking in tongues was being abused and misused and the Church might not have been edified by their behavior.

Spiritual Gifts Should Not Excuse Ungodly Behavior

A word of caution might be in order here. There is an emphasis by some, on “knowing what my spiritual gift is.” I think this can be good, but it should not be done to the fault of excusing myself for bad behavior because “I have this gift and not the other.” For example, the prophet might excuse himself for being harsh because his gift is that of a prophet; since he may not have the gift of mercy, people may be unnecessarily hurt. We will all probably have a primary gift or gifts. As much as we may try to be well-equipped with as many of the gifts as we can, some will still be more dominant than others.

I have asked numerous people which gift was primary in the life of our Lord Jesus and the short answer is that He was full of the Holy Ghost and without measure and had them all. True enough, but even so, since we all want to be like Jesus, maybe we should stop excusing ourselves to one limited gift and pursue to be as fully equipped as possible. I know, and you know, that in this flesh we will not master them all and yet we should be receptive to them all. Having said that, we must realize, we are meant to be interdependent; that is why Jesus handed out these gifts severally to each man and we will all have our primary gift or gifts. But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will –1 Corinthians 12:11. Nevertheless, let’s be careful that we do not excuse wrong behavior, or, on the other hand, negligence of doing good, because “Well, that is just not my gift”.

Spiritual Gifts Are Not The Christian’s Identity

A couple of cautions may also be in place when seeking to understand spiritual gifts. Our identity should not be the gift that we have but rather that our identity is in Christ. We are a child of the King; we are not primarily a prophet, a teacher, or an evangelist. However, in being a child of the King, we have been given a gift by Him, to do His work, with His power. Recognizing first and foremost who we are in Christ will keep us in a beautiful place of humility, but if our primary identity is “this gift that I have,” I suppose it would be hard not to fall into pride and thus we open ourselves up to many pitfalls and dangers.

Spiritual Gifts Are God-Given, Not To Be Sought After By Man

Could there be a caution given in how we seek this gift? What does it mean when the Scripture says that God gives gifts according to His choosing? For instance, God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will? –Hebrews 2:4. Or, But all these worketh that one and the selfsame Spirit, dividing to every man severally as he will –1 Corinthians 12:11.

Do you notice in both verses the WILL of God being very involved in the giving of gifts in the Church? Maybe our “seeking spiritual gifts” should be done alone in our closet, asking God to make me humble and endue me with whatever gift He wants me to have to make me a useful tool in the church body that I am a part of—“Not my will, but thine be done”. Maybe He has given me a gift that I am not recognizing or using, and what I actually need is to stir up that gift and not neglect it, but rather use it in the place I fill in the church. Could it be possible that, if I were to seek enough after another spiritual gift, I just might get myself a counterfeit?

Also, it would be good to mention very directly again that when there is a focused seeking after spiritual gifts usually there is some resulting negative problem. Sometimes a select few are lifted out and taught to be more spiritually important, such as speaking in tongues, miracles, and healing. Some will promote that there is little to no value in the teaching of spiritual gifts and that the only ones which are for our day are the ones pertaining to the ordained church leaders such as government, pastors, and teachers. While some people use their understanding of spiritual gifts to become individualistic and they see little value in being a part of a body. This is wrong, since a careful reading of these Scriptures show us that ALL the gifts are essential so that God will have the ability to make use of all the gifts by a collaboration of all the people. Could it be possible that where certain gifts are elevated above the rest, whether it is speaking in tongues, healings, and miracles; or if it is evangelism; or if it is those more suited for the ordained among us, that there could be an unrecognized element of pride in our midst? We are so prone to disillusionment that it would be good to check our hearts thoroughly when seeking after spiritual gifts.

Spiritual Gifts Are Not Included In The Biblical List of Qualifications For Church Leaders

Paul told Timothy, Neglect not the gift that is in thee, which was given thee by prophecy, with the laying on of the hands of the presbytery –1 Timothy 4:14. Maybe rather than seeking out a gift, we need to stop neglecting the gift that has been given to us. Rather than seeking something new and exciting, we should stir up the gift we do have. It has happened that men in leadership have been removed from their post, because they do not have the gift for that which they were ordained. I would be very slow and very prayerful before removing an ordained brother from his office for that reason. Would it not be better to pray that God would increase that gift that had been given him by the laying on of hands? To quickly conclude that he does not have the gift may just be the easy way out.

We would never do that in a marriage. How often has it happened that a wife was more gifted in leadership than her husband? Disannulling the marriage is not an option, nor is it an option to add a third person to the marriage union to bring balance to the perceived lack of a proper balance of gifting. We have often seen that when prayer and the Holy Ghost was involved in a situation like this, God gave the husband what he lacked (1 Corinthians 12:24-25), and the wife learned to yield her gifting in a way that allowed her husband to be the godly head of the home.

God can also give the necessary gift to those in such a marriage and in such a ministry team if they find themselves lacking. For our comely parts have no need: but God hath tempered the body together, having given more abundant honour to that part which lacked: That there should be no schism [division] in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another –1 Corinthians 12:24-25. Is there ever a time to remove one from an office because of the lack of gifting? Maybe so, but let’s be very cautious, slow, careful, and prayerful.

In the case of church difficulty that seems to be due to the lack of gifting among the ordained, we need to consider the following verses. Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge among you? let him shew out of a good conversation his works with meekness of wisdom. But if ye have bitter envying and strife in your hearts, glory not, and lie not against the truth. This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish. For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work. But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be intreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy. And the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace of them that make peace. –James 3:13-18. Very rare is the case of church trouble involving church leadership when there is not a major lack by one or more of the ordained to be fully living out of God’s will and wisdom as defined herein.

The biblical answer to solving church problems that involves church leaders is three-fold. (1a) The leaders in question must humble their hearts in repentance before God and His Word, before the rest of the ordained, and where necessary before the local church. (1b) If the situation has deteriorated too much, then the wisdom of outside overseers should be sought. (2) The leaders who may be lacking in a specific gift should seek God through fervent prayer, both personally and of the local church, and should seek God’s provision for enabling ability through …the laying on of the hands of the presbytery –1 Timothy 4:14. (3) Then AFTER stability is restored the local brotherhood is at a good place to seek God’s will together about ordaining another brother to assist.

God’s Goal for Spiritual Gifts

I would see two main reasons for the gifts of the Spirit to be given to the Church.

The first reason is for the benefit of the church. In Ephesians we read: and he gave… [various spiritual gifts to believers] [to some this gift and to others a different gift] … For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: –Ephesians 4:11-12. First Corinthians chapter 12 has a long dialogue on how the gifts are to be utilized so as to benefit the body of Christ (the local church) and in verse 25 in particular, that there should be no schisms in the body, but that the members should have the same care one for another.

There are those who are going about preaching the need to have spiritual gifts, encouraging specific gifts such as evangelism, healing, miracles, and tongues, and it can be seen in many cases that this focused teaching actually causes divisions rather than unity. The Bible says that the gifts were given to bring the Church together and if it is not doing that, we should consider whether it is the real thing or if it is a counterfeit. I realize divisions happen for many reasons, but if the gifts in the body are not bringing together but dividing, we had better seek God for answers on why, because the gifts were meant to bring unity, oneness, and edification.

The second reason is for the benefit of the unbeliever. Some of the gifts were given as a sign for the unbeliever. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe –1 Corinthians 14:22. We see that throughout the New Testament tongues, miracles and healings followed the gospel in places where it was being presented to those who had never heard it before. This was a way that God used to solidify and validate in the hearts and minds of the unbeliever that this gospel must be of God because of the supernatural manifestations. We see that tongues also followed the spreading of the gospel so that all could hear it in their own language as on the day of Pentecost.

I would consider these to be the two main reasons and are the primary purposes of the gifts. We would do well to evaluate our gifts in light of these two main reasons to be sure we have the real thing and are using them according to the purposes for which they were given.

It is interesting that of the 19 gifts we are considering, most of these will be best utilized in the local Church. Remember, God uses the church to reach the world. Some of the gifts given to the church are for reaching the world, for instance, the evangelist has a more unique calling to reach the world. Gifts like healings, miracles, and speaking in tongues are some of the gifts that are more prevalent on the frontier of the gospel. This is not to say that these gifts are never seen in the local church. My prayer is that if someone came into our services who cannot understand a word of English, and there is no one who can interpret the preaching of the Word into their language, then may God give us the gifts of tongues so that they might hear the gospel and be edified.

We have seen where there was sickness, and the elders of the church were called and there was anointing and prayer. At times God chose to miraculously heal. However, just because we (believers) have this wonderful gift of healing it does not necessarily mean that God wants all of us to be healed of every illness. The apostle Paul prayed three times to be healed from his recurring illness (2 Corinthians 12:7-12), yet God told him no. If he was not healed when he had healed many others, why would I think it needs to be different for me? So, it is with all the gifts that are given to the church; they are allowed by God to be exercised according to His will, not ours. It is absolutely essential for me and you to be a part of a local body so we will have the gifts of the Spirit working together through all the members, for the work of the church, in bringing unity, oneness, and edification, and for the ongoing work of the Church in calling men from a world of sin and calling them into His kingdom.

The Gift of Tongues

It is important to consider for a moment the spiritual gift of tongues and specifically the place it fills in the Kingdom of God. The Apostle Paul tells us they are given for a sign. Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to them that believe not: but prophesying serveth not for them that believe not, but for them which believe –1 Corinthians 14:22.

It is not a sign to the believer that he really has the Holy Spirit, but it is a sign to the unbeliever that the gospel message is real. The classic example was on the day of Pentecost. We do not determine Peter’s credibility because he spoke in another language. We all would agree without any doubt, that Peter was born again, and that the many different languages were not for his approval but rather so that the ones hearing would know that this speaking in many different languages was supernatural. It would have taken a stubborn soul to scoff at the message being preached that day.

Recently, I was made aware of studies that have been done by recording the gibberish that comprises most of what is called tongues today. Interestingly, they found that English speakers used English syllables in repetition, and that Spanish speaking people used Spanish syllables, thus, they deducted that most of what is called tongues today is a counterfeit where the person, in their own language, repeats syllables of their native tongue in repetition. I believe that in many cases it is done innocently because of the vast amount of deception that follows the speaking in tongues.

What I understand as the real thing is the example of a lady in Canada, who only knew French and did not understand any English. This woman happened to come to a revival meeting where the revivalist was preaching in English with no French interpreter. She responded in repentance to the message and those who counseled with her asked her how she understood the message, which was in English. She responded that what she had heard was shared in the most beautiful French she had ever heard. Clearly a miracle took place so that she would hear the message of salvation and be able to respond to it. I am sure it was heartwarming to know how it was supernatural that she was able to hear it. I suspect there is a good possibility that at times, the one speaking in tongues may not even be aware of it. Surely, if God could confound the languages of those working on the tower of Babel, He can also cause the words of an English-speaking preacher to be converted into French words before entering the ears of a French-speaking hearer.

The reason we find in scripture for the gift of speaking in tongues, is twofold, and is for the unbeliever who comes among us. The first reason is so that he would hear the gospel message in his own language. The second reason is that when he hears it miraculously in his own language and the one speaking does not know his language, it is a sign for the unbeliever to cause him to acknowledge that the message he is hearing is of God, and by God.

In conclusion, we find that two of the main purposes of God giving gifts to the church, giving them severally as He wills, is for the unity and edification of the body of Christ, and for the unbeliever to hear and be persuaded of the gospel message. Let us seriously consider whether the spiritual gifts we have and those gifts that are evident in our churches are fulfilling the purpose for which they were given.

Quiero introducir este artículo sobre Dones espirituales observando un versículo interesante: Por lo cual dice: Subiendo a lo alto, llevó cautividad cautiva, y dio dones a los hombres –Efesios 4:8. A lo largo de la historia, cuando un rey iba a la guerra contra una ciudad y la conquistaba, él y su ejército regresaban a casa, para ser recibidos por su pueblo con gran algarabía. Marchaban por la ciudad con todos los despojos de la guerra, tras lo cual el rey repartía regalos de lo tomado en batalla, dándolos a su pueblo.

De igual manera, cuando Jesús fue crucificado, por Su muerte y resurrección, venció al enemigo. Quitó el poder de la muerte, del infierno, de la tumba y del mismo Satanás para los que se arrepienten y creen en Él. Cuando regresó a casa (subió a lo alto) dio dones a Su pueblo—la Iglesia. Aquí en Efesios tenemos una lista condensada de dones espirituales: Y él [Dios] dio a unos, apóstoles; y a otros, profetas; y a otros, evangelistas; y a otros, pastores y maestros –Efesios 4:11.

Observamos descripciones más detalladas de estos dones dados a la Iglesia en 1 Corintios capítulo 12 tanto al comienzo como al final del capítulo y en Romanos capítulo 12 versículos 6 a 8. En 1 Corintios vemos los siguientes dones concedidos—la palabra de sabiduría, la palabra de ciencia, fe, sanidades, milagros, lenguas, discernimiento de lenguas, ayudas y gobiernos. Luego, en Romanos se añaden más dones a nuestra lista—ministerio, exhortación, don de dar, dominio y mostrar misericordia.

Si no me equivoco, hay un total de 19 dones dados a la iglesia. ¡Qué riqueza de dones se han dado a la iglesia cuando Jesús subió a lo alto! Sería bueno que hiciéramos un estudio a fondo de cada uno de estos dones para poder reconocerlos en nuestras congregaciones. Una cosa que puede observarse es que nuestros amigos pentecostales han destacado unos pocos de estos dones, como los milagros, la sanidad y el hablar en lenguas, y los han puesto por encima del resto, convirtiéndolos en una validación de si una persona ha nacido de nuevo, si fue bautizada en el Espíritu Santo, o si es más espiritual que los que carecen de esos dones. O podemos considerar cómo los evangélicos tienden a hacer lo mismo con el don de evangelismo, que ha penetrado en muchas iglesias anabautistas conservadoras. Finalmente, podríamos examinar cómo algunas de nuestras iglesias sencillas toman solo los dones que tienen que ver con el gobierno de la Iglesia, dejando que solo los ordenados tengan dones, mientras que la mayoría de los demás dones quedan sin reconocer.

Todo esto me lleva a plantear la pregunta: “¿Deberíamos elevar uno o dos dones por encima del resto y enfatizarlos, o deberían reconocerse todos los dones por igual?” La única vez que veo que uno se eleva por encima del resto es en la carta de Pablo a los Corintios, en el último versículo del capítulo 12 y el primer versículo del capítulo 14, donde los exhorta a codiciar el mejor don que, con una lectura cuidadosa, notaremos que se refiere a la profecía. Al continuar con nuestra lectura cuidadosa, descubrimos que la profecía debería tener precedencia sobre el hablar en lenguas puesto que, aparentemente, la comprensión corintia del hablar en lenguas estaba siendo abusada y mal utilizada y la Iglesia podría no haber sido edificada por su comportamiento.

Dones espirituales no deben excusar conducta impía

Podría convenir aquí una palabra de precaución. Hay un énfasis por parte de algunos en “saber cuál es mi don espiritual”. Creo que esto puede ser bueno, pero no debe hacerse hasta el punto de excusar mi mala conducta porque “tengo este don y no el otro”. Por ejemplo, el profeta podría justificarse por ser duro porque su don es el de profeta; como puede que no tenga el don de misericordia, la gente podría resultar innecesariamente herida. Probablemente todos tengamos un don o dones principales. Por mucho que intentemos estar bien equipados con la mayor cantidad posible de dones, algunos seguirán siendo más dominantes que otros.

He preguntado a numerosas personas cuál era el don principal en la vida de nuestro Señor Jesús y la respuesta corta es que Él estaba lleno del Espíritu Santo y sin medida y los tenía todos. Es cierto, pero aun así, puesto que todos queremos ser como Jesús, quizá deberíamos dejar de excusarnos con un don limitado y perseguir llegar a estar lo más equipados posible. Yo sé, y usted sabe, que en esta carne no los dominaremos todos y, sin embargo, deberíamos ser receptivos a todos. Dicho esto, debemos darnos cuenta de que estamos destinados a ser interdependientes; por eso Jesús repartió estos dones separadamente a cada hombre y todos tendremos nuestro don o dones primarios. Pero todos éstos los hace un solo y mismo Espíritu, repartiendo a cada uno en particular como él quiere –1 Corintios 12:11. No obstante, tengamos cuidado de no excusar la conducta errada, o, por otro lado, la negligencia de hacer el bien, porque “bueno, ese simplemente no es mi don”.

Los dones espirituales no son la identidad del cristiano

También pueden aplicarse un par de precauciones al buscar entender los dones espirituales. Nuestra identidad no debe ser el don que tenemos, sino que nuestra identidad es en Cristo. Somos hijos del Rey; no somos primordialmente profetas, maestros o evangelistas. Sin embargo, al ser hijos del Rey, se nos ha dado un don por Él, para hacer Su obra, con Su poder. Reconocer ante todo quiénes somos en Cristo nos mantendrá en un hermoso lugar de humildad, pero si nuestra identidad primaria es “este don que tengo”, supongo que sería difícil no caer en el orgullo y, por tanto, nos exponemos a muchas trampas y peligros.

Los dones espirituales son dados por Dios, no para que los busque el hombre

¿Podría haber una advertencia respecto a cómo buscamos este don? ¿Qué significa cuando la Escritura dice que Dios da dones conforme a su elección? Por ejemplo, Dios, que también da testimonio juntamente con señales y prodigios, y con diversos milagros y repartimientos del Espíritu Santo, según su voluntad –Hebreos 2:4. O, Pero todas estas cosas las obra un mismo y único Espíritu, repartiendo a cada uno en particular como él quiere –1 Corintios 12:11.

¿Notan en ambos versículos la VOLUNTAD de Dios muy involucrada en el dar de dones en la Iglesia? Tal vez nuestro “buscar dones espirituales” deba hacerse a solas en nuestro aposento, pidiéndole a Dios que me haga humilde y que me capacite con el don que Él quiera que tenga para hacerme una herramienta útil en el cuerpo de la iglesia de la cual soy parte—“No mi voluntad, sino la tuya”. Quizá Él me ha dado un don que no estoy reconociendo ni usando, y lo que realmente necesito es avivar ese don y no descuidarlo, sino emplearlo en el lugar que ocupo en la iglesia. ¿Podría ser posible que, si buscara con excesiva insistencia otro don espiritual, podría conseguirme una falsificación?

También conviene mencionar de forma muy directa que cuando hay una búsqueda concentrada de dones espirituales usualmente aparece algún problema negativo. A veces se elevan unos pocos seleccionados y se les enseña que son más espiritualmente importantes, como hablar en lenguas, milagros y sanidades. Algunos promueven que hay poco o ningún valor en la enseñanza de los dones espirituales y que los únicos que son para nuestro tiempo son los referentes a los líderes ordenados de la iglesia, tales como el gobierno, pastores y maestros. Mientras tanto, algunas personas usan su entendimiento de los dones espirituales para volverse individualistas y ven poco valor en ser parte de un cuerpo. Esto es incorrecto, ya que una lectura cuidadosa de estas Escrituras nos muestra que TODOS los dones son esenciales para que Dios pueda hacer uso de todos ellos mediante la colaboración de todo el pueblo. ¿Podría ser posible que donde ciertos dones se elevan por encima del resto, ya sea el hablar en lenguas, las sanidades y los milagros; o si es el evangelismo; o si son los más apropiados para los ordenados entre nosotros, haya un elemento no reconocido de orgullo en medio nuestro? Somos tan proclives a la desilusión que sería bueno examinar bien nuestros corazones cuando buscamos dones espirituales.

Los dones espirituales no están incluidos en la lista bíblica de cualificaciones para los líderes de la iglesia

Pablo dijo a Timoteo: No descuides el don que hay en ti, que te fue dado por profecía con la imposición de las manos del presbiterio –1 Timoteo 4:14. Quizá, en lugar de buscar un don, necesitemos dejar de descuidar el don que se nos ha dado. En vez de buscar algo nuevo y emocionante, deberíamos avivar el don que ya tenemos. Ha ocurrido que hombres en el liderazgo han sido removidos de su puesto porque no tienen el don para aquello para lo que fueron ordenados. Sería muy lento y muy orante el proceder antes de apartar a un hermano ordenado de su cargo por esa razón. ¿No sería mejor orar para que Dios aumentara ese don que se le dio por la imposición de manos? Llegar rápidamente a la conclusión de que no tiene el don tal vez sea simplemente la salida fácil.

No haríamos eso en un matrimonio. ¿Cuántas veces ha sucedido que una esposa fue más dotada en liderazgo que su esposo? Anular el matrimonio no es una opción, ni es opción añadir una tercera persona a la unión matrimonial para equilibrar la percepción de falta de equilibrio en los dones. A menudo hemos visto que cuando la oración y el Espíritu Santo estuvieron involucrados en una situación así, Dios dio al esposo lo que le faltaba (1 Corintios 12:24-25), y la esposa aprendió a ceder su don de una manera que permitió que su marido fuera la cabeza piadosa del hogar.

Dios también puede dar el don necesario a los que en tal matrimonio y en tal equipo ministerial se encuentran con carencia. Porque nuestras partes hermosas no tienen necesidad; pero Dios juntó el cuerpo, habiendo dado más abundante honor a la parte que carecía; para que no haya desmembramiento en el cuerpo, sino que los miembros tengan el mismo cuidado los unos por los otros –1 Corintios 12:24-25. ¿Hay alguna vez ocasión de apartar a alguien de un oficio por falta de don? Quizá sí, pero seamos muy cautelosos, lentos, cuidadosos y orantes.

En el caso de una dificultad eclesial que parezca deberse a la falta de dones entre los ordenados, debemos considerar los siguientes versículos. ¿Quién es el sabio y entendido entre vosotros? Que lo manifieste por su buena conducta con hechos hechos en sabia mansedumbre. Pero si tenéis envidia amarga y contención en vuestros corazones, no os jactéis ni mintáis contra la verdad. Esta sabiduría no desciende de lo alto, sino que es terrenal, sensual, diabólica. Porque donde hay envidia y contención, hay perturbación y toda obra perversa. Mas la sabiduría que es de lo alto es primeramente pura, luego pacífica, amable, benigna, llena de misericordia y de buenos frutos, sin incertidumbre ni hipocresía. Y el fruto de justicia se siembra en paz por los que hacen la paz. –Santiago 3:13-18. Muy raro es el caso de problemas en la iglesia relacionados con el liderazgo cuando no existe una falta importante por parte de uno o más de los ordenados de vivir plenamente conforme a la voluntad y sabiduría de Dios tal como se define aquí.

La respuesta bíblica para resolver problemas eclesiales que involucren a líderes de la iglesia es triple. (1a) Los líderes en cuestión deben humillar sus corazones en arrepentimiento delante de Dios y de Su Palabra, delante del resto de los ordenados y, cuando sea necesario, delante de la iglesia local. (1b) Si la situación se ha deteriorado demasiado, entonces debe buscarse la sabiduría de supervisores externos. (2) Los líderes que puedan carecer de un don específico deben buscar a Dios mediante ferviente oración, tanto personal como de la iglesia local, y deben buscar la provisión de Dios para la capacidad habilitadora mediante …la imposición de manos del presbiterio –1 Timoteo 4:14. (3) Entonces, DESPUÉS de que se restaure la estabilidad, la hermandad local estará en un buen lugar para buscar juntos la voluntad de Dios acerca de ordenar a otro hermano para que ayude.

El propósito de Dios para los dones espirituales

Veo dos razones principales por las cuales se dan los dones del Espíritu a la Iglesia.

La primera razón es para el beneficio de la iglesia. En Efesios leemos: y él dio… [varios dones espirituales a los creyentes] [a unos este don y a otros otro don]… Para perfecting of the saints, para la obra del ministerio, para la edificación del cuerpo de Cristo: –Efesios 4:11-12. (Note: The bracketed English phrase in the source has been preserved in meaning: “la perfección de los santos”, but original verse reference and phrasing are maintained.) El capítulo 12 de 1 Corintios tiene un largo diálogo sobre cómo deben utilizarse los dones para beneficiar al cuerpo de Cristo (la iglesia local) y en el versículo 25 en particular, para que no haya desmembramiento en el cuerpo, sino que los miembros tengan el mismo cuidado los unos por los otros.

Hay quienes van predicando la necesidad de tener dones espirituales, animando a buscar dones específicos como el evangelismo, la sanidad, los milagros y las lenguas, y puede verse en muchos casos que esta enseñanza focalizada causa divisiones más que unidad. La Biblia dice que los dones fueron dados para unir a la Iglesia y si no lo están haciendo, deberíamos considerar si es lo genuino o si es una falsificación. Me doy cuenta de que las divisiones ocurren por muchas razones, pero si los dones en el cuerpo no están uniendo sino dividiendo, será mejor que busquemos a Dios por respuestas sobre por qué, porque los dones estaban destinados a traer unidad, unidad y edificación.

La segunda razón es para el beneficio del no creyente. Algunos de los dones fueron dados como señal para el no creyente. Por tanto, las lenguas son por señal, no a los que creen, sino a los que no creen; pero la profecía no es por señal a los que no creen, sino a los que creen –1 Corintios 14:22. Vemos que a lo largo del Nuevo Testamento las lenguas, los milagros y las sanidades seguían al evangelio en lugares donde éste se estaba presentando a quienes nunca lo habían oído antes. Esta era una manera en que Dios usaba para solidificar y validar en los corazones y mentes del no creyente que este evangelio debía ser de Dios por las manifestaciones sobrenaturales. Vemos que las lenguas también siguieron la difusión del evangelio para que todos pudieran oírlo en su propia lengua, como en el día de Pentecostés.

Consideraría estas dos las razones principales y los propósitos primarios de los dones. Haríamos bien en evaluar nuestros dones a la luz de estas dos razones principales para asegurarnos de que tenemos lo genuino y los usamos conforme a los propósitos para los cuales fueron dados.

Es interesante que de los 19 dones que estamos considerando, la mayoría de ellos se utilizan mejor en la Iglesia local. Recuerde, Dios usa la iglesia para alcanzar al mundo. Algunos de los dones dados a la iglesia son para alcanzar al mundo; por ejemplo, el evangelista tiene un llamado más singular para alcanzar al mundo. Dones como las sanidades, los milagros y el hablar en lenguas son algunos de los dones que son más prevalentes en la frontera del evangelio. Esto no significa que estos dones nunca se vean en la iglesia local. Mi oración es que si alguien entrara en nuestros servicios que no entiende ni una palabra de inglés, y no hay nadie que pueda interpretar la predicación de la Palabra a su idioma, que Dios nos conceda los dones de lenguas para que puedan oír el evangelio y ser edificados.

Hemos visto donde hubo enfermedad, y se llamaron a los ancianos de la iglesia y hubo unción y oración. A veces Dios eligió sanar milagrosamente. Sin embargo, solo porque nosotros (creyentes) tengamos este maravilloso don de sanidad no significa necesariamente que Dios quiera que todos seamos sanados de toda enfermedad. El apóstol Pablo oró tres veces por ser librado de su aflicción corporal (2 Corintios 12:7-12), y aun así Dios le dijo que no. Si él no fue sanado cuando había sanado a muchos otros, ¿por qué pensaría que para mí debería ser distinto? Así es con todos los dones que se dan a la iglesia; son permitidos por Dios para ejercerse conforme a Su voluntad, no a la nuestra. Es absolutamente esencial para usted y para mí ser parte de un cuerpo local para que tengamos los dones del Espíritu obrando en conjunto a través de todos los miembros, para la obra de la iglesia, trayendo unidad, unidad y edificación, y para la obra continua de la Iglesia en llamar a los hombres desde un mundo de pecado y traerlos a Su reino.

El don de las lenguas

Es importante considerar por un momento el don espiritual de las lenguas y, específicamente, el lugar que ocupa en el Reino de Dios. El apóstol Pablo nos dice que se dan como señal. Por tanto, las lenguas son por señal, no a los que creen, sino a los que no creen; pero la profecía no es por señal a los que no creen, sino a los que creen –1 Corintios 14:22.

No es una señal para el creyente de que realmente tiene el Espíritu Santo, sino que es una señal para el no creyente de que el mensaje del evangelio es verdadero. El ejemplo clásico fue en el día de Pentecostés. No determinamos la credibilidad de Pedro porque habló en otra lengua. Todos estaríamos de acuerdo sin duda alguna en que Pedro había nacido de nuevo, y que las muchas lenguas no eran para su aprobación sino para que los oyentes supieran que aquel hablar en muchas lenguas era sobrenatural. Hubiera sido necesario un alma obstinada para burlarse del mensaje predicado aquel día.

Recientemente, me enteré de estudios que se han hecho grabando la galimatía que compone la mayor parte de lo que hoy se llama lenguas. Curiosamente, hallaron que los hablantes de inglés usaban sílabas inglesas en repetición, y que los de habla hispana usaban sílabas españolas, por lo que dedujeron que la mayor parte de lo que hoy se llama lenguas es una falsificación en la que la persona, en su propio idioma, repite sílabas de su lengua nativa en repetición. Creo que en muchos casos se hace de manera inocente debido a la gran cantidad de engaño que acompaña al hablar en lenguas.

Lo que entiendo como lo genuino es el ejemplo de una señora en Canadá, que solo conocía el francés y no entendía nada de inglés. Esta mujer asistió a un servicio de avivamiento donde el evangelista predicaba en inglés sin intérprete en francés. Ella respondió en arrepentimiento al mensaje y quienes la aconsejaron le preguntaron cómo había entendido el mensaje, que estaba en inglés. Ella respondió que lo que había oído se le presentó en el francés más hermoso que jamás había escuchado. Claramente tuvo lugar un milagro para que oyera el mensaje de salvación y pudiera responder a él. Seguro fue reconfortante saber cuán sobrenatural fue que pudiera oírlo. Sospecho que es posible que, en ocasiones, quien habla en lenguas ni siquiera sea consciente de ello. Seguramente, si Dios pudo confundir las lenguas de los que edificaban la torre de Babel, también puede hacer que las palabras de un predicador angloparlante se conviertan en palabras en francés antes de entrar en los oídos de un oyente francófono.

La razón que hallamos en las Escrituras para el don de hablar en lenguas es doble, y es para el no creyente que viene entre nosotros. La primera razón es que oiga el mensaje del evangelio en su propia lengua. La segunda razón es que cuando lo oye milagrosamente en su lengua propia y quien habla no conoce su idioma, es una señal para el no creyente que le haga reconocer que el mensaje que oye es de Dios y por Dios.

En conclusión, hallamos que dos de los principales propósitos por los que Dios da dones a la iglesia, dándolos separadamente según su voluntad, son para la unidad y edificación del cuerpo de Cristo, y para que el no creyente oiga y sea persuadido del mensaje del evangelio. Consideremos seriamente si los dones espirituales que tenemos y los dones que son evidentes en nuestras iglesias están cumpliendo el propósito para el cual fueron dados.
